events.title: The Crossing
events.body: Humans come ashore on Dia-thìr, bringing their Church with them, and are given leave to stay. They are the first strangers met since the Sundering.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Three of Harrow's men buried above the tide-line

events.title: The ships met off the north-west
events.body: That winter the mist that had lain on the eastern sea since the fleet of the Sundering sailed into it lifts from the northern water. Two fishing boats of Achadh àrsaidh, working the water off the north-west cape where the Sea-Watcher is seen, meet three ships coming down out of the thin grey from the north, and hail them; neither side understands the other. The fishers turn south and the ships follow them down the coast toward Cuan shean. The fishers call the place Coinneachadh nan Long, the meeting of the ships, and the boats of Achadh àrsaidh still slow there.

events.title: The word brought home to Achadh àrsaidh
events.body: The second of the two Achadh àrsaidh boats that met the strangers' ships off the north-west cape turns home and brings the word to its households, while Lachlann Odhar's boat leads the strangers' ships south toward Cuan shean. Achadh àrsaidh is the first place on the island to hear of the strangers, and it hears of them from its own fishers.

events.title: Lachlann Odhar leads the ships down the coast
events.body: Lachlann Odhar steers south from the north-west cape the length of a winter day, past the empty headlands of the north-west, with the strangers' ships shortening sail to keep behind him. He runs his boat up the shingle at Cuan shean after dark and wakes the custodians.

events.title: The ships stand off Cuan shean in the westerly weather
events.body: A run of westerly gales keeps Na Trì Longan standing off and on beyond the bar of Cuan shean for many days. The town watches them from the dunes, and the custodian Oighrig nic Leòid forbids any boat to put off to them or any fire to be lit on the strand.

events.title: Three ships off Cuan shean
events.body: Three ships down from the north anchor off Cuan shean, the first hulls of their size seen from Dia-thìr since the fleet of the Sundering. Their master, a captain the rolls name Edmund Harrow, comes ashore unarmed with eleven men and asks by signs for water.

events.title: The rider from Cuan shean reaches Cathair dhearg
events.body: A rope-maker's son of Cuan shean rides the valley road to the capital in a day with Oighrig nic Leòid's letter on the ships. The clerk of the council reads it standing. The council's answer, two days later, bids Cuan shean feed the strangers, keep them apart and decide nothing.

events.title: Oighrig nic Leòid gives water on the shingle
events.body: Edmund Harrow wades ashore at Cuan shean with an empty cask, and the custodian Oighrig nic Leòid gives him and his eleven men water from the town well under the old law of the shore. She has seven casks filled and refuses anything more on her own word.

events.title: Three of Harrow's men buried above the tide-line
events.body: Three of the strangers, sick from the long voyage, die on the strand below the dunes at Cuan shean. Their own people bury them above the tide-line with a reading from a book and kneeling on the sand, while the town's children watch from the dunes.

events.title: Harrow's men mend nets on the dunes
events.body: Recovered from their sickness, the strangers penned below the dunes at Cuan shean begin mending the fishers' nets spread on the strand, unasked. The fishers learn from them a flat knot that does not slip, and call it the strangers' knot.

told_in.section: IV. Of the Forty Days below the Dunes

events.title: Buttons traded for fish on the strand
events.body: The first trade between the island and the strangers begins on the strand at Cuan shean, yellow-metal coat buttons for fish. The custodians forbid it twice and it goes on behind the dunes; at last Oighrig nic Leòid lets it be, and the fishwives wear the buttons on cords.

events.title: Forty days on the dunes
events.body: The custodians of Cuan shean will not decide alone, and send inland to the capital for counsel. For forty days the strangers are fed on the beach and kept below the dunes.

events.title: Manannan's priests keep the tide-prayer through the forty days
events.body: Through the forty days the strangers are fed below the dunes, the priests of Manannan at Seann Skell say their prayer to keep the sea shut at every tide without missing one. The harbour scribe enters their number each week, nine, with the weather and the thinness of Ceò Mhanannain.

events.title: The custodian of Baile fhiadhaich rides south
events.body: Word of the ships reaches Baile fhiadhaich, up the western coast, in two days. Its custodian rides south to see them, and writes to the council that the strangers' ropes are better than ours and their manners worse.

events.title: Oighrig nic Leòid's letter to the council from her sickbed
events.body: From her bed at Cuan shean Oighrig nic Leòid writes to the council that she gave the strangers water under the law of the shore and nothing more on her own word, and that a leave given in the roll cannot be ungiven. She asks that it be read before the vote. The clerk notes it received.

events.title: The strangers sheltered in the net-lofts
events.body: With the autumn gales the custodians of Cuan shean let the strangers off the open strand into the net-lofts along the harbour. The ships lie in the harbour with their yards sent down and a few hands aboard. The roll enters the lofts as a shelter for the winter and no leave.

events.title: Oighrig nic Leòid falls ill
events.body: At Samhain the custodian of Cuan shean takes a cough that goes into her chest, and by an Dùbhlachd she cannot leave her bed. Custodians riding up to the council at Cathair dhearg stop at her bedside on the way.

events.title: The Council of Custodians grants leave
events.body: The Council of Custodians at Cathair dhearg, which has sat in the crown's place since the crown fell empty at the close of the Age of Sundering, confirms the strangers' leave to stay under the high custodian Tormod mac Ailein. The council roll gives the vote as with one voice; a later hand in the margin notes that three custodians were absent.

events.title: The leave read on the strand at Cuan shean
events.body: A custodian of Cuan shean reads the council's leave to the strangers from an upturned boat on the strand, with a stranger who has learned some words in the net-lofts putting it into his own tongue. The strangers cheer three times and begin to send their ships' yards back up.

events.title: The quarter of sea they came from
events.body: Old sailors at Cuan shean say that the strangers came in from the same quarter of sea the fleet of the Sundering sailed into. The council forbids the saying in its hall. It is written down all the same, and never answered.

events.title: The struck line in the council roll
events.body: Bidden to strike from the council's roll the old sailors' saying about the quarter of the sea, the clerk at Cathair dhearg strikes it and writes beneath the striking what he was told to strike, so that the next clerk should know. The saying stands in the roll so, struck and unanswered.

told_in.section: VI. Of the Quarter of the Sea

events.title: Lachlann Odhar's words at the harbour wall
events.body: Going home at last to Achadh àrsaidh in an Gearran, Lachlann Odhar stands on the harbour wall at Cuan shean and says aloud that the ships came out of the quarter Cabhlach an Scaraidh sailed into. Nobody on the harbour answers him, and he puts out for the north.

events.title: The land beyond
events.body: The strangers name their homeland in their own tongue, but no scribe of the Dia-thìrich writes the word down. From the first season the scribes call it an Tìr Thall, the land beyond, and its people simply the humans.

links.label: At the same time
links.title: Crìosd and an Eaglais written in the council roll

events.title: The humans pray in a sail-loft at Cuan shean
events.body: On the day the strangers keep for their god a sailmaker of Cuan shean lends them his loft against the rain. They kneel on the sailcloth, the captain with the rest, while a priest reads from a book; they light no fire and burn nothing. Two priests of Manannan watch from the stair and go down to the water to say their own prayer. It is the first entry of the humans at prayer under a roof.

events.title: Wren and the priests come up to Cathair dhearg
events.body: Two priests of the humans and a boy ride up from Cuan shean on ponies of the town, a long day's road, and come over the bridge at dusk soaked through. The council lodges them in a house below the temple and gives them a long room on the east side of the hall. The younger priest, Samuel Wren, coughs in the damp of the lake country.

events.title: Crìosd and an Eaglais written in the council roll
events.body: In the same season as an Tìr Thall the clerk of Comhairle a' Chùraim enters the name of the strangers' one god as the island hears it, Crìosd, and calls their faith an Eaglais, after the word their priests use of the whole company of their believers. They are the first words of the humans' tongue that the island takes and keeps.

events.title: The keeping of the word-list given to Gormshuil nic Fhearchair
events.body: The humans' priests ask Cuan shean for someone to trade words with them at a table, and Cuan shean sends to the capital. Tormod mac Ailein calls Gormshuil nic Fhearchair, who sits on the council for Clann Fhearchair and writes the best hand in the hall, and the council gives her the keeping of the island's side of the list. Her niece Muireall is to make the fair copy.

events.title: The first attempts at speech
events.body: For a whole season clerics of the humans' Church and custodians of Dia-thìr labour to make a store of words in common. Neither side's account of what was agreed survives whole.

events.title: Wren sets his months against the moons
events.body: Wren draws the twelve months of the humans' sun-year as a wheel, and Gormshuil nic Fhearchair gives him the island's moons from Samhnas round to the stags' moon. He writes each moon's name beside the month it most nearly matches. For Eadrach, the between-moon, he finds no place, and writes it outside the wheel with the humans' mark of a question.

events.title: Wren names the fuel of his own country
events.body: Over a brazier of peat in the long room Wren shows by signs that his people burn peat too, and also a black stone dug from under the ground, which they burn in every house. Gormshuil nic Fhearchair writes his word for it and, in the Dia-thìris column, the black stone the humans dig in their own country and burn on their hearths.

events.title: Wren's word-lists
events.body: The human cleric Samuel Wren and the custodian Gormshuil nic Fhearchair keep word-lists side by side through the season of speech-making. Wren's list survives in the Administration's letter-books. Gormshuil's is lost; only its first leaf, with forty words for the colours of broken coal, is known from a copy.

events.title: Muireall copies the first leaf
events.body: In the gap-moon Gormshuil nic Fhearchair gives her loose sheets to her niece Muireall to copy fair into a book for Clann Fhearchair, and orders the colours set first, before cup and bread, alone on the first leaf with room left at the foot. Muireall copies the forty words in her young, careful hand and stops at the right-hand column, where the humans' side has one word to give.

events.title: The basket of broken coal on the table
events.body: In the wolf-moon Gormshuil nic Fhearchair takes a double handful from the capital's measure for the shrines and tips it on the table before Samuel Wren in the winter sun. She names forty colours at the breaks. Wren writes some of them, then stops, turns a piece in the light and gives one word for the whole heap. She waits for him to ask for hers; he holds up a candle.

events.title: One word for the coal
events.body: The humans have a single word for the coloured coal, and it is their word for the black fuel they burn at home. Gormshuil's copyist notes that no Dia-thìris word in either list answers to it, and that the humans did not ask for one.

events.title: Gormshuil nic Fhearchair begins the humans' letters
events.body: Since Wren cannot learn her colours, Gormshuil nic Fhearchair asks him by signs to teach her his letters. He writes them across a sheet of his white paper, large and small, and her name beneath as he hears it, and she copies it stroke by stroke. By the end of the spring she can spell out a line of his word-list, and finds his one word under her colours.

events.title: Trade begins
events.body: At first the trade is fair on both sides: the goods of Dia-thìr for tools and knowledge the lonely island lacks. For a few years it seems it may last.

links.title: The first bargains entered in the council roll

events.title: The first bargains entered in the council roll
events.body: At the moon of the bright fire the strangers' iron, glass, lamp-oil and paper come up to the capital's market, and wool, hides, salt fish and dyed cloth go down to Cuan shean. Comhairle a' Chùraim enters the first bargains in its roll, fleece for knife and cloth for glass, with both prices in the island's reckoning. The measure is good on both sides.

events.title: The copy of the list sent to the loft at Muileann chaol
events.body: Having watched the humans burn their spoiled paper, Gormshuil nic Fhearchair has Muireall make a second fair copy of the whole list, the colours first and the note at the foot of the first leaf. She seals it in an oak chest with the seal of Clann Fhearchair and sends it east with the carriers to the loft of Beathag nic Thòmais, where nothing is burned.

events.title: The trading post at Ros dhomhain
events.body: The humans set up a trading post at Ros dhomhain, the capital's harbour, and give iron tools, window glass, lamp-oil and paper for wool, salt fish, hides and dyed cloth. The first tally-book of the post, kept by the trader Thomas Pike, balances evenly through its first year.

events.title: The custodians' clerk keeps a slate beside Pike's book
events.body: The custodians of the capital shore set a clerk on a stool by the door of the humans' post at Ros dhomhain. He keeps his own tally of the day's goods on a slate in the old strokes, and each evening he and Thomas Pike read their two counts aloud and find them level.

told_in.section: I. Of the Counter

events.title: Goods carted from Cuan shean to the post
events.body: In the first weeks of the post every bale and cask goes between the strangers' ships at Cuan shean and the counter at Ros dhomhain by cart over the moor road, two days each way. The carters of Cuan shean charge by the creel, and Harrow goes to the pilots of Caol leathan for a way by water.

events.title: The pilots' double toll entered as fair
events.body: The pilots of Caol leathan go over the smallest of Harrow's hulls and name twice the toll of a Dia-thìreach boat for bringing her up the Abhainn gheal. Harrow is angry. Pike enters the price in the post's tally-book and writes beside it that it is fair, since the pilots know the shallows.

events.title: The first hull on Loch chrom
events.body: Pilots of Caol leathan bring the first of the strangers' ships up the Abhainn gheal into Loch chrom, towing her with boats through the shallows below Baile ghlas, and she anchors off Ros dhomhain. Thereafter the humans' goods come to the capital shore by water, and the pilots charge a stranger's hull twice the toll of a Dia-thìreach boat.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Goods carted from Cuan shean to the post

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The pilots' double toll entered as fair

events.title: Cathair naomh sends its wool
events.body: Cathair naomh, the city above Seann Toll on the northern coast, sends its first wool south to the humans' post by coasting boat. Its custodians take their payment in paper and ink, and with them begin the town's roll afresh.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The gift of paper to Cathair naomh

events.title: The gift of paper to Cathair naomh
events.body: Paying the custodians of Cathair naomh for their wool in paper and ink, Pike adds a quire of his own writing-paper uncounted. It is the one line of the post's first tally-book that he does not balance, and he marks it as a gift.

links.title: Cathair naomh sends its wool

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The pilots' double toll entered as fair

links.title: Harrow sails north-about with three hulls

told_in.book: Of the Post at Ros dhomhain
told_in.section: II. Of the Hull in the Shallows

events.title: Harrow sails north-about with three hulls
events.body: At the end of an Lùnastal Edmund Harrow sails from Cuan shean for an Tìr Thall with all three hulls, north-about, carrying hides and dyed cloth. He leaves Thomas Pike at Ros dhomhain with four men, the loft, the tally-book and the goods not yet traded.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Harrow's second voyage

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The gift of paper to Cathair naomh

told_in.book: Of the Post at Ros dhomhain
told_in.section: II. Of the Hull in the Shallows

events.title: Iron in the smithies
events.body: The smiths of Cathair dhearg take the humans' bar-iron gladly and learn to temper it in a winter. Within a few seasons the old bronze hoes are melted down for bells.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The ships' smith at the forge in Cathair dhearg

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Gilleasbuig Gobha's first tempered blade

links.label: Legacy of
links.title: The warehouse door hung

events.title: The ships' smith at the forge in Cathair dhearg
events.body: A smith off Harrow's ships, sent up by Pike, comes to the smiths' lane below Drochaid Cathair dhearg and works through the autumn at the forge of Gilleasbuig Gobha. Having no words in common, the two smiths agree on the colours of hot iron.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Iron in the smithies

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Gilleasbuig Gobha's first tempered blade

told_in.book: Of the Post at Ros dhomhain
told_in.section: III. Of the Bar-Iron

events.title: Gilleasbuig Gobha's first tempered blade
events.body: In the last days of an Dùbhlachd Gilleasbuig Gobha tempers his first blade alone at his forge in Cathair dhearg, a knife of the humans' bar-iron drawn to the straw next the brown. It cuts hide that the old bronze knives only bruise. He gives it to his wife Sìne.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Iron in the smithies

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The ships' smith at the forge in Cathair dhearg

told_in.book: Of the Post at Ros dhomhain
told_in.section: III. Of the Bar-Iron

events.title: Iron hoes on the capital's fields
events.body: Through am Faoilleach and am Màrt the smiths of Cathair dhearg forge iron hoes, and the farmers above the lake pay for them with their old bronze hoes, brought down in sacks. Some of the bronze hoes bear the marks of the fields they worked.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Iron in the smithies

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Gilleasbuig Gobha's first tempered blade

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The bells of Cathair dhearg cast from the hoes

told_in.book: Of the Post at Ros dhomhain
told_in.section: IV. Of the Hoes and the Bells

events.title: The bells of Cathair dhearg cast from the hoes
events.body: At the asking of the custodians, Gilleasbuig Gobha and two smiths of the lane melt down the bronze hoes in a mould-pit behind his forge and cast four bells. They hang in the market gate, at the bridge and at the temple of Cathair dhearg, and are first rung together at Lùnastal.

links.title: Iron in the smithies

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Iron hoes on the capital's fields

links.title: The trading house's letter read at the post

told_in.book: Of the Post at Ros dhomhain
told_in.section: IV. Of the Hoes and the Bells

events.title: Dyes for Baile Mòr mhòr
events.body: The weavers of Baile Mòr mhòr on the northern coast trade their cloth for the humans' dyes, a red and a blue brighter than any the island could make. Within a few years the old madder fields about the town go back to grass.

events.title: Harrow's second voyage
events.body: Harrow sails for home with hides and dyed cloth and comes back with four ships in place of three. He brings carpenters, a surgeon, and a letter from a trading house in an Tìr Thall asking what else the island has.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Harrow sails north-about with three hulls

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The trading house's letter read at the post

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Pike writes home of the island's coal

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Carpenters and a cooper come ashore at Baile dhìreach

events.title: The trading house's letter read at the post
events.body: Toward the end of an Dàmhair Thomas Pike reads at his counter the letter Harrow has brought from the trading house over the sea, aloud in both tongues. It asks what else the island has: timber, tin, copper, lead, and what the rocks hold. Gilleasbuig Gobha hears it read.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Harrow's second voyage

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The bells of Cathair dhearg cast from the hoes

told_in.book: Of the Post at Ros dhomhain
told_in.section: V. Of the Letter from over the Sea

events.title: The shipwrights of Inis mhòr
events.body: The shipwrights of Inis mhòr come to look at the humans' hulls and measure them with knotted cords. Their guild had built nothing greater than a coaster since the fleet of the Sundering, and the old craft of building for deep water was half forgotten.

events.title: The surgeon Jonas Tull
events.body: The humans' surgeon, Jonas Tull, sets the broken leg of a fisherman of Cuan shean who had been given up as lame. The town's custodian enters it in the roll as the first debt owed to a stranger.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Oighrig nic Leòid witnesses the setting of the leg

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Tull draws Ceann a' Chùraim's tooth

events.title: Oighrig nic Leòid witnesses the setting of the leg
events.body: Old and ill, Oighrig nic Leòid, custodian of Cuan shean, is carried to the fisherman's house to watch Jonas Tull break and set the crooked leg again. Told he has done it eleven times and nine have walked, she says that nine of eleven is more than the island has, and writes the debt in the roll.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The surgeon Jonas Tull

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The trading house's letter read at the post

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Pike's first two years balanced

told_in.book: Of the Post at Ros dhomhain
told_in.section: VI. Of the First Debt

events.title: Salt from Seann Warr
events.body: The salt-pans of Seann Warr begin to sell to Pike's post by the barrel. They are the first goods of Dia-thìr that the humans come back asking for twice.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Pike's first two years balanced

events.title: Pike's first two years balanced
events.body: In the first days of an Giblean Thomas Pike closes the tally-book of the post at Ros dhomhain on its second year. Over two nights he and the custodians' clerk go through every line of both years, book against slate, and the two counts stand level.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The trading post at Ros dhomhain

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Salt from Seann Warr

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Oighrig nic Leòid witnesses the setting of the leg

told_in.book: Of the Post at Ros dhomhain
told_in.section: VII. Of the Middling Coal

events.title: Wool at Caol leathan
events.body: The walled harbour of Caol leathan sends its first wool-ship to the humans' post. Its merchants will be paid only in iron by weight, and the tally-book of the post names them the hardest bargainers on the island.

events.title: Pike writes home of the island's coal
events.body: Answering the trading house, Thomas Pike writes of the island's timber, salt, wool, hides and smiths, and that it has copper, tin and some silver. Having held a piece from a custodian's hearth to the window, he writes that the island has coal of a middling sort, and much of it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Harrow's second voyage

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The trading post at Ros dhomhain

told_in.book: Of the Post at Ros dhomhain
told_in.section: VII. Of the Middling Coal

events.title: Gilleasbuig Gobha forges a hinge for Pike's chest
events.body: Gilleasbuig Gobha makes a new hinge of the strangers' bar-iron for the iron-bound chest under Pike's counter, where letters for over the sea are kept. He tempers it to the blue and will take nothing for the work. Pike's letter on the coal goes over the sea in that chest.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Iron in the smithies

told_in.book: Of the Post at Ros dhomhain
told_in.section: VII. Of the Middling Coal

events.title: Carpenters and a cooper come ashore at Baile dhìreach
events.body: A boat of the humans' post rows down from Cuan shean deep with sawn plank and grounds on the shingle north of the quay at Baile dhìreach. Seven men of Harrow's ships come ashore, the carpenter William Rook and the cooper Samuel Hale among them, seeking a sheltered beach for a slip where the small craft of the post may be mended and built.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Harrow's second voyage

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first mixed settlement

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The rule of the shingle read to the strangers

told_in.book: Of the Council of Six
told_in.section: II. Of the Rule of the Shingle

events.title: The rule of the shingle read to the strangers
events.body: The shingle above the wrack-line at Baile dhìreach is held in keeping for the whole town and may not be sold. Seonag nic Aoidh of the salt-house reads the town's rule to the strangers on the shore: the well drawn in turn, no fire on the shingle in the herring season, no hammer on the rest-nights. Rook says his men will keep it.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first mixed settlement

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Carpenters and a cooper come ashore at Baile dhìreach

told_in.book: Of the Council of Six
told_in.section: II. Of the Rule of the Shingle

events.title: The first mixed settlement
events.body: A small coastal town takes in both Dia-thìrich and humans under one rule. It is not tried again.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Carpenters and a cooper come ashore at Baile dhìreach

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The rule of the shingle read to the strangers

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first human house on the shingle

events.title: The compact written in both tongues
events.body: Through the moons of harvest six sit at the mending-table in the net-loft of Baile dhìreach, three of the town and three of the strangers, and write the town's rule twice. A clerk of Inis thais writes the Dia-thìris book and William Rook the humans'. The net-maker Eilidh nic Ruairidh and the cooper Samuel Hale are fetched to find the words for the moorings.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Baile dhìreach under one council

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The chair set to turn at the humans' new year

told_in.book: Of the Council of Six
told_in.section: VI. Of the Turning of the Humans' Year

events.title: The chair set to turn at the humans' new year
events.body: The six of Baile dhìreach find that the town's year turns at Samhain and is counted by moons, while the humans' year turns in the dead of winter on a fixed day. They write in both books that Iain mac Chaluim holds the chair until the humans' year turns, and William Rook for the year after, and so in turn.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Baile dhìreach under one council

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first council of Baile dhìreach

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The compact written in both tongues

told_in.book: Of the Council of Six
told_in.section: IV. Of the Compact Written Twice

events.title: Baile dhìreach under one council
events.body: The small port of Baile dhìreach on the south-west coast takes Dia-thìrich and humans under one council of six, three of each. Its founding compact is written twice, once in each tongue, the only such compact of the age.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The compact written in both tongues

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The chair set to turn at the humans' new year

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Two letters on the harbour of Baile dhìreach

links.title: Ruairidh refuses the cooper

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The council asked for a ruling on the marriage

links.label: Answered by
links.title: The terms asked for in two tongues

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The shingle clause read from both books

events.title: The first council of Baile dhìreach
events.body: The council is chaired in alternate years by the fisherman Iain mac Chaluim and the human carpenter William Rook. The harbour dues go half to the custodians at Cathair dhearg and half to the humans' post.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The chair set to turn at the humans' new year

links.title: The first dues shared

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Iain mac Chaluim hands the chair to William Rook

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Rook's ruling on the dragged mooring

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ruairidh relents

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The council asked for a ruling on the marriage

events.title: Samuel Hale tightens the herring barrels
events.body: The human cooper Samuel Hale takes down the leaking herring barrels of Baile dhìreach stave by stave and makes every one of them tight by the end of summer, beginning with the idle row of the salter Ruairidh. He takes a bowl from the pot for his pay, and asks for Dia-thìris words, which he writes under his own.

told_in.book: Of the Council of Six
told_in.section: III. Of Rope and Knot

events.title: The first boat off the humans' slip
events.body: On the first evening of Lùnastal the humans' slip at Baile dhìreach launches a small coaster of the strangers' pattern, deeper in the keel than the boats of the south-west. She is built for the fisherman Iain mac Chaluim, paid for in fish and labour and rigged with the town's rope; his wife pours sea water on her bow and asks Manannan to keep her.

told_in.book: Of the Council of Six
told_in.section: III. Of Rope and Knot

events.title: A stranger's prayer at the lamps of the drowned
events.body: At the dark of the year Baile dhìreach sets lamps along its quay for its drowned, as the harbours of the west do. The humans of the shingle stand in the line, and the cooper Samuel Hale says a prayer to Crìosd in his own tongue for shipmates lost in the northern sea on the voyage out. Eilidh nic Ruairidh sets a lamp for them.

told_in.book: Of the Council of Six
told_in.section: V. Of Her Father's No

events.title: The first human house on the shingle
events.body: The carpenters of Baile dhìreach lay a slip of split logs, raise an open shed, and build a house of sawn plank on a sill of beach stones, with a window of glass. Since nothing may be built on the shingle, the town rules that the house is a tent, and calls it so. The humans' book of the town enters it as the first house.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first mixed settlement

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Two letters on the harbour of Baile dhìreach

told_in.book: Of the Council of Six
told_in.section: III. Of Rope and Knot

events.title: Two letters on the harbour of Baile dhìreach
events.body: The humans' post at Ros dhomhain writes to ask why the dues of a harbour its own men have half rebuilt go wholly to the custodians at Cathair dhearg. The custodians of Inis thais write to ask by what rule strangers keep a yard on a shingle held in keeping. Iain mac Chaluim says the town must write its rule down.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Baile dhìreach under one council

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first human house on the shingle

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first dues shared

told_in.book: Of the Council of Six
told_in.section: IV. Of the Compact Written Twice

events.title: The first dues shared
events.body: At its first sitting the council of six of Baile dhìreach settles a quarrel over a mooring ring and sends the harbour dues out in two halves: one in a sack by a boy up the road to the custodians at Cathair dhearg, the other round by boat to the humans' post at Ros dhomhain.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first council of Baile dhìreach

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Two letters on the harbour of Baile dhìreach

told_in.book: Of the Council of Six
told_in.section: IV. Of the Compact Written Twice

events.title: Ruairidh refuses the cooper
events.body: On the night of Samhain, while the town keeps its fire on the headland above the quay and the humans watch from the last cairn, the cooper Samuel Hale comes to the door of the salter Ruairidh to ask for his daughter Eilidh nic Ruairidh. Ruairidh sends him away, saying that a council is one thing and a hearth another.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Baile dhìreach under one council

told_in.book: Of the Council of Six
told_in.section: V. Of Her Father's No

events.title: The bidding carried to Inis thais
events.body: In the black moon the council of Baile dhìreach sends its compact along the shore to the temple city of Inis thais in both tongues, with a clause bidding any town of the coast sit with it on the same terms. The pilot Murchadh mac Iain carries it by boat and brings back word that the custodian will write.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Inis thais declines the compact

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Iain mac Chaluim hands the chair to William Rook

told_in.book: Of the Council of Six
told_in.section: V. Of Her Father's No

events.title: Inis thais declines the compact
events.body: The city of Inis thais, whose harbour lies a few miles from Baile dhìreach, is bidden to join the joint council and declines. Its custodian writes that one town may be a trial, but two would be a rule.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The bidding carried to Inis thais

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Iain mac Chaluim hands the chair to William Rook

events.title: Iain mac Chaluim hands the chair to William Rook
events.body: On the morning the humans' year turns, in the net-loft of Baile dhìreach, the fisherman Iain mac Chaluim gives up the chair of the council of six and the carpenter William Rook takes it, as the compact bids. Both books enter it in a line, the one by the day and the year, the other by the moon. The letter from Inis thais is read the same morning.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first council of Baile dhìreach

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Inis thais declines the compact

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The bidding carried to Inis thais

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Rook's ruling on the dragged mooring

told_in.book: Of the Council of Six
told_in.section: VI. Of the Turning of the Humans' Year

events.title: Rook's ruling on the dragged mooring
events.body: A boat of the post drags her anchor at Baile dhìreach and fouls the salter Ruairidh's mooring, and her master will not pay. William Rook, in the chair, orders his own countryman to pay the town's rate for rope and ring, in iron by weight, that day, and asks Ruairidh whether the rate is fair.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first council of Baile dhìreach

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Iain mac Chaluim hands the chair to William Rook

told_in.book: Of the Council of Six
told_in.section: VI. Of the Turning of the Humans' Year

events.title: The storm of the wolf-moon at Baile dhìreach
events.body: A three-day storm off the west drives the sea over the quay of Baile dhìreach and up the shingle towards the boats. On the second night the town and the humans haul the boats over the crest together with ropes, blocks and a capstan-bar from the slip. The salt-house chimney and half the roof of the humans' house are lost.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ruairidh relents

told_in.book: Of the Council of Six
told_in.section: VI. Of the Turning of the Humans' Year

events.title: Ruairidh relents
events.body: After half a moon of the carpenter in the chair, in which nothing in Baile dhìreach has fallen but a chimney, the salter Ruairidh helps the humans roof their house again and sends word by his daughter Eilidh nic Ruairidh that the cooper Samuel Hale may come up to the house for his bowl himself.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first council of Baile dhìreach

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The storm of the wolf-moon at Baile dhìreach

told_in.book: Of the Council of Six
told_in.section: VI. Of the Turning of the Humans' Year

events.title: A supply ship lost on the western reefs
events.body: A human supply ship strikes the reefs off the western coast in fog, and nine of her crew drown. Her master was sailing by a chart drawn from memory, the humans' letter-books complain, on a coast lit only by the old driftwood fires.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The nine drowned buried on the western shore

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The chart from memory brought to the post

events.title: The nine drowned buried on the western shore
events.body: The nine drowned of the human supply-brig are buried in the dunes above the tide-line at Baile fhiadhaich, on ground the custodian gives. A townswoman wets each grave with sea-water as the coast does for its own drowned. The mason Torcall Clachair cuts nine headstones with a line for the sea, and the ship's mate scratches the names beneath.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A supply ship lost on the western reefs

told_in.book: Of the Five Headlands
told_in.section: I. Of the Nine on the Western Shore

events.title: The chart from memory brought to the post
events.body: The mate of the lost brig carries her drowned master's chart, drawn from memory, to the post at Ros dhomhain. It sets the point where she struck a mile too far out to sea and shows no reefs below it. The ships' masters at the post argue over it at Thomas Pike's counter.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A supply ship lost on the western reefs

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The beacons asked for

told_in.book: Of the Five Headlands
told_in.section: I. Of the Nine on the Western Shore

events.title: The beacons asked for
events.body: Human seamen, strange to the coasts of Dia-thìr, ask for standing beacons. The builders of the Dia-thìrich agree, not yet seeing what the beacons will bring.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The chart from memory brought to the post

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The masters of building answer the strangers

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Pike writes of the natives

events.title: The masters of building answer the strangers
events.body: Comhairle a' Chùraim passes the strangers' asking to the seven master builders of Cathair dhearg. They agree that towers may be raised on the headlands where each place's custodian gives leave, with a Dia-thìreach builder to choose the ground. Torcall Clachair alone asks about coal, and the old ruling that no coal feeds a sea-fire is kept.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The beacons asked for

links.label: Legacy
links.title: No coal on the beacons

told_in.book: Of the Five Headlands
told_in.section: II. Of the Asking

events.title: The beacon headlands walked
events.body: The human navigator James Fenn and the Dia-thìreach mason Torcall Clachair walk the coast together to choose the places of the new beacons, and mark the five headlands of the old fires. Fenn's chart survives; Torcall's cairns for the most part do not.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Torcall's first cairn on the Tobar dhearg headland

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The second cairn on the eastern cape

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The households of Àth dhearg asked hearth by hearth

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Three yards of ash at Muileann bheag

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Baile chrom's condition for the fifth cairn

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The island's names written on Fenn's chart

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Torcall's cairn set in the footing of the tower

events.title: Pike writes of the natives
events.body: Thomas Pike enters in the post's letter-book that the islanders have agreed to the lights without difficulty and without asking what they would cost. It is the first page of his letter-book to call the Dia-thìrich the natives. The custodians' roll sets down the same asking as a request that the old sea-fires be built higher and kept all night.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The beacons asked for

told_in.book: Of the Five Headlands
told_in.section: II. Of the Asking

events.title: No fire on Binnean a' Chlachair
events.body: James Fenn asks for a night fire on the summit of Binnean a' Chlachair, the highest ground of the island. Torcall Clachair and the herders of Muileann gheal refuse, keeping the custom of the hills. Torcall lays one stone on the herders' cairn, and Fenn takes his sights by day to a linen square, four days slower. The two winter at Muileann gheal.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Fenn's line

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Torcall's first cairn on the Tobar dhearg headland

told_in.book: Of the Five Headlands
told_in.section: VI. Of Fenn's Line

events.title: Torcall's first cairn on the Tobar dhearg headland
events.body: On the southern cape at Tobar dhearg, beside the old dry-stone fire-tower where the village households burn driftwood and seal fat in turn, Torcall Clachair builds a cairn to mark ground for a new tower. James Fenn writes a name from his own shore on the cape in his chart. Torcall answers that the cape has a name.

events.title: The second cairn on the eastern cape
events.body: At Baile ìseal, whose fire is lit to bring the boats home in a storm, Torcall Clachair and James Fenn sit up with the watch and see a raiders' light on the nearest islet. The watchman says a greater light would bring home more men of both kinds. He helps Torcall lift the capstone of the second cairn.

events.title: The households of Àth dhearg asked hearth by hearth
events.body: The custodian of Àth dhearg will not give away the fire-shelf above the rock-cut stair, saying it belongs to the households who cut it. Torcall Clachair and James Fenn go round the hearths for eleven days. Most say yes and two say no. The third cairn is raised at the end of the shelf, and the custodian climbs up with bread.

events.title: Three yards of ash at Muileann bheag
events.body: Seeking the depth for a tower's footing, James Fenn digs beside the old shore-fire on the northern point at Muileann bheag with Torcall Clachair and a boy of the village. They go down through bands of black ash and red earth and find no rock at three yards. Torcall sets the fourth cairn inland on sound rock.

events.title: Baile chrom's condition for the fifth cairn
events.body: The households of Baile chrom, whose headland fire has always warned boats off the water of Uilebheist na Mara, say the old fire cannot both warn and call. They give leave for a tower on condition that the old fire be kept alight beside it on driftwood. James Fenn agrees, and Torcall Clachair builds the fifth cairn.

events.title: The fire on the north-west headland raised for Fenn
events.body: At Lùnastal Torcall Clachair keeps a high fire of driftwood and seal fat on the headland at Baile chrom for three nights, burning no coal. On the third night James Fenn, rowed west by fishers of Achadh àrsaidh past Coinneachadh nan Long, sees it sink below the sea's rim at near thirty miles. The sea end of his line is fixed there.

told_in.section: VI. Of Fenn's Line

events.title: The cairns of the line laid across the island
events.body: Through the autumn James Fenn sights station after station east from the Baile chrom headland, and Torcall Clachair raises a narrow cairn capped with a white stone on each chosen top. Hired boys carry a chain of iron links between them. The string of cairns crosses the moors south of Cnoc bheag and the hills of the interior.

events.title: Fenn's line
events.body: On the same survey James Fenn runs a line of sights across the whole island, from the open sea off the north-west, where ships coming down from the north first raise the land, to the water off the eastern cape. He makes it a hundred and fifty-five miles, some thirty of them sea at the western end. It is the first measure of Dia-thìr from side to side, and every chart the Company draws afterwards is scaled to it.

events.title: The council asked for a ruling on the marriage
events.body: Iain mac Chaluim writes for the council of Baile dhìreach to the custodians at Cathair dhearg, asking whether the marriage of a Dia-thìreach net-maker to a human cooper may be entered in the custodians' roll, and whether its children stand as a Dia-thìreach mother's. The rider returns with no answer. The council resolves to enter the marriage itself.

events.title: A marriage in two tongues
events.body: At Baile dhìreach the net-maker Eilidh nic Ruairidh weds the human cooper Samuel Hale. The council enters the marriage in both its books; the custodians at Cathair dhearg, asked for a ruling, send none.

events.title: Torcall witnesses in the Dia-thìreach book
events.body: At the wedding on the quay of Baile dhìreach no custodian comes to witness. James Fenn signs for the bridegroom in the humans' book, and Iain mac Chaluim calls the mason Torcall Clachair from the crowd to sign the Dia-thìreach book. William Rook and Iain mac Chaluim close the two books side by side.

events.title: The island's names written on Fenn's chart
events.body: On the night of the wedding at Baile dhìreach James Fenn writes the Dia-thìris names of the five headlands under his own on his chart, as Torcall Clachair tells them: Tobar dhearg, Baile ìseal, Àth dhearg, Muileann bheag and Baile chrom. At the mountain in the middle of his line he writes Binnean a' Chlachair.

events.title: Harrow asks for the terms in writing
events.body: Edmund Harrow comes up the lake road to Cathair dhearg with Thomas Pike to speak for him and asks Tormod mac Ailein that the terms on which the humans stay be written and signed by both sides. He says that a man is coming from an Tìr Thall to speak for its government, and that he himself has asked for him. The council's leave, he says, stands only in the council's roll.

told_in.section: II. Of Tormod's Reasons

events.title: Tull draws Ceann a' Chùraim's tooth
events.body: Passing through Cathair dhearg on his way to the post at Ros dhomhain, the surgeon Jonas Tull draws a rotten tooth from the jaw of Tormod mac Ailein, which the capital's physician had left to wait a month. Tormod keeps the tooth in a box. It is the second debt owed to a stranger that the custodians know of, and it is owed by Ceann a' Chùraim.

events.title: Pell lands at Cuan shean
events.body: Josiah Pell comes ashore at Cuan shean from the first ship of the year down from the north, dry-shod on a plank, with a leather case he lets no one carry. He asks for a horse. Oighrig nic Leòid, who gave Harrow water, lends him her own and writes to the council the same day that he did not ask for water.

told_in.section: III. Of the Man Who Asked for a Horse

events.title: Pell rides to the council hall
events.body: Josiah Pell rides the twenty-six miles from Cuan shean to Cathair dhearg in a day and, passing by the humans' post, asks at dusk for the council hall and Ceann a' Chùraim. Tormod mac Ailein comes down to him in his house-shoes. With no one to carry words between them, Pell greets him with the island's word of leave-taking, learned on the ship.

events.title: The terms asked for in two tongues
events.body: In the talks at Cathair dhearg and Ros dhomhain, with Samuel Wren putting each sentence into the other tongue, Tormod mac Ailein asks that the terms be written twice, as the compact of Baile dhìreach was. Pell answers that one text must govern before the lawyers of an Tìr Thall, and that a copy in Dia-thìris will follow when there is leisure. Wren gives it as an dèidh làimh.

events.title: The first written treaty
events.body: The terms on which the humans stay are first set down in writing, in the humans' tongue only. No one among the Dia-thìrich speaks against it at the time.

events.title: The treaty signed at Cathair dhearg
events.body: The treaty is signed in the council hall at Cathair dhearg by Tormod mac Ailein for the custodians, and for the Administration by Josiah Pell, newly come as the humans' first Commissioner. Tormod could not read the tongue it was written in. Who read it to him is not told.

events.title: Gormshuil called back from Muileann chaol
events.body: Gormshuil nic Fhearchair, gone east with the season's copies for the loft of Beathag nic Thòmais at Muileann chaol, is sent for by rider when the talks with Pell run fast. She starts back the day the rider finds her, but the rain is on the hills and the fords are up, and she is still on the road when the terms are signed.

events.title: Gormshuil given a copy of the terms
events.body: Two days after the signing Gormshuil nic Fhearchair comes in from the hills, reads the entry in the roll standing, and asks Pell through Samuel Wren for the terms in the strangers' tongue, since the copy in Dia-thìris is to wait for leisure. Pell's secretary makes one within the week. She begins to read it a word at a time, and does not bring it before the council.

told_in.section: IV. Of the Line Read Twice

events.title: The masons of the capital build for Pell
events.body: The masons of the masons' lane at Cathair dhearg take up Pell's house on the rise, paid in bar-iron by the humans' day, which begins at midnight where the island's begins at dusk. They float grey stone over the lake on rafts and build the house square to Pell's drawn plan, facing the harbour, with its back to the capital. The council does not ask it turned.

links.title: The Residency above Ros dhomhain

told_in.book: Of Cùmhnant Cathair dhearg
told_in.section: V. Of the House on the Rise

events.title: The clerk leaves the day blank
events.body: Entering Cùmhnant Cathair dhearg in the council's roll, the custodians' clerk writes the year by the count of An Diosal and the moon of Bealltach. The strangers have dated their sheets by their own day and month, and no one in the hall can turn the one into the other, so he leaves the day empty. It is the first such page in the roll.

links.title: The treaty signed at Cathair dhearg

told_in.book: Of Cùmhnant Cathair dhearg
told_in.section: IV. Of the Line Read Twice

events.title: The rise above Ros dhomhain given
events.body: Pell asks the council for the bare rise behind the harbour of Ros dhomhain, where the town's goats graze, to build a house for Riaghaltas nan Coigreach. The goat-keepers are paid in iron pots and are glad of it, and the council gives the ground without a vote, holding it a matter of goats.

told_in.book: Of Cùmhnant Cathair dhearg
told_in.section: V. Of the House on the Rise

events.title: The Residency above Ros dhomhain
events.body: Josiah Pell builds a house of dressed stone on the rise above Ros dhomhain and calls it the Residency. Captain Harrow, needed ashore no longer, goes back to the sea trade.

events.title: Harrow takes his leave of Tormod
events.body: Edmund Harrow comes up to Cathair dhearg with Thomas Pike to say that Pell will govern now and a ship's master is needed ashore no longer. He tells Tormod mac Ailein that he and Pike are to have a licence to trade, and that the charter will be sent to the council and found in order. He sails north-about from Ros dhomhain two tides later.

events.title: The Company chartered
events.body: Harrow and Pike found a trading house under licence of the Administration, known on Dia-thìr simply as the Company. Its charter gives it first refusal of "all fuels, ores and minerals the island may yield."

events.title: The charter lodged with the council
events.body: A copy of Cairt na Companaidh comes to the council at Cathair dhearg in the strangers' tongue, four sheets under a red seal. The clerk enters its coming in the roll and lays it in the chest under the east window of the hall, beside the unanswered letter from Baile dhìreach, and there it lies a month unread.

events.title: Gormshuil reads the charter to Tormod
events.body: At midsummer Gormshuil nic Fhearchair takes the charter from the council's chest and reads it by night to Tormod mac Ailein at his hearth. In the clause of all fuels, ores and minerals the island may yield she finds Wren's one word for the coal, and she shows him that the charter's licence hangs from the line on goods he had asked to hear twice. He asks her to keep it between them.

events.title: The shore at Cathair dhomhain sold
events.body: Thomas Pike buys a strip of shingle and rough grass above the lake at Cathair dhomhain from a fishing family that has drawn its nets there since An Aois Naomh, for a keg of nails, two lamps and a sheet of window-glass. The custodian of the lake shore enters the sale. It is the first ground on Dia-thìr the strangers hold by sale and not by the council's leave.

told_in.section: VII. Of the Door at Cathair dhomhain

events.title: The warehouse at Cathair dhomhain
events.body: The Company builds a stone warehouse at Cathair dhomhain, along the lake shore from the capital, to keep its tools from the harbour thieves of Ros dhomhain. It is the first building on Dia-thìr the Company owns outright.

events.title: The warehouse door hung
events.body: The oak door of A' Chompanaidh's warehouse at Cathair dhomhain comes down the shore road from Cathair dhearg and is hung at dusk on strap hinges forged by Gilleasbuig Gobha in the smiths' lane below the bridge. Thomas Pike locks it with a long iron key. Tormod mac Ailein, who has walked out from the capital, watches it hung; the lake-shore roll calls it a good door.

events.title: The strangers' fever
events.body: A fever comes ashore at Cuan shean with a crowded ship and runs down the west coast. Ninety-one Dia-thìrich die, and eleven humans. The custodians shut the town to ships for a season, and Pell protests in writing.

events.title: The hill's coal carried to Cuan shean
events.body: Eleven carriers of the hills bring the measured coal for the western hearths down from the store at Taigh na Fèithe to Cuan shean, five days on the road with ponies and a custodian's clerk. Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill of Muileann chrom goes among them for the first time. Oighrig nic Leòid counts the baskets in by lamplight at the custodians' store.

links.title: The strangers' fever

told_in.section: I. Of the Carriers at Cuan shean

events.title: The carriers kept at Cuan shean
events.body: When the fever breaks out among the net-sheds, the clerk of the hill carriers and Oighrig nic Leòid forbid the eleven to take the road home, lest they carry the sickness into the hills. The carriers stay in the town through an t-Samhain, carrying water to the fever houses and the dead to their burying.

events.title: Oighrig answers Pell's protest
events.body: Pell's letter protesting the shutting of Cuan shean is read to Oighrig nic Leòid in the custodians' store by the humans' trader of the quay. It claims the harbour open under Cùmhnant Cathair dhearg and holds the town answerable for spoiled cargo. She asks whether it says anything of the dead, and sends back the number, forty-one, and word that the ships may wait.

events.title: The fever at Baile àrsaidh
events.body: The strangers' fever comes to Baile àrsaidh, a day's walk up the coast, and kills its custodian and both her sons. No humans dwell in the town at all, and the custodians of the west take note of it.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The hills keep their roads open

events.title: The fever turned back at Cnoc àrsaidh
events.body: At Cnoc àrsaidh in the south-west the townsfolk block the road with carts and turn back every traveller for a season, and the fever does not reach them. The Administration fines the town for hindering trade.

links.title: The hills keep their roads open

events.title: Prospectors in the central hills
events.body: The Company sends two prospectors, Abel Stone and Hugh Mercer, into the hills east of the capital. They come back with sacks of broken coal, and word that the black seam runs "further than can be walked in a day."

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The prospectors find no guide

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The seam walked with the prospectors

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The custodians write for the coal

events.title: The fever dead buried beyond the dunes
events.body: The custodians of Cuan shean will not lay the fever dead in the old ground by the harbour, and bury them in the sand beyond the dunes, out of sight of the town. The human dead lie in the same ground in a row of their own, read over by their priest. The burying slackens at the dark of the year and ends before Là Fhèill Brìde.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The strangers' fever

told_in.book: Of the Fever and the Sacks of Coal
told_in.section: II. Of the Dunes and the Road Home

events.title: The hills keep their roads open
events.body: After the fever at Baile àrsaidh, where no human lived, the custodians of the hills meet at Taigh na Fèithe and talk of shutting the hill roads. They decide against it, since the roads carry the meal, the salt and the lamp-oil. Their roll gives the reason in the words of Seonag Liath of the old cutting: nine years of salt eaten with the strangers.

links.title: The fever at Baile àrsaidh

told_in.section: III. Of the Word from the West

events.title: Cnoc àrsaidh pays its fine in wool
events.body: Cnoc àrsaidh, fined by Riaghaltas nan Coigreach for turning back travellers with its carts, pays the fine in sacks of wool. The hill carters carry the story east and tell it at the mill of Muileann chrom as a jest against the strangers, who have no use for so much wool.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The fever turned back at Cnoc àrsaidh

told_in.book: Of the Fever and the Sacks of Coal
told_in.section: III. Of the Word from the West

events.title: The prospectors find no guide
events.body: Abel Stone and Hugh Mercer come up the road to Muileann chrom with a letter of A' Chompanaidh asking lodging and a guide into the hills. The miller houses and feeds them, but no man of the hill will lead strangers onto it with a hammer. Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill offers himself for a silver coin of an Tìr Thall, against his father's wish.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Prospectors in the central hills

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The seam walked with the prospectors

told_in.book: Of the Fever and the Sacks of Coal
told_in.section: IV. Of the Two Prospectors

events.title: The seam walked with the prospectors
events.body: For eleven days Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill leads Stone and Mercer through the hills north and east of Muileann chrom, by the stream-cuts where the seam shows. They break coal at every gully, a sack to each, and Mercer counts the paces between. Raghnall names the colours of the broken coal; the prospectors have one word for all of it. He carries a sack down on his own back.

links.title: Prospectors in the central hills

links.title: The prospectors find no guide

told_in.section: IV. Of the Two Prospectors

events.title: The custodians write for the coal
events.body: The custodians of the vein send a letter in Dia-thìris to Thomas Pike at Ros dhomhain, asking that all the coal broken on the hill above Muileann chrom without leave be brought back to be laid in the rock with the proper words. They write twice more in the spring before any answer comes.

links.title: Prospectors in the central hills

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The sacks returned to the rock

told_in.book: Of the Fever and the Sacks of Coal
told_in.section: V. Of the Half Carried West

events.title: The sacks returned to the rock
events.body: The custodians of the vein demand the broken coal back, to lay it in the rock again with the proper words. The Company returns half. The custodians' roll enters the other half as "carried west."

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The custodians write for the coal

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Six sacks come back to Muileann chrom

links.title: The returned half laid in the rock

events.title: The first mining contracts
events.body: Trade sours into bargain. Dia-thìrich hands mine the vein on a scale that no reverent custom had ever used.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first contract read at the mill

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Raghnall chosen to lead the thirty
