links.title: The contract carried up to Doire mhòr

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Lisle's rider gathers the papers of the hill

events.title: The first pit at Muileann chrom
events.body: Under the first contract a Dia-thìreach crew of thirty opens a working at Muileann chrom, paid by the ton in iron tools and lamp-oil. The custodians' own cuttings had never been measured by weight at all.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Raghnall chosen to lead the thirty

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first ton weighed at Muileann chrom

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first crew paid in iron and oil

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first coal barge goes down from Ceann fhada

events.title: Six sacks come back to Muileann chrom
events.body: At the summer's end a human carter brings six of the thirteen sacks back up the road to the mill of Muileann chrom with a paper no one there can read. Asked for the rest, he points west, towards Ros dhomhain and the ships, and turns his cart round.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The sacks returned to the rock

told_in.book: Of the Fever and the Sacks of Coal
told_in.section: V. Of the Half Carried West

events.title: The first contract read at the mill
events.body: Abel Stone brings the first contract of A' Chompanaidh to Muileann chrom with two carts of steel-pointed picks, bar-iron and lamp-oil. It is read at the mill in both tongues. The interpreter from Ros dhomhain can find no Dia-thìris for the ton and calls it "a great load, weighed". Some of the older hewers walk out before the end.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first mining contracts

told_in.book: Of the Fever and the Sacks of Coal
told_in.section: VI. Of the Contract and the First Ton

events.title: Raghnall chosen to lead the thirty
events.body: Abel Stone names Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill, who walked the seam with him, to lead the first crew of the hill. The crew is thirty: young men of the hewers' and shepherds' households, two from the mill and three older hewers of the old cutting. Raghnall's father, a hewer of that cutting, will not join it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first mining contracts

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first pit at Muileann chrom

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The returned half laid in the rock

told_in.book: Of the Fever and the Sacks of Coal
told_in.section: VI. Of the Contract and the First Ton

events.title: The returned half laid in the rock
events.body: At the old cutting above Muileann chrom the custodians of Taigh na Fèithe and Seonag Liath sort the returned coal by colour and by gully, and the hewers lay it back into the clefts with clay while the custodians say the words for a thing taken out of season. Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill carries all six sacks up to the face. He gives the clerk the word "west" for the rest.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The sacks returned to the rock

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Raghnall chosen to lead the thirty

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first ton weighed at Muileann chrom

told_in.book: Of the Fever and the Sacks of Coal
told_in.section: V. Of the Half Carried West

events.title: The first ton weighed at Muileann chrom
events.body: On the day the first pit is opened below the old cutting, A' Chompanaidh sets up an iron beam on a timber tripod at the pit-mouth. At dusk the clerk adds his figures and Stone calls out one ton, the first coal of the hills ever weighed. The crew cheers, and the figure is written in the pit-book against Raghnall's name.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first pit at Muileann chrom

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The returned half laid in the rock

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first crew paid in iron and oil

told_in.book: Of the Fever and the Sacks of Coal
told_in.section: VI. Of the Contract and the First Ton

events.title: The first crew paid in iron and oil
events.body: On the first market-day after the opening of the pit, the crew of thirty at Muileann chrom are paid for their tons in picks and lamp-oil at the rate written on the contract, to the last measure of oil. The pit-book of A' Chompanaidh balances to the line.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first pit at Muileann chrom

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first ton weighed at Muileann chrom

told_in.book: Of the Fever and the Sacks of Coal
told_in.section: VII. Of What the Hill Had Never Been Weighed By

events.title: A coal quay at Ceann fhada
events.body: The Company builds a stone quay at Ceann fhada, a fishing hamlet below the hills, for loading coal into coasting barges. The fishermen are paid for their foreshore in iron nails, by weight.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The nails weighed again at Ceann fhada

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first coal barge goes down from Ceann fhada

events.title: The nails weighed again at Ceann fhada
events.body: The river-fishers and pilots of Ceann fhada, paid by weight in iron nails for the foreshore under the new coal quay, carry their nails to the fish-shed and weigh each man's share again on the old beam they weigh salmon on. Every share is true to the ounce. A pilot enters in the roll of Ceann fhada that the weight was true and the men ashamed.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A coal quay at Ceann fhada

told_in.book: Of the Door at Doire mhòr
told_in.section: II. Of Nails by Weight

events.title: The first coal barge goes down from Ceann fhada
events.body: Carts from the pit at Muileann chrom tip the first coal into a flat barge moored against the new quay at Ceann fhada. Two pilots of the hamlet, paid by A' Chompanaidh, take her down the Abhainn uaine at the sweeps, since no one else knows the river.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A coal quay at Ceann fhada

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first pit at Muileann chrom

told_in.book: Of the Door at Doire mhòr
told_in.section: II. Of Nails by Weight

events.title: Wren's grammar
events.body: Samuel Wren finishes a grammar of Dia-thìris for the Mission, the house of the humans' Church on Dia-thìr. It is careful and true in most things, and it gives the word for the vein's custodians as "keepers of the coal."

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Gormshuil nic Fhearchair reads Wren's grammar to the custodians

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A hawk-priest's note beside the three words

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The hawk-priests of Cnoc bheag show Wren their margins

events.title: Gormshuil nic Fhearchair reads Wren's grammar to the custodians
events.body: At the Samhain sitting of the council at Cathair dhearg, Gormshuil nic Fhearchair reads Samuel Wren's grammar aloud to the custodians of the hills and puts it into Dia-thìris. She tells them that in the humans' tongue a keeper is one who has a thing and holds it until paid. Beathag Dhubh of Doire mhòr enters in her roll that the strangers' book calls the custodians keepers.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Wren's grammar

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A hawk-priest's note beside the three words

told_in.book: Of the Door at Doire mhòr
told_in.section: III. Of Three Words in a Grammar

events.title: The hawk-priests read Wren
events.body: The hawk-priests of Cnoc bheag ask the Mission for a copy of Wren's grammar, to read what the humans write of them. The Mission sends one. Of all the copies that survive it bears the most notes in the margins.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A hawk-priest's note beside the three words

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The hawk-priests of Cnoc bheag show Wren their margins

events.title: A hawk-priest's note beside the three words
events.body: In the copy of Wren's grammar kept by the hawk-priests of Cnoc bheag, a priest writes in the margin beside the humans' name for the custodians, in Dia-thìris, that Wren writes as a man counts sacks, and signs it with a hawk's head.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The hawk-priests read Wren

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Wren's grammar

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Gormshuil nic Fhearchair reads Wren's grammar to the custodians

told_in.book: Of the Door at Doire mhòr
told_in.section: III. Of Three Words in a Grammar

events.title: The custodians of the hills called on the contracts
events.body: At the dark of the year the council at Cathair dhearg calls the custodians of the hills to say what their villages make of the contracts coming up from Muileann chrom. It hears four days of talk of iron, lamp-oil and the ton, and makes no ruling.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first mining contracts

told_in.book: Of the Door at Doire mhòr
told_in.section: IV. Of the Bell before the Fleet

events.title: The Mission chapel
events.body: The Mission raises a timber chapel on the quay at Ros dhomhain, the first church on the island. Its bell is the first iron bell on the island, and the custodians ask that it not be rung before the fishing fleet is out.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The bell rung once before the fleet was out

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The chapel bell kept until the fleet is out

events.title: The bell rung once before the fleet was out
events.body: On the morning of its hanging the iron bell of the chapel on the quay at Ros dhomhain is rung for the first service while the fishers are loading their boats in silence, as the rule of that quay requires. The crews unload and go home. Three boats of more than twenty go out on the lake that day.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Mission chapel

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The chapel bell kept until the fleet is out

told_in.book: Of the Door at Doire mhòr
told_in.section: IV. Of the Bell before the Fleet

events.title: The chapel bell kept until the fleet is out
events.body: At the chapel door the custodian of Ros dhomhain tells the minister, with Samuel Wren putting it into the humans' tongue, that a bell over the water before the boats are out is the bell for the drowned. The minister agrees at once, and the bell is rung thereafter only when the last boat is clear of the harbour mouth.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Mission chapel

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The bell rung once before the fleet was out

told_in.book: Of the Door at Doire mhòr
told_in.section: IV. Of the Bell before the Fleet

events.title: The contract carried up to Doire mhòr
events.body: A boy of Muileann chrom carries a contract of A' Chompanaidh up to Doire mhòr, naming the south slope of its hill under the oaks for a working. Beathag Dhubh has it read to her twice in the mill-house at Muileann chrom by the young man of Ros dhomhain who puts A' Chompanaidh's words into Dia-thìris.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first mining contracts

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first refusal

told_in.book: Of the Door at Doire mhòr
told_in.section: V. Of the Paper at the Hearth

events.title: The first refusal
events.body: One mining settlement will not sign a contract. For the present it is passed by, not punished.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The contract carried up to Doire mhòr

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Beathag calls Doire mhòr's households to the hearth

events.title: Beathag calls Doire mhòr's households to the hearth
events.body: On the evening the day for the marks goes by, Beathag Dhubh calls the seven households of Doire mhòr to her fire and has the contract told to them. They talk of iron, oats and sheep. The oldest woman of the hill says that the hill is not theirs, and the households give the answer to the custodian to give.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first refusal

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Beathag Dhubh of Doire mhòr

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The agent's report sent down from Muileann chrom

told_in.book: Of the Door at Doire mhòr
told_in.section: V. Of the Paper at the Hearth

events.title: Beathag Dhubh of Doire mhòr
events.body: The settlement that refused was Doire mhòr, in the hills above Muileann chrom, and its custodian was Beathag Dhubh. Her answer to the Company's agent is known only in his words: that the hill was not hers to sell nor his to buy.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Beathag calls Doire mhòr's households to the hearth

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The agent's report sent down from Muileann chrom

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Beathag writes the road into the roll of Doire mhòr

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The hill buries Beathag Dhubh

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Beathag Dhubh dies at Doire mhòr

events.title: The agent's report sent down from Muileann chrom
events.body: The agent of A' Chompanaidh who climbed to Doire mhòr writes that night at the pit-office by the mill that the custodian heard him out in the rain, did not ask him in, and answered that the hill was not hers to sell nor his to buy. He sends it to Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir with the week's figures and advises that the working be opened elsewhere.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Beathag Dhubh of Doire mhòr

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The road around Doire mhòr

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Beathag calls Doire mhòr's households to the hearth

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The road pegged across Doire mhòr's fields and moved

told_in.book: Of the Door at Doire mhòr
told_in.section: VI. Of the Door

events.title: The road around Doire mhòr
events.body: The Company opens its next working at Cnoc fhiadhaich instead, and runs its cart-road round the fields of Doire mhòr and not through them.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The agent's report sent down from Muileann chrom

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The road pegged across Doire mhòr's fields and moved

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The cart-road round Doire mhòr finished

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The carters water their horses at Doire mhòr

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Beathag writes the road into the roll of Doire mhòr

events.title: The road pegged across Doire mhòr's fields and moved
events.body: Surveyors of A' Chompanaidh peg the line of the new cart-road from Cnoc fhiadhaich straight across the three best fields of Doire mhòr. Beathag Dhubh sends word to the custodian of Muileann chrom that the fields are in no contract. Five days later the surveyors pull their pegs and lay the line round the foot of the field walls, a mile the longer.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The road around Doire mhòr

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The agent's report sent down from Muileann chrom

told_in.book: Of the Door at Doire mhòr
told_in.section: VII. Of the Road round the Fields

events.title: Fenn's lens carried to Tobar dhearg
events.body: The great glass for the new tower on the southern cape, ground over the sea, is carried from Ros dhomhain to Tobar dhearg on a cart packed in straw. James Fenn sets it in the lamp-room of the tower Torcall Clachair has raised over the old fire-tower.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg lit

told_in.book: Of the Door at Doire mhòr
told_in.section: VIII. Of the Light at Tobar dhearg

events.title: Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg lit
events.body: The first of the new beacons is finished on the southern headland at Tobar dhearg: a round tower of grey stone raised over the old fire-tower, paid for by the Company, with a Dia-thìreach keeper. Torcall Clachair builds it; James Fenn sets its lens.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Fenn's lens carried to Tobar dhearg

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Anna nic Dhòmhnaill's tally of lit nights cut on the stair wall

events.title: The cart-road round Doire mhòr finished
events.body: Hill men paid in iron finish the cart-road of A' Chompanaidh from Cnoc fhiadhaich round the fields of Doire mhòr to the quay at Ceann fhada, with a timber bridge at the lower ford of the Doire mhòr stream. The first loaded carts come round the bend in the autumn.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The road around Doire mhòr

told_in.book: Of the Door at Doire mhòr
told_in.section: VII. Of the Road round the Fields

events.title: The carters water their horses at Doire mhòr
events.body: The carters on the new road ask Beathag Dhubh's leave to water their horses at the stream where the road crosses it below Doire mhòr, and she gives it. In wet weather they eat their bread under the oaks before the last pull down to the river.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The road around Doire mhòr

told_in.book: Of the Door at Doire mhòr
told_in.section: VII. Of the Road round the Fields

events.title: The first keeper of Tobar dhearg
events.body: The first keeper of the southern beacon is Anna nic Dhòmhnaill of Tobar dhearg village, a fisherman's widow, who climbs the tower twice a night for the rest of her life. The village holds the keepership as a trust and keeps it in its own families through the age.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Anna nic Dhòmhnaill's tally of lit nights cut on the stair wall

events.title: Anna nic Dhòmhnaill's tally of lit nights cut on the stair wall
events.body: Anna nic Dhòmhnaill, keeper of Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg, who cannot write, begins her count on the wall of the tower stair below the lamp-room: one stroke cut with a knife for every night the light is lit, and a stroke across every thirty.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg lit

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first keeper of Tobar dhearg

told_in.book: Of the Door at Doire mhòr
told_in.section: VIII. Of the Light at Tobar dhearg

events.title: Raiders in the north-western waters
events.body: A Company brig is boarded off the north-west coast and stripped of her cargo of tools. The raiders are never known. The Administration blames the custodians of the coast, and the custodians answer that those waters have always kept their own law.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The answer of the coast read in the hills

events.title: The answer of the coast read in the hills
events.body: The council at Cathair dhearg copies the answer of the custodians of the north-western coast to Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir over the stripped brig, that those waters have always kept their own law, and sends it round the districts. It is read out at the mill at Muileann chrom.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Raiders in the north-western waters

told_in.book: Of the Door at Doire mhòr
told_in.section: IX. Of the Brig and the Bend

events.title: Beathag writes the road into the roll of Doire mhòr
events.body: Under the sixteenth year Beathag Dhubh enters in the roll of Doire mhòr the answer of the coast word for word, and then the road round the village's fields, a mile the longer and well built, with two words after it: for now.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The road around Doire mhòr

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Beathag Dhubh of Doire mhòr

told_in.book: Of the Door at Doire mhòr
told_in.section: IX. Of the Brig and the Bend

events.title: The hawk-priests of Cnoc bheag show Wren their margins
events.body: Samuel Wren comes to Cnoc bheag at the hawk-priests' asking and is shown their copy of his grammar, written in along every margin in the stag-letters. Beside his words keepers of the coal they have set the island's word three times, which means those who have the care of the vein. Wren copies all their notes by the priest's fire.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Wren's grammar

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The hawk-priests read Wren

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The obelisk at Cnoc bheag copied

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The custodian of Cnoc bheag answers Wren at the stakes

told_in.book: Of the Mark and Its Hundred Pence
told_in.section: I. Of Carragh Cnoc bheag

events.title: The obelisk at Cnoc bheag copied
events.body: Samuel Wren copies the writing on the obelisk near Cnoc bheag and sends it over the sea to the scholars of an Tìr Thall. No answer comes. The custodians tell him the stone is older than the Dia-thìrich and that none living can read it.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The hawk-priests of Cnoc bheag show Wren their margins

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The custodian of Cnoc bheag answers Wren at the stakes

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Lowe sets Colbh Cnoc chiar beside Wren's copy of Carragh Cnoc bheag

events.title: The custodian of Cnoc bheag answers Wren at the stakes
events.body: At Carragh Cnoc bheag the custodian of the town tells Samuel Wren what her house has told every asker: the stone is older than the Dia-thìrich, the old schools' letters matched nothing on it, and the four words below were cut later by one who could read no more of it. Wren copies the line three times in the rain.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The obelisk at Cnoc bheag copied

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The hawk-priests of Cnoc bheag show Wren their margins

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Wren blesses the striking-press at Ros dhomhain

told_in.book: Of the Mark and Its Hundred Pence
told_in.section: I. Of Carragh Cnoc bheag

events.title: The first coin
events.body: The humans' coin is brought in beside the old barter, for ease, it is said. Within ten years nothing that needs a tool from over the sea can be had for anything else.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Half of Dùn dhearg comes to the board

events.title: Wren blesses the striking-press at Ros dhomhain
events.body: At Josiah Pell's asking Samuel Wren says a prayer over the new striking-press in its shed on the quay at Ros dhomhain, in the humans' tongue and then in Dia-thìris for the fishers watching at the door. The first mark is lifted from the die with tongs and dropped ringing in the tray.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The mark and its hundred pence

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The custodian of Cnoc bheag answers Wren at the stakes

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Muireall's rubbing of the first mark sent to the loft

told_in.book: Of the Mark and Its Hundred Pence
told_in.section: II. Of the Ship on the Coin

events.title: The mark and its hundred pence
events.body: The coins are struck at Ros dhomhain from silver and copper shipped from an Tìr Thall: the mark and its hundred pence. The first striking bears a ship on one face, and nothing of Dia-thìr on either.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Wren blesses the striking-press at Ros dhomhain

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Muireall's rubbing of the first mark sent to the loft

events.title: Muireall's rubbing of the first mark sent to the loft
events.body: Samuel Wren brings one of the first marks to Gormshuil nic Fhearchair in the long room of the council hall. Her niece Muireall takes a rubbing of both faces, writes beneath it that the island is on neither face, and the rubbing goes east that autumn with the season's copies to the loft of Beathag nic Thòmais at Muileann chaol.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The mark and its hundred pence

links.title: Two books at the capital market

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Wren blesses the striking-press at Ros dhomhain

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The market-clerk's sentence in both books

told_in.book: Of the Mark and Its Hundred Pence
told_in.section: II. Of the Ship on the Coin

events.title: Cathair mhòr refuses the mark
events.body: The market of Cathair mhòr, greatest below the hills east of the capital, refuses the humans' coin for a whole year. The custodians of the town give way when the Company's tool-sellers will not cross their bridge.

events.title: Two books at the capital market
events.body: At the market of Cathair dhearg the tool-sellers take only marks, while cloth and fish still go by barter. The custodians' clerks begin to keep two sets of books, and complain of it in both.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Muireall's rubbing of the first mark sent to the loft

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The market-clerk's sentence in both books

events.title: The market-clerk's sentence in both books
events.body: Tadhg, the custodians' market-clerk at Cathair dhearg, keeps the dues of barter in one book and the dues in marks in another, and can make no single figure of them for the council. At the foot of each he writes that the one book cannot be added to the other, in the stag-letters and again in the humans' tongue.

links.title: Two books at the capital market

links.title: Muireall's rubbing of the first mark sent to the loft

links.title: The masters of Dùn thais invite Wren

told_in.book: Of the Mark and Its Hundred Pence
told_in.section: III. Of the Two Books

events.title: The masters of Dùn thais invite Wren
events.body: The masters of Feallsanachd an Fhèidh at Dùn thais write to Samuel Wren at Ros dhomhain, in the stag-letters, asking him to come for the dark of the year and dispute with them. He goes east with the carriers at the end of an t-Samhain, five days on the road through Cathair mhòr and the hills.

links.title: Wren's winter at Dùn thais

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The market-clerk's sentence in both books

told_in.book: Of the Mark and Its Hundred Pence
told_in.section: IV. Of the Winter at Dùn thais

events.title: Wren's winter at Dùn thais
events.body: The masters of the druid school at Dùn thais receive Samuel Wren for a winter of disputation. He asks them why the vein should be holy; they ask him why his fuel should be burned. Neither telling of that winter names a winner.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The masters of Dùn thais invite Wren

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Wren's letter home on the druids

events.title: Wren's letter home on the druids
events.body: From Dùn thais, in the last days of the year, Samuel Wren writes to the house of his order over the sea by the packet of Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir. He sets down a tale the eldest master told at the hearth of a holy man's voyage west in a boat of hides, very like the voyage of Naomh Breandan as an Eaglais tells it, told from the other shore.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Wren's winter at Dùn thais

told_in.book: Of the Mark and Its Hundred Pence
told_in.section: IV. Of the Winter at Dùn thais

events.title: Drochaid Cathair dhearg rebuilt
events.body: Company masons rebuild in dressed stone the old bridge over Abhainn dhomhain at Cathair dhearg, wide enough for coal-carts to pass two abreast.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Queen Sìleas's stone set back in the bridge

events.title: Queen Sìleas's stone set back in the bridge
events.body: When the masons of A' Chompanaidh take down the parapets of Drochaid Cathair dhearg, Gormshuil nic Fhearchair asks the master mason to keep the block cut with Queen Sìleas's name. He has it dressed on its back and sides, its face left as it was, and sets it again in the new downstream parapet near the middle of the bridge.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Drochaid Cathair dhearg rebuilt

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Tormod mac Ailein walks behind the carriage

told_in.book: Of the Mark and Its Hundred Pence
told_in.section: V. Of the Bridge and the Carriage

events.title: The Commissioner's carriage
events.body: Company wheelwrights build a closed carriage for Josiah Pell, and he drives in it over the new bridge from the Residency to the council at Cathair dhearg. It is the first carriage on the island. The custodians still walk to the council, and say so.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Tormod mac Ailein walks behind the carriage

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Maddox greets the council

events.title: Tormod mac Ailein walks behind the carriage
events.body: Josiah Pell's carriage stops beside Tormod mac Ailein and Gormshuil nic Fhearchair on the new bridge, and Pell offers Ceann a' Chùraim a seat as far as the council hall. Tormod thanks him and answers aloud that they will walk, and the two custodians come up the hill on foot long after the carriage.

links.title: The Commissioner's carriage

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Queen Sìleas's stone set back in the bridge

told_in.book: Of the Mark and Its Hundred Pence
told_in.section: V. Of the Bridge and the Carriage

events.title: Gormshuil reads the harbour articles to the council
events.body: Before the signing of Puingean a' Chalaidh, Gormshuil nic Fhearchair reads the eight sheets aloud to the council at Cathair dhearg, each clause first in the humans' tongue and then in Dia-thìris. Ailean Ruadh of Baile ghlas asks to hear the clause on the anchorages twice.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The Harbour Articles

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Tormod mac Ailein walks behind the carriage

told_in.book: Of the Mark and Its Hundred Pence
told_in.section: VI. Of Puingean a' Chalaidh

events.title: The Harbour Articles
events.body: A second compact, the Harbour Articles, fixes the dues and anchorages of Ros dhomhain in the Company's favour. Like the first treaty it is written in the humans' tongue only, and this time two custodians refuse to sign.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Gormshuil reads the harbour articles to the council

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Gormshuil nic Fhearchair refuses Puingean a' Chalaidh

links.label: Leads to

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Alasdair Liath chosen Ceann a' Chùraim

events.title: Gormshuil nic Fhearchair refuses Puingean a' Chalaidh
events.body: Gormshuil nic Fhearchair passes the sheet of Puingean a' Chalaidh on unsigned, and tells Josiah Pell in his own tongue that she will not put her name under what she has read. Ailean Ruadh of Baile ghlas refuses with her. The council's roll names the two, the first custodians to refuse a writing of the strangers.

links.title: The Harbour Articles

links.title: The fishermen of Baile ghlas

told_in.book: Of the Mark and Its Hundred Pence
told_in.section: VI. Of Puingean a' Chalaidh

events.title: The fishermen of Baile ghlas
events.body: The fishermen of Baile ghlas, whose boats had anchored free at Ros dhomhain time out of mind, are charged anchorage under the Harbour Articles. They take their catch to their own small harbour and sell it there to anyone but the Company.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Gormshuil nic Fhearchair refuses Puingean a' Chalaidh

events.title: The northern concession
events.body: The council grants the Administration upland pasture in the north-west about Muileann àrsaidh, for human families who will not work in the pits. The grant is for grazing; the families build houses of stone.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The council's letter on the grazing

events.title: The council's letter on the grazing
events.body: At Tormod mac Ailein's sickbed Gormshuil nic Fhearchair reads him the letter from Muileann àrsaidh. At his word she writes to the families on the grazing, in both tongues, that the council granted summer grazing and shielings, and sends it north the next morning.

links.title: The northern concession

links.title: Gormshuil nic Fhearchair refuses Puingean a' Chalaidh

told_in.section: VII. Of Grazing, and Chimneys

events.title: Death of Tormod mac Ailein
events.body: Tormod mac Ailein, the high custodian who signed the first treaty, dies at Cathair dhearg. The council chooses Coinneach Glas of Ceann àrsaidh after him, who had never met a human before the Crossing and has dealt with little else since.

events.title: Tormod mac Ailein buried at Cathair dhearg
events.body: Six custodians carry Tormod mac Ailein to the ground behind the council hall, with the bells of the capital ringing, and the mourners lay their stones on the grave going round sunwise. Josiah Pell walks up from the bridge-foot bareheaded to stand at the edge of the ground. Samuel Wren stands at the gate.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Death of Tormod mac Ailein

told_in.section: VIII. Of Tormod's Burying

events.title: Tormod mac Ailein waked three nights
events.body: Tormod mac Ailein is waked three nights in his house below the temple at Cathair dhearg, by the old custom. On the second night the council, meeting below, chooses Coinneach Glas of Ceann àrsaidh in a single evening, and the roll enters the choice as unanimous.

links.title: Death of Tormod mac Ailein

links.title: Tormod mac Ailein buried at Cathair dhearg

told_in.section: VIII. Of Tormod's Burying

events.title: Harrow lost at sea
events.body: Edmund Harrow's ship does not come back from the crossing. The Company passes wholly into Thomas Pike's hands, and the humans' letter-books mourn Harrow as the man who found Dia-thìr.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Harrow's name read in the chapel at Ros dhomhain

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Pike's letter to the council

events.title: Harrow's name read in the chapel at Ros dhomhain
events.body: A' Chompanaidh's men at Ros dhomhain give up Harrow's ship a month past her day. The chapel bell is rung slowly, the flag over the warehouse is lowered to half its pole, and Thomas Pike reads Harrow's name and the names of his crew at the humans' prayers, with Samuel Wren's help.

links.title: Harrow lost at sea

links.title: Pike's letter to the council

told_in.section: I. Of the Ship That Did Not Come Home

events.title: Pike's letter to the council
events.body: The humans' clerks write to the council at Cathair dhearg, in their own tongue and under seal, that A' Chompanaidh has passed wholly to Thomas Pike. Coinneach Glas reads the letter to the sitting and it is entered in the roll.

told_in.section: I. Of the Ship That Did Not Come Home

events.title: The counters' fee held over
events.body: At its autumn sitting the council, its share of the vein-dues now paid in marks by A' Chompanaidh and fewer than before, finds it cannot meet every fee. The fee of the counters who keep the boards of the measured handful is held over to the next sitting.

links.title: The Small-Burning Law

links.title: Pike's letter to the council

told_in.section: II. Of the Empty Board at Dùn dhearg

events.title: Half of Dùn dhearg comes to the board
events.body: At Samhain only the old households of Dùn dhearg bring their sacks to the counters' board in the old granary. The young households have bought their coal by the sack at the market of Cathair mhòr off A' Chompanaidh's carts. Pàdraig Cam counts the season without a fee.

links.title: The Small-Burning Law lapses

links.title: The first coin

told_in.section: II. Of the Empty Board at Dùn dhearg

events.title: The Small-Burning Law lapses
events.body: Centuries of measured burning end within one generation. The Law is never repealed; once its keeping no longer pays, it is no longer kept.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The counters' fee held over

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Half of Dùn dhearg comes to the board

events.title: The last count at Doire mhin
events.body: The custodians of Doire mhin keep the old count of the Small-Burning Law, the measure of coal that might be burned in a year, one season longer than any others. They enter it in their roll with the note that no one asked for it.

events.title: The counter of Dùn dhearg dies
events.body: Pàdraig Cam, counter of Dùn dhearg for forty years, dies in an Gearran. His son is at the pits of Muileann chrom and does not take the board, which hangs in the old granary with the pegs of the last Samhain in their holes. Fionnghal nic Artair begins her letter to the council.

events.title: A defence of the Law at Dùn dhearg
events.body: Fionnghal nic Artair, a custodian of Dùn dhearg, writes to the council in defence of the Small-Burning Law, the only such defence that survives. She holds that the Law was never for the coal's sake but for the people, who would become whatever the burning made them.

events.title: The council files the letter from Dùn dhearg
events.body: Fionnghal nic Artair reads her letter standing to the council at Cathair dhearg. Coinneach Glas thanks her and bids it kept with the rolls, and the roll enters it as read and filed. The same sitting grants Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir leave to widen the road to Muileann chrom for the coal-carts.

events.title: Fionnghal nic Artair rides to Cathair dhearg
events.body: In an t-Ògmhios Fionnghal nic Artair rides west from Dùn dhearg with her letter in defence of Lagh an Loscaidh Bhig sewn in calfskin. She lodges at Doire mhin, where the custodian Anndra mac Eòin shows her the last count of the valley, and reads him the letter by his lamp.

told_in.section: III. Of the Letter and the Road West

events.title: A fair copy of the defence for the loft
events.body: At Gormshuil nic Fhearchair's asking Fionnghal nic Artair makes a fair copy of her letter in her own hand. Muireall nic Fhearchair sends it to the loft of Beathag nic Thòmais at Muileann chaol, where the custodians' papers are kept dry.

told_in.section: IV. Of the Filing

events.title: Murchadh Seabhag preaches at Seann Skell
events.body: At Seann Skell the hawk-priest Murchadh Seabhag preaches that Mòd, the Hungry Hawk of Acaill, starves those who eat faster than the land can feed them. The sermon is copied and carried to the camps, and it is the first writing of the Dia-thìrich that the Company's agents are told to seize.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The hawk sermon carried south in the bird-bags

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A' Chompanaidh's agents seize the hawk sermon in the camps

events.title: The hawk sermon carried south in the bird-bags
events.body: A scribe of the hawk-shrine at Seann Skell writes Murchadh Seabhag's sermon down from his mouth. Fowlers taking birds to the autumn markets carry copies south, and from the markets carters and pedlars bring them into the camps of Muileann chrom and Cnoc fhiadhaich, where readers are given their supper to read them aloud.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Murchadh Seabhag preaches at Seann Skell

told_in.book: Of the Going Out of Lagh an Loscaidh Bhig
told_in.section: V. Of An Seabhag Acrach

events.title: The hearths of Achadh naomh
events.body: The households of Achadh naomh, in the hills north of the workings, who keep Na Seann Spioradan, will not light their hearths with coal bought of the Company. They burn peat as their grandparents did, and their elders teach that coal burned for wages is burned without the ancestors' leave.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Fionnghal nic Artair at the hearths of Achadh naomh

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The custodian of Dùn dhearg goes back to peat

events.title: A' Chompanaidh's agents seize the hawk sermon in the camps
events.body: A' Chompanaidh's agents at Muileann chrom go from hut to hut through the crews' camp with a basket and take every copy of Murchadh Seabhag's sermon they find, eleven in one morning. One woman burns her copy on her hearth before them, and her name is written down.

links.title: Murchadh Seabhag preaches at Seann Skell

events.title: Fionnghal nic Artair at the hearths of Achadh naomh
events.body: Bidden by the elders of Achadh naomh, Fionnghal nic Artair rides north through the hills in an Giblean and reads her letter at the hearth of Sìleas nic Uilleim to the whole village. Asked what burns on her own hearth, she answers bought coal. She is sent home with a creel of peats.

events.title: The custodians at the pump-house of Muileann chrom
events.body: Three custodians sent by Coinneach Glas, Fionnghal nic Artair among them, go down to Muileann chrom to ask that the tally of the hill be kept. Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill takes them to the pump at the deep gallery, where the furnaces are fed by the cartload.

events.title: Burning by the cartload
events.body: The Company's furnaces at Muileann chrom burn coal by the cartload to drive the new pumps, and no heed is paid to the custodians' tally of what the hill may give in a year. Coinneach Glas's council asks that the tally be kept, and is sent a copy of the Company's accounts.

events.title: A' Chompanaidh's accounts filed beside the defence
events.body: The copy of A' Chompanaidh's half-year accounts, sent in answer to the council's asking, is read aloud in its totals by Coinneach Glas and laid in the press of the council hall on the shelf that holds the letter of the custodian of Dùn dhearg.

events.title: Henry Maddox Commissioner
events.body: Josiah Pell sails home to an Tìr Thall and does not return. After him comes Henry Maddox, bidden to double the yield, with a letter from the Company promising him a share of it.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Maddox greets the council

events.title: Maddox greets the council
events.body: Henry Maddox comes before the council at Cathair dhearg in An t-Àrd-mhaor's carriage, greets each custodian in Dia-thìris learned on the ship, and tells them his orders are to double the yield of the pits. He does not speak of A' Chompanaidh's letter promising him a share of it.

told_in.section: VII. Of the Oaks of Cathair fhada

events.title: The oaks of Cathair fhada
events.body: Maddox buys the oak woods about Cathair fhada for pit-props. The town had cut them sparingly for generations; they are gone within the working lives of the men who fell them.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The last oak of Cathair fhada's own cutting

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The woodreeve of Cathair fhada before the council

links.title: The heading at Cnoc fhiadhaich driven without props

events.title: The last oak of Cathair fhada's own cutting
events.body: Before A' Chompanaidh's fellers come, the woodreeve of Cathair fhada and his men fell with axes the one oak the spring lot had fallen on, as the town had cut since An Aois Naomh, and plant six acorns in the ring of its roots. The fellers begin with long saws on the morning after.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The oaks of Cathair fhada

told_in.book: Of the Going Out of Lagh an Loscaidh Bhig
told_in.section: VII. Of the Oaks of Cathair fhada

events.title: The woodreeve of Cathair fhada before the council
events.body: Eòghann mac Phàdraig, woodreeve of Cathair fhada, asks the council to undo the sale of the town's oak woods to Maddox. The council holds that the custodians of Cathair fhada, in debt to A' Chompanaidh's store for seed, had the right to sell, and the clerk enters it.

links.title: The oaks of Cathair fhada

events.title: The custodian of Dùn dhearg goes back to peat
events.body: Home from Cathair fhada in am Màrt, Fionnghal nic Artair has the coal raked out of her grate and lights it again with the peats of Achadh naomh. She sends to find a man of Dùn dhearg who still knows how to cut peat, and pays him what he asks.

events.title: The heading at Cnoc fhiadhaich driven without props
events.body: Under Henry Maddox's order to double the yield, the new gallery at Cnoc fhiadhaich is driven north along the seam on the pay of the ton, and the oak props from Cathair fhada stop at the head of the carters' drift. The agent of A' Chompanaidh writes that the heading will be timbered when the yield allows.

events.body: A tunnel worked faster than any Dia-thìreach crew would have worked it falls in and kills eleven. It is entered as an accident.

events.title: The eleven buried at Muileann chrom
events.body: The eleven dead of the fall at Cnoc fhiadhaich are buried in the ground above the mill at Muileann chrom on the fourth day after the fall. Marsaili nic Sheumais, keeper of the old cutting for Taigh na Fèithe, reads their names at the graves and writes each into the roll with father, mother and hearth, and the place as under the wild hill.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first deaths of haste

links.title: The eleven of Cnoc fhiadhaich

told_in.book: Of the Eleven of Cnoc fhiadhaich
told_in.section: III. Of the Eleven

events.title: Old Dòmhnall says the words at the pit-mouth
events.body: When the eleven are brought out of the fallen heading at Cnoc fhiadhaich, Dòmhnall, an old hewer of the custodians' cutting and father of Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill, says the words of the face at the mouth of the drift, and the old hewers take them up. They had not been said at that pit-mouth since it was opened.

links.title: The first deaths of haste

links.title: The eleven of Cnoc fhiadhaich

links.title: The eleven buried at Muileann chrom

told_in.book: Of the Eleven of Cnoc fhiadhaich
told_in.section: III. Of the Eleven

events.title: The fallen heading cleared and timbered
events.body: The fall at Cnoc fhiadhaich is cleared by midsummer and the heading timbered pair by pair as it is cleared, with oak brought up from Cathair fhada in an t-Ògmhios. The crews are paid nothing for the days of digging, and the yield of the year is short.

links.title: The first deaths of haste

told_in.section: IV. Of the Breakers at the Pit-Mouth

events.title: The eleven of Cnoc fhiadhaich
events.body: The fall was at Cnoc fhiadhaich, in a gallery driven forward without the timbering the Dia-thìrich crews had asked for. The custodians' roll names all eleven dead. The Company's report names none, and calls the gallery "unsound ground."

links.title: The eleven buried at Muileann chrom

links.title: Old Dòmhnall says the words at the pit-mouth

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The fallen heading cleared and timbered

events.title: Raghnall asks three times for timber at the heading
events.body: Between an Gearran and an Giblean the crew-leaders Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill and Ailean mac Dhùghaill ask the agent at Cnoc fhiadhaich three times for props over the heading, where the shale roof has turned the colour the hewers read as bad ground. The agent writes the asking in his book and answers that oak will come in the summer.

links.title: The first deaths of haste

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The fallen heading cleared and timbered

told_in.book: Of the Eleven of Cnoc fhiadhaich
told_in.section: II. Of the Colour in the Roof

events.title: The coughing sickness
events.body: A dry cough runs through the camps at Muileann chrom and Cnoc fhiadhaich, worst among the boys who break coal at the pit-mouth, and thirty-eight die of it. The Mission's surgeon calls it a winter complaint. It lasts through the summer.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Dòmhnall mac Raghnaill at the pit-mouth

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The custodians ask that the breakers' benches be shut

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The hill crews go home to the harvest

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The orphans carried to Cill thais

events.title: Dòmhnall mac Raghnaill at the pit-mouth
events.body: Dòmhnall, the six-year-old son of the crew-leader Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill, who had gone to the breakers' benches at Muileann chrom in the autumn, takes An Casad Tioram in am Màrt. He coughs nine nights on his father's knee and wakes well on the tenth morning, and goes back to the benches in the autumn.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The coughing sickness

told_in.book: Of the Eleven of Cnoc fhiadhaich
told_in.section: IV. Of the Breakers at the Pit-Mouth

events.title: The custodians ask that the breakers' benches be shut
events.body: With An Casad Tioram running through the summer among the children who break coal, the custodians of Taigh na Fèithe ask the agent of A' Chompanaidh to shut the benches at Muileann chrom and Cnoc fhiadhaich until it has passed. He writes the asking in his book, and the benches stay open to feed the pump furnaces.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The coughing sickness

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Burning by the cartload

told_in.book: Of the Eleven of Cnoc fhiadhaich
told_in.section: IV. Of the Breakers at the Pit-Mouth

events.title: The hill crews go home to the harvest
events.body: At the harvests after the fall and after An Casad Tioram the crews of Muileann chrom and Cnoc fhiadhaich go home to their oats, a third of them the first year and half the second, and many stay home through the autumn. The yield of A' Chompanaidh in the hills falls short three years together.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Henry Maddox Commissioner

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The coughing sickness

told_in.book: Of the Eleven of Cnoc fhiadhaich
told_in.section: VII. Of the Offer and the Huts at the Ford

events.title: The orphans of Cill thais
events.body: The village of Cill thais takes in the children orphaned by the coughing sickness and keeps a house for them at its own custodians' cost. The Company, asked to give toward it, sends a crate of Mission primers.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The orphans carried to Cill thais

events.title: The orphans carried to Cill thais
events.body: In an t-Iuchar Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill drives fourteen orphans of the fall and An Casad Tioram in a borrowed cart from Muileann chrom to Cill thais, two days west, with the crate of primers sent by A' Chompanaidh. The warden of Cill thais lifts each child down, has their names written, and sets the crate on a shelf of Taigh nan Dìlleachdan.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The orphans of Cill thais

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The coughing sickness

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first deaths of haste

told_in.book: Of the Eleven of Cnoc fhiadhaich
told_in.section: V. Of the Cart to Cill thais

events.title: Hill coal burned for the lime of Baile ìseal
events.body: The lime for the mortar of the tower at Baile ìseal is burned in a kiln on the shore with coal carted over the hills from Muileann chrom. The tower is built by the masons of the eastern coast of the grey stone of the cape, with a lamp sent by A' Chompanaidh.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Taigh-solais Baile ìseal lit

told_in.book: Of the Eleven of Cnoc fhiadhaich
told_in.section: VI. Of the Light on the Eastern Cape

events.title: Taigh-solais Baile ìseal lit
events.body: The second beacon is lit on the eastern shore at Baile ìseal. Torcall Clachair, now too old to climb, directs its building from a chair at the foot of the headland.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Hill coal burned for the lime of Baile ìseal

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The fishing families of Baile ìseal draw lots for the watches

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Torcall Clachair's last cairn

events.title: The fishing families of Baile ìseal draw lots for the watches
events.body: At the custodians' asking, the keeping of Taigh-solais Baile ìseal is given to the fishing households that had kept the driftwood fire on the cape. They draw lots for the watches at Samhain as they had drawn them for the fire, and the old fire is still lit beside the tower.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Taigh-solais Baile ìseal lit

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The keepers of Baile ìseal

told_in.book: Of the Eleven of Cnoc fhiadhaich
told_in.section: VI. Of the Light on the Eastern Cape

events.title: The keepers of Baile ìseal
events.body: The keepers of the eastern beacon are drawn from the fishing families of Baile ìseal. The town's custodians ask for a rule, and get it, that the lamp be lowered on the nights the boats go out to the deep grounds, lest the fish take fright. When the rule lapsed no one wrote down.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The fishing families of Baile ìseal draw lots for the watches

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Torcall Clachair's last cairn

events.title: Torcall Clachair's last cairn
events.body: Going home west from Baile ìseal in the spring after the lighting, Torcall Clachair has his cart stopped where the road tops the first rise of the moor and the tower first shows over the heather. Seated by the road, he lays a small cairn with his own hands from stones a boy brings from the ditch. He builds no more.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Taigh-solais Baile ìseal lit

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The keepers of Baile ìseal

told_in.book: Of the Eleven of Cnoc fhiadhaich
told_in.section: VI. Of the Light on the Eastern Cape

events.title: Seòlaid Ceann òg
events.body: The traders' boats from the new quay at Ceann òg go down the Abhainn ìseal past Cnoc bheag and Inis bhàn to the north coast, west along it, round the western capes, and south past Inis thais into the capital's water. Their lane is called Seòlaid Ceann òg after the quay. Off the north-west it swings far out into the open sea, and there the ships bound for an Tìr Thall leave it for the passage north-about, and the ships coming down from the north come in.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Men of the foreshores shipped to Ceann òg

events.title: Raghnall takes the leader's share
events.body: The agent at Cnoc fhiadhaich offers Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill a leader's share on every ton his three crews raise, paid to him alone, if he keeps them at the face through harvest and winter; otherwise men of the coast will be brought up. Raghnall puts his mark to the paper in an Cèitean and keeps his crews below through the harvest.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The camp at Àth ìseal

told_in.book: Of the Eleven of Cnoc fhiadhaich
told_in.section: VII. Of the Offer and the Huts at the Ford

events.title: Men of the foreshores shipped to Ceann òg
events.body: In the autumn A' Chompanaidh gathers fishers and net-menders whose foreshores it has bought, ships them from the capital's quays in the traders' boats of Seòlaid Ceann òg round the western capes and up the Abhainn ìseal to Ceann òg, and walks them over the hills to the workings in companies of twenty with their families.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Seòlaid Ceann òg

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The camp at Àth ìseal

told_in.book: Of the Eleven of Cnoc fhiadhaich
told_in.section: VII. Of the Offer and the Huts at the Ford

events.title: The camp at Àth ìseal
events.body: The Company builds a camp of timber huts at Àth ìseal, at the ford below the new workings, for crews brought in from the coast. It is the first settlement on Dia-thìr made for nothing but the pit.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Raghnall takes the leader's share

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Men of the foreshores shipped to Ceann òg

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first crews in the huts at Àth ìseal

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first households leave Doire mhòr

events.title: The first crews in the huts at Àth ìseal
events.body: The first companies from the coast move into the plank huts at Àth ìseal, three long huts with a stove in each, a store and a well, with more rows pegged out beyond. The roll of Taigh na Fèithe notes that the camp has no custodian and has asked for none.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The camp at Àth ìseal

told_in.book: Of the Eleven of Cnoc fhiadhaich
told_in.section: VII. Of the Offer and the Huts at the Ford

events.title: Doire mhòr's water taken
events.body: The Company turns the stream that watered Doire mhòr to wash coal at Cnoc fhiadhaich. No order is written; the stream is dammed one season and not let go. Beathag Dhubh's people carry water by hand for two summers, and then begin to leave.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Beathag Dhubh asks for the order at Cnoc fhiadhaich

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Doire mhòr carries its water from the cattle spring

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Beathag Dhubh's letter to the council entered

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first households leave Doire mhòr

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Beathag Dhubh dies at Doire mhòr

events.title: Beathag Dhubh asks for the order at Cnoc fhiadhaich
events.body: Beathag Dhubh, custodian of Doire mhòr, goes down to the washing-floors at Cnoc fhiadhaich with the carter Seònaid Bhàn and asks the agent Amos Tanner to show her the order that took her village's stream. He has none. The washing needs water, he says, and the stream goes with the working; a complaint may be written and sent on to Ros dhomhain.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Doire mhòr's water taken

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Doire mhòr carries its water from the cattle spring

told_in.book: Of the Green River Run Black
told_in.section: II. Of the Order That Was Not Written

events.title: Doire mhòr carries its water from the cattle spring
events.body: With the stream penned behind the washing gang's bank, the households of Doire mhòr carry their water by yoke and pail from the cattle spring at the foot of the brae, the better part of a mile each way. Beathag Dhubh's roll names every household that carries, and among the carriers is Tormod, son of Ruairidh.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Doire mhòr's water taken

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Beathag Dhubh asks for the order at Cnoc fhiadhaich

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Beathag Dhubh's letter to the council entered

told_in.book: Of the Green River Run Black
told_in.section: I. Of the Stream at Doire mhòr

events.title: Beathag Dhubh's letter to the council entered
events.body: The custodian of Doire mhòr writes to Comhairle a' Chùraim at Cathair dhearg of the taking of Doire mhòr's stream. Seònaid Bhàn carries the letter down the road in her cart and puts it into the hand of a custodians' clerk. The council enters it in its roll, and the stream is not let go that season.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Doire mhòr's water taken

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Doire mhòr carries its water from the cattle spring

told_in.book: Of the Green River Run Black
told_in.section: II. Of the Order That Was Not Written

events.title: The short hunger in the hills
events.body: The men drawn from the farms into the pits, the hill villages of Muileann chrom lose their oats to rain, with none at home to cut ahead of it. The Company sells meal at the camp stores for marks, and the villages have few.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The store at Àth ìseal takes no barter

events.title: Muireall carries Gormshuil's papers to the loft at Muileann chaol
events.body: Muireall nic Fhearchair drives her aunt Gormshuil's papers east in a hired pony-cart to the loft of Beathag nic Thòmais at Muileann chaol, away from the reach of Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir. Held by rain at Cuan chrom, she reads Clàr nan Dà Fhichead Dath aloud to the carter Seònaid Bhàn.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Wren's word-lists

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The store at Àth ìseal takes no barter

told_in.book: Of the Green River Run Black
told_in.section: V. Of the Chest for the Loft

events.title: The store at Àth ìseal takes no barter
events.body: In the hungry autumn the store of A' Chompanaidh at Àth ìseal sells meal to the hill villages over its counter for marks only. Its clerk refuses cheese, wool and a woman's bronze brooch, having no book for them, and the women of the villages send their men back to the pits for coin.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The short hunger in the hills

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Muireall carries Gormshuil's papers to the loft at Muileann chaol

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The meal-carts of Doire fhiadhaich lodged at Cuan chrom

told_in.book: Of the Green River Run Black
told_in.section: III. Of the Wet Harvest

events.title: The meal-carts of Doire fhiadhaich lodged at Cuan chrom
events.body: Nine ox-carts of meal from the villages of Doire fhiadhaich, sent north to the hungry hills under Lagh a' Bhìdh Roinnte, reach the ford at Cuan chrom in the rain of an Dàmhair. The carter of Cuan chrom, Seònaid Bhàn's father, takes their drivers and oxen into his own house and byre for the night.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Meal-carts at Doire fhiadhaich

links.label: Legacy
links.title: The first recorded famine averted

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The store at Àth ìseal takes no barter

told_in.book: Of the Green River Run Black
told_in.section: IV. Of the Meal-Carts from the South

events.title: Meal-carts at Doire fhiadhaich
events.body: The villages of Doire fhiadhaich in the south send carts of meal north to the hill villages, as the old custom of the Holy Age bids in a hungry year. The Company's agents at Àth ìseal buy up two of the carts on the road.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The meal-carts of Doire fhiadhaich lodged at Cuan chrom

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Seven carts give their meal at the village doors

events.title: Seven carts give their meal at the village doors
events.body: Of the nine meal-carts from Doire fhiadhaich, the seven that refuse the agents' marks at Àth ìseal go on into the hills and give their meal away sack by sack at the doors of the hill villages, as Lagh a' Bhìdh Roinnte bids. Their drivers come home by the carriers' road with empty carts.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Meal-carts at Doire fhiadhaich

links.label: Legacy
links.title: The first recorded famine averted

told_in.book: Of the Green River Run Black
told_in.section: IV. Of the Meal-Carts from the South

events.title: The mountain dug by the ton
events.body: For the first time in the history of Dia-thìr the mountain is worked by the ton, and for ends no custom of the Dia-thìrich would have chosen.

events.title: Rope for the winding-gear
events.body: The rope-walks of Dùn chrom, which had made cable for the fishing boats, turn wholly to winding-rope for the pit-heads. The Company pays well, and the town grows by half.

events.title: Gormshuil nic Fhearchair dies at Cathair dhearg
events.body: Gormshuil nic Fhearchair dies at Cathair dhearg in the last days of an t-Sultain, in her seventy-first year. She had kept the council's list of the island's words since the ships came, refused to sign Puingean a' Chalaidh, and learned the humans' letters in her old age.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Wren's word-lists

links.label: Follows from
links.title: One word for the coal

told_in.book: Of the Green River Run Black
told_in.section: V. Of the Chest for the Loft

events.title: The Company's second charter
events.body: The Company is chartered again in an Tìr Thall, with new money and a new name the Dia-thìrich never take up. Its agents at Ros dhomhain now outnumber the Administration's own clerks four to one.

events.title: The first households leave Doire mhòr
events.body: In the second summer of the carrying the first households of Doire mhòr leave the village. Most go down to the timber huts at Àth ìseal, others to Muileann chrom or the capital. Tormod, who had carried water up for two summers, goes down to Àth ìseal with the rest. Beathag Dhubh stays.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Doire mhòr's water taken

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The camp at Àth ìseal

told_in.book: Of the Green River Run Black
told_in.section: VI. Of the Going Down from Doire mhòr

events.title: Barges at Cidhe Beag
events.body: Coal barges begin to load at Cidhe Beag on Abhainn uaine and float the black coal down to the coast. The old canoe landing, used since before the Sundering, is widened with cut stone, and its shrine is moved uphill.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The shrine-stone of Cidhe Beag set under a rowan

events.title: The shrine-stone of Cidhe Beag set under a rowan
events.body: When the canoe landing at Cidhe Beag is widened into a coal quay, the old ferryman of the landing chooses a new place for its shrine-stone on the bank above, under a rowan within sight of the water. Four masons carry it up on a hurdle, and the ferryman puts meal in its hollow.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Barges at Cidhe Beag

told_in.book: Of the Green River Run Black
told_in.section: VI. Of the Going Down from Doire mhòr

events.title: Abhainn uaine silts black
events.body: The washing of coal upstream fills Abhainn uaine with black slurry, and within a few seasons the salmon runs at its mouth fail. The river keeps its name, the green river, and the fishermen speak it bitterly.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The last salmon netted at the green river's mouth

events.title: The last salmon netted at the green river's mouth
events.body: The fishermen of Ceann leathan net the last salmon taken at the mouth of the Abhainn uaine, a small hen fish found empty of eggs. The next spring no fish come in from the sea, the gravel of their spawning grounds lying under the grey slurry from the washing-floors.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Abhainn uaine silts black

told_in.book: Of the Green River Run Black
told_in.section: VII. Of the Green River

events.title: Baile Mòr dhomhain a barge town
events.body: As the coal comes down to it from Cidhe Beag, Baile Mòr dhomhain on the river road grows into the busiest barge town of the north. Its people double in number, most of the newcomers bargemen from the coast.

events.title: Seònaid Bhàn marries Pàdraig mac Artair
events.body: Seònaid Bhàn, carter of Cuan chrom, marries Pàdraig mac Artair, a carter of Doire chaol. They live in her father's house at Cuan chrom beside the roofless carters' house at the quay, and their son Murchadh is born there the next winter.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: An Taigh-seinnse Mòr reopens

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Seònaid Bhàn takes the old carters' house at Cuan chrom

told_in.book: Of the Green River Run Black
told_in.section: VII. Of the Green River

events.title: Baile dhomhain raised as a camp town
events.body: A Company surveyor lays out a second camp, Baile dhomhain, on a grid, the first town of the Dia-thìrich drawn on paper before it was built. Within two seasons it houses four hundred.

events.title: Seònaid Bhàn takes the old carters' house at Cuan chrom
events.body: The custodians of Cuan chrom let the roofless carters' house at their quay to Seònaid Bhàn for a rent of one cheese a year. Twenty carters of Doire chaol give a week's work each towards the new roof for a year's lodging at half price, and its timber comes up from Doire fhiadhaich.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: An Taigh-seinnse Mòr reopens

links.label: Legacy
links.title: The house at the middle of the road

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Seònaid Bhàn marries Pàdraig mac Artair

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Seònaid's rule of marks and barter

told_in.book: Of the Green River Run Black
told_in.section: VIII. Of the House at the Half-way

events.title: An Taigh-seinnse Mòr reopens
events.body: The old carters' house at the half-way stage of the coal road between the capital and the hills is built again, opens its doors at Lùnastal, and keeps the name An Taigh-seinnse Mòr. Its first keeper, Seònaid Bhàn, takes both marks and barter, the only innkeeper on the road who will.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Seònaid Bhàn marries Pàdraig mac Artair

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Seònaid Bhàn takes the old carters' house at Cuan chrom

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Seònaid's rule of marks and barter

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A staff left at An Taigh-seinnse Mòr

events.title: Seònaid's rule of marks and barter
events.body: On the first night of An Taigh-seinnse Mòr Seònaid Bhàn takes a hill carter's cheese and fleece for his bed and supper at the same rate as marks. She has the rule cut on a board over the eastern hearth in the old strokes: Bonn no bathar, an aon bhobhla, coin or goods, the same bowl.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: An Taigh-seinnse Mòr reopens

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Seònaid Bhàn takes the old carters' house at Cuan chrom

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The carters of Doire chaol swear at Seònaid's table

told_in.book: Of the Green River Run Black
told_in.section: VIII. Of the House at the Half-way

events.title: Rathad na Mèinne
events.body: The Company's road-gangs finish metalling the carriers' road from Cathair dhearg by Doire chaol and the ford of Àth chiar to the workings at Achadh dhomhain, wide enough for coal-carts to pass both ways. The carters call it Rathad na Mèinne, the mine road. The posts with the crown's sign that had marked it since the Age of Sundering are left standing along it.

events.title: The carters of Doire chaol swear at Seònaid's table
events.body: Through the winter some thirty carters of Doire chaol, Cuan chrom and the capital meet at the eastern hearth of An Taigh-seinnse Mòr over the lowered rate for hauling coal. On Pàdraig mac Artair's counsel they swear, with their hands on the board of Seònaid's rule, to go to Ros dhomhain together and haul nothing at the new rate.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The carters of Doire chaol

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Seònaid's rule of marks and barter

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Amos Tanner bargains with the carters at An Taigh-seinnse Mòr

told_in.book: Of the Green River Run Black
told_in.section: IX. Of the Carters at Her Table

events.title: The carters of Doire chaol
events.body: The carters of Doire chaol, on the road just east of the capital, band together in a guild to bargain with the Company over the rates for hauling coal. It is the first Dia-thìreach guild of the age, and the Company owns it because that is cheaper than breaking it.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The carters of Doire chaol swear at Seònaid's table

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Amos Tanner bargains with the carters at An Taigh-seinnse Mòr

events.title: Seann Toll made a coal landing
events.body: The Company takes the river landing at Seann Toll, below the workings, and builds a loading stage there for the barges that carry the coal down the Abhainn uaine to Ceann leathan. The town's fishing boats are moved to the next reach.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Amos Tanner bargains with the carters at An Taigh-seinnse Mòr

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A coal ship runs down a Ceann leathan boat

events.title: Amos Tanner bargains with the carters at An Taigh-seinnse Mòr
events.body: Amos Tanner, agent of A' Chompanaidh for the carriage of coal, rides up Rathad na Mèinne to meet the carters' guild of Doire chaol at An Taigh-seinnse Mòr. He tells them of the new coal stage at Seann Toll and the lesser hauling on the road, and they bargain over the rate into the night.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The carters of Doire chaol

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Seann Toll made a coal landing

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The carters of Doire chaol swear at Seònaid's table

told_in.book: Of the Green River Run Black
told_in.section: IX. Of the Carters at Her Table

events.title: The coal ships' lane
events.body: From the landing at Seann Toll the coal barges go down the Abhainn uaine to Ceann leathan, where the Company's ships load at the river mouth and go out by the southern lane, Slighe-mhara Caol fhiadhaich, west along the south coast to the wild strait and the open sea. The fishers of the south coast, who had used the lane for five hundred years, learn to keep out of the coal ships' way.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A coal ship runs down a Ceann leathan boat

events.title: A coal ship runs down a Ceann leathan boat
events.body: A coal ship of A' Chompanaidh coming out of the river mouth on the ebb runs down a fishing boat of Ceann leathan off the bar and does not stop. The two men aboard are taken from the water alive by their neighbours. Within a season the town's boats keep inshore of the ships' track and lie to at the bar when a hull comes down.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Seann Toll made a coal landing

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The coal ships' lane

told_in.book: Of Raghnall Maor
told_in.section: I. Of the Barges Going Down

events.title: Enoch Pratt offers Raghnall the staff
events.body: In an Cèitean Enoch Pratt, agent of A' Chompanaidh at the pits of Muileann chrom, offers Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill a staff of ash capped with brass, a weekly wage in marks and a house, to be set over all the crews of the hill and answer for them to the agent. Raghnall, forty-six years old, takes it.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first Dia-thìreach overseer

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Raghnall Maor

told_in.book: Of Raghnall Maor
told_in.section: II. Of the Staff

events.title: The first Dia-thìreach overseer
events.body: A Dia-thìreach is set over other Dia-thìrich miners, answerable to human masters. It is the first open crack within the Dia-thìrich themselves, and not only between them and the humans.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Enoch Pratt offers Raghnall the staff

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Lisle's rider gathers the papers of the hill

events.title: Raghnall Maor
events.body: The first overseer is Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill of Muileann chrom, a crew-leader who had worked the pits since the first contract. He is given the Company's staff and a house with a slate roof, and from the office the Dia-thìrich give him his byname: Raghnall Maor, Raghnall the steward.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Enoch Pratt offers Raghnall the staff

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Raghnall's slate-roofed house

events.title: Raghnall's slate-roofed house
events.body: A' Chompanaidh's masons from Ros dhomhain build Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill a house of two rooms and a loft on common grazing above the mill at Muileann chrom, with glass windows and a roof of slate, the first slate roof in the town. The miller's wife names him Raghnall Maor as he goes by, and the crews take up the name.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Raghnall Maor

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The roll of Taigh na Fèithe stops naming the overseers

told_in.book: Of Raghnall Maor
told_in.section: III. Of the Slate Roof

events.title: The roll of Taigh na Fèithe stops naming the overseers
events.body: Marsaili nic Sheumais, who keeps the roll of Taigh na Fèithe, enters the first four overseers of the hill by name, then puts the matter to the custodians of the vein. From then on the roll gives only their number under the date, seven in the first year, and says of them only that several are hawk-faithful.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The overseers multiply

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Hawk-priests barred from the camps

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Raghnall's slate-roofed house

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Seumas Dubh set over the pits at Cnoc mhòr

told_in.book: Of Raghnall Maor
told_in.section: IV. Of the Number in the Roll

events.title: The overseers multiply
events.body: Within a few years there are overseers at every working in the district, all Dia-thìrich, all answerable to the Company's agents. The custodians' roll no longer names them, and gives only their number.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The roll of Taigh na Fèithe stops naming the overseers

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Seumas Dubh set over the pits at Cnoc mhòr

events.title: Seumas Dubh set over the pits at Cnoc mhòr
events.body: When A' Chompanaidh opens new pits at Cnoc mhòr and asks for an overseer, Raghnall Maor gives the name of Seumas Dubh, who came into his crews at fifteen. Seumas takes the staff and goes south with his household to a crew of Cnoc mhòr men new to the seam, and runs the haulage three tubs to the rope.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The overseers multiply

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Seumas Dubh killed at Cnoc mhòr

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The roll of Taigh na Fèithe stops naming the overseers

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Coinneach Beag crushed on the haulage

told_in.book: Of Raghnall Maor
told_in.section: V. Of Seumas Dubh

events.title: Coinneach Beag crushed on the haulage
events.body: The haulage rope at Cnoc mhòr parts under three full tubs, and the tubs run back into the gallery-mouth and crush Coinneach Beag, a boy of eleven coming up the rails with an empty. The custodians' roll of Cnoc mhòr gives his name, his age and his mother's name; A' Chompanaidh's report gives the cost of the rope.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Seumas Dubh killed at Cnoc mhòr

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Seumas Dubh set over the pits at Cnoc mhòr

told_in.book: Of Raghnall Maor
told_in.section: V. Of Seumas Dubh

events.title: Seumas Dubh killed at Cnoc mhòr
events.body: Seumas Dubh, overseer of the new pits at Cnoc mhòr, is killed by his own crew after a boy is crushed on a haulage he had ordered hurried. The Company hangs two men at Ros dhomhain, the first hanging done by the Administration on Dia-thìr.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Seumas Dubh set over the pits at Cnoc mhòr

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Coinneach Beag crushed on the haulage

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The two hanged named in the custodians' roll

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The overseers made to stand at the hanging

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A staff left at An Taigh-seinnse Mòr

events.title: The two hanged named in the custodians' roll
events.body: The roll of Cnoc mhòr names the two hewers hanged at Ros dhomhain for the killing of Seumas Dubh, Eòin Ruadh and Fionnlagh mac Aonghais, and records that their neighbours carried them home and buried them in the town's ground. The letter-book of Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir gives them as two of the crew.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Seumas Dubh killed at Cnoc mhòr

told_in.book: Of Raghnall Maor
told_in.section: V. Of Seumas Dubh

events.title: The overseers made to stand at the hanging
events.body: By Henry Maddox's order every overseer of the island stands in a row in front of the crowd at the hanging at Ros dhomhain, fourteen men with their staffs, inside a square of the soldiers of Riaghaltas nan Coigreach. The custodians' roll of Ros dhomhain enters in a line of its own that the overseers stood in front.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Seumas Dubh killed at Cnoc mhòr

told_in.book: Of Raghnall Maor
told_in.section: V. Of Seumas Dubh

events.title: A staff left at An Taigh-seinnse Mòr
events.body: Riding home from the hanging, an overseer of Àth ìseal leaves his staff against the wall of Seònaid Bhàn's house at the half-way stage of Rathad na Mèinne, and in the morning it is gone. He tells the agent it is lost, and A' Chompanaidh gives him another.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: An Taigh-seinnse Mòr reopens

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Seumas Dubh killed at Cnoc mhòr

told_in.book: Of Raghnall Maor
told_in.section: V. Of Seumas Dubh

events.title: Hawk-priests barred from the camps
events.body: Henry Maddox bars the priests of Òrd an t-Seabhaig from the camps, for their preaching slows the work. The overseers enforce the order, though several of them are hawk-faithful, as the roll says. The Mission's chaplains, who keep a chapel in every camp, are not barred.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The roll of Taigh na Fèithe stops naming the overseers

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The sermon in the road at Àth ìseal

events.title: The sermon in the road at Àth ìseal
events.body: Turned back at the gate of the camp at Àth ìseal under Maddox's order by the hawk-faithful overseer Iomhar Bàn, an old priest of Òrd an t-Seabhaig sits down in the road outside the fence, and the crews come out to hear him there. When he is done Iomhar kneels in the road for his blessing. Raghnall Maor stands by.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Hawk-priests barred from the camps

told_in.book: Of Raghnall Maor
told_in.section: VI. Of the Priest at the Gate

events.title: The pox at Ros dhomhain
events.body: A spotted pox comes ashore at Ros dhomhain on a Company ship and climbs the coal road into the camps. The Mission counts four hundred and six dead. The custodians count more, and write the difference in the margin of the Mission's list.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The pox dead of the hill buried below Achadh dhomhain

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The custodians write their dead into the chaplains' margin

events.title: The pox dead of the hill buried below Achadh dhomhain
