events.body: A' Bhreac Bhallach comes up Rathad na Mèinne into the camps of the hill in the last days of an Dàmhair, worst at Àth ìseal and Achadh dhomhain. A' Chompanaidh keeps the pits working. The custodians will not let the pox dead lie among the old graves, and the crews bury them by lamplight in new ground below Achadh dhomhain.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The pox at Ros dhomhain

told_in.book: Of Raghnall Maor
told_in.section: VII. Of the Spotted Pox

events.title: The custodians write their dead into the chaplains' margin
events.body: Marsaili nic Sheumais goes from hearth to hearth on the hill in the spring and writes down the pox dead the chaplains had not found. The custodians borrow the chaplains' list, write their own names down both margins in the old letters with the total at the foot, and send it back to Ros dhomhain, where it is filed.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The pox at Ros dhomhain

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The hill buries Beathag Dhubh

told_in.book: Of Raghnall Maor
told_in.section: VII. Of the Spotted Pox

events.title: The pox in the south
events.body: The pox spreads south from the harbour to Baile chiar and the villages about it. The custodians there cut the names of the dead into the stone lintel of the council house, and they can still be read.

events.title: Baile dhìreach loses its harbour dues
events.body: The Administration moves its customs house from Baile dhìreach to Ros dhomhain and ends the sharing of the harbour dues. The mixed council, left with half an income, cuts its members from six to four.

events.title: The hill buries Beathag Dhubh
events.body: Some hundreds come up to Doire mhòr for Beathag Dhubh's burying, crews from the galleries unwashed among them, leaving A' Chompanaidh's cart-road at the bend to cross her fields by the old path. Raghnall Maor comes without his staff and stands at the back. The roll of Taigh na Fèithe writes her the last door of Doire mhòr that did not open.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Beathag Dhubh of Doire mhòr

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The custodians write their dead into the chaplains' margin

told_in.book: Of Raghnall Maor
told_in.section: VIII. Of the Last Door at Doire mhòr

events.title: Maddox's goods carried down to the ships
events.body: For a week A' Chompanaidh's carts go down Rathad na Mèinne to Ros dhomhain with Henry Maddox's goods, a tall clock lashed upright in a cart of its own among them, and all go aboard the ship that brought Arthur Lisle. The carters say that he came out with one chest.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Arthur Lisle Commissioner

told_in.book: Of Raghnall Maor
told_in.section: IX. Of the Bound Book

events.title: Arthur Lisle Commissioner
events.body: Henry Maddox leaves Dia-thìr a rich man. Arthur Lisle, a lawyer, comes after him, and his first act is to have every compact since the first treaty copied into one bound book.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Maddox's goods carried down to the ships

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Lisle's rider gathers the papers of the hill

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Lisle's clerks bind the agreements in one book

events.title: Beathag Dhubh dies at Doire mhòr
events.body: Beathag Dhubh, custodian of Doire mhòr, who sent A' Chompanaidh's agent down the hill, dies in her own house in an Giblean at sixty-one, among the few hearths left lit after the stream was taken. She is laid out with Doire mhòr's own coal at her head and feet, and the whole hill comes up to her.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Beathag Dhubh of Doire mhòr

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Doire mhòr's water taken

told_in.book: Of Raghnall Maor
told_in.section: VIII. Of the Last Door at Doire mhòr

events.title: Lisle's rider gathers the papers of the hill
events.body: Under Arthur Lisle's first order a rider of Riaghaltas nan Coigreach takes the papers of the pits at Muileann chrom down to Ros dhomhain: the contract of the first thirty and the paper of Raghnall's leader's share. Asked for the agreement that gave the overseers their staffs, Enoch Pratt finds that there is none.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Arthur Lisle Commissioner

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first mining contracts

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first Dia-thìreach overseer

told_in.book: Of Raghnall Maor
told_in.section: IX. Of the Bound Book

events.title: A customs house at Ros gheal
events.body: Lisle opens a second customs house at Ros gheal on the northern coast, where hawk-faithful fishing towns had traded with Company ships without paying dues. The customs officer is twice chased out of the town in his first year.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Lisle's clerks bind the agreements in one book

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The hawk-faithful carry the customs officer out of Ros gheal

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ros gheal rows the customs officer down the coast

events.title: Lisle's clerks bind the agreements in one book
events.body: Arthur Lisle's two clerks spend the winter at Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir copying every agreement made between the island and the strangers since the leave, with Cairt na Companaidh bound at the back. Lisle reads the book through with a pen and writes his queries in the margins; the letter-books keep forty pages of his notes.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Arthur Lisle Commissioner

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A customs house at Ros gheal

told_in.book: Of the Ledgers at the Adit
told_in.section: I. Of the Bound Book

events.title: The hawk-faithful carry the customs officer out of Ros gheal
events.body: Eleven days after the customs house opens, some thirty hawk-faithful of Ros gheal come down from the hawk-house at dusk, carry the officer's table, book and scale into the street, and walk him to the last house on the road south. He returns within the month with two clerks and a letter from Lisle.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A customs house at Ros gheal

links.label: Legacy
links.title: The hawk-house at Ros gheal

told_in.book: Of the Ledgers at the Adit
told_in.section: I. Of the Bound Book

events.title: Ros gheal rows the customs officer down the coast
events.body: At the autumn herring the fishing families of Ros gheal put the customs officer, his clerks, his table and his scale into a boat and set them ashore on a roadless beach two miles down the coast. The town's roll says only that he went away by water. Lisle writes that the town has broken no page, since none yet binds it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A customs house at Ros gheal

told_in.book: Of the Ledgers at the Adit
told_in.section: I. Of the Bound Book

events.title: The silver of Muileann chiar
events.body: The humans seek to claim the silver seam at Muileann chiar as well. It is one of the few things the Dia-thìrich keep wholly in their own hands through all this age.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ùna nic Choinnich calls the guild to the hall

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Coinneach Glas lends Ùna the council's copies

events.title: Ùna finds no silver in Cùmhnant Cathair dhearg
events.body: Reading the council's copies by rushlight at the inns of Rathad na Mèinne on her way home, Ùna nic Choinnich finds coal named on every page of Cùmhnant Cathair dhearg and no word of silver, nor of any metal but the iron the humans paid with. At the inn below Muileann chrom she tells her grandson that A' Chompanaidh holds no paper for the seam.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first written treaty

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ùna nic Choinnich calls the guild to the hall

told_in.book: Of the Ledgers at the Adit
told_in.section: III. Of the Council's Copies

events.title: Ùna nic Choinnich calls the guild to the hall
events.body: The agent of A' Chompanaidh at Muileann chrom sends notice to Muileann chiar that surveyors will measure the silver seam in spring under the charter's first refusal. Ùna nic Choinnich reads the letter in both tongues to forty-one members of Comann an Airgid gathered in the guild hall by night, and resolves to ask the council what it holds.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The silver of Muileann chiar

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Company chartered

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Ùna finds no silver in Cùmhnant Cathair dhearg

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Coinneach Glas lends Ùna the council's copies

told_in.book: Of the Ledgers at the Adit
told_in.section: II. Of the Silver Town

events.title: Coinneach Glas lends Ùna the council's copies
events.body: Ùna nic Choinnich rides three days to Cathair dhearg. Coinneach Glas, Ceann a' Chùraim, aged sixty-eight and ailing, hears her out in the room of the rolls and gives her the council's own copies of Cùmhnant Cathair dhearg, Puingean a' Chalaidh and the pit contracts, bidding her look for the silver before the humans do.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The silver of Muileann chiar

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first written treaty

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Harbour Articles

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Ùna nic Choinnich calls the guild to the hall

told_in.book: Of the Ledgers at the Adit
told_in.section: III. Of the Council's Copies

events.title: Ùna nic Choinnich and the silver guild
events.body: The silver seam was held for the town by its guild of refiners, led by Ùna nic Choinnich. When the Company's surveyors came she met them at the adit with every member of the guild and all its ledgers, and bade them find the humans' name anywhere in either.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The surveyor's report reaches Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Lisle writes that the charter gives A' Chompanaidh nothing

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The guild asks for the compact in both tongues

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A' Chompanaidh charges Comann an Airgid with the burning

events.title: The surveyor's report reaches Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir
events.body: The chief surveyor reports to Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir that the whole of Muileann chiar met him at the working, silent, and that he found no grant or payment to A' Chompanaidh in either of the guild's books and did not think it prudent to proceed. Lisle writes beneath it that he would not have found it either, and sends for the bound book.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Ùna nic Choinnich and the silver guild

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Lisle writes that the charter gives A' Chompanaidh nothing

told_in.book: Of the Ledgers at the Adit
told_in.section: V. Of What the Lawyer Found

events.title: Lisle writes that the charter gives A' Chompanaidh nothing
events.body: In a long letter to the master of A' Chompanaidh, Arthur Lisle sets out that Cairt na Companaidh is a promise made by its own masters and grants nothing on the island, where the only title is Cùmhnant Cathair dhearg, which speaks of coal and says nothing of silver. The master of A' Chompanaidh protests; Lisle answers in two lines.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Ùna nic Choinnich and the silver guild

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Company chartered

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first written treaty

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The surveyor's report reaches Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The guild asks for the compact in both tongues

told_in.book: Of the Ledgers at the Adit
told_in.section: I. Of the Bound Book

events.title: The guild asks for the compact in both tongues
events.body: Answering Lisle's proposal of a compact, Ùna nic Choinnich writes in the humans' letters that the guild will sign, that it must be signed at Muileann chiar where the seam lies, and that it be written in both tongues line against line. Lisle strikes out his clerk's query and agrees, and says he will come himself on Là Fhèill Brìde.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Ùna nic Choinnich and the silver guild

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Lisle writes that the charter gives A' Chompanaidh nothing

told_in.book: Of the Ledgers at the Adit
told_in.section: V. Of What the Lawyer Found

events.title: The Silver Compact
events.body: Arthur Lisle, reading the treaties closely, finds nothing in them touching silver. On Là Fhèill Brìde he signs a compact with the silver guild leaving the seam to the town, the first writing of the age in which the Dia-thìrich keep the better terms.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The compact read in the guild hall

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Lisle sees the silver seam

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Death of Coinneach Glas

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ùna locks the compact in the guild chest

events.title: The council's copies returned from Muileann chiar
events.body: In the spring after the compact Ùna nic Choinnich sends the council's leaves of Cùmhnant Cathair dhearg, Puingean a' Chalaidh and the pit contracts back to Cathair dhearg by her grandson Fionnlagh, wrapped in the same oilcloth they came in, with a bar of silver for the clerk who keeps the presses.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The compact read in the guild hall

told_in.book: Of the Ledgers at the Adit
told_in.section: VI. Of the Guild Chest

events.title: The compact read in the guild hall
events.body: On the evening of the signing, after Lisle's carriage has gone down the valley, Cùmhnant an Airgid is read aloud to Comann an Airgid in the guild hall of Muileann chiar from its Dia-thìris column, and read a second time for the apprentices. It is laid that night in the guild chest under three locks.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Silver Compact

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The council's copies returned from Muileann chiar

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Lisle sees the silver seam

told_in.book: Of the Ledgers at the Adit
told_in.section: V. Of What the Lawyer Found

events.title: Lisle sees the silver seam
events.body: Before leaving Muileann chiar Arthur Lisle asks to see the seam, and Ùna nic Choinnich takes him into the adit with a lamp. He tells her he has never seen the colours in the coal but can see the silver; she answers that the Dia-thìrich see it the same, and that this is why silver is not holy.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Silver Compact

links.label: Legacy
links.title: Silver is not holy

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The compact read in the guild hall

told_in.book: Of the Ledgers at the Adit
told_in.section: V. Of What the Lawyer Found

events.title: Death of Coinneach Glas
events.body: Coinneach Glas, Ceann a' Chùraim since the death of Tormod mac Ailein, dies in his chair in the room of the rolls at Cathair dhearg, aged sixty-nine, after twenty-four years in the seat. He has had Cùmhnant an Airgid read to him twice and called it a better paper than any he signed.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Death of Tormod mac Ailein

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Silver Compact

told_in.book: Of the Ledgers at the Adit
told_in.section: III. Of the Council's Copies

events.title: Alasdair Liath chosen Ceann a' Chùraim
events.body: Comhairle a' Chùraim chooses Alasdair Liath, aged forty-nine, to sit as Ceann a' Chùraim after Coinneach Glas. He has sat on the council since before Puingean a' Chalaidh and voted to sign them. The roll records his age and the number of voices and nothing more.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Death of Tormod mac Ailein

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Harbour Articles

told_in.book: Of the Ledgers at the Adit
told_in.section: VI. Of the Guild Chest

events.title: Seann Bhral the silver port
events.body: The silver guild sends its bars to the sea by the old port of Seann Bhral and not by the Company's quays, and pays the port's custodians in silver for the use of it. The Company finds no ground in the compact to object.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first silver carts go down to Seann Bhral

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The guild's book of weighings filled

events.title: The first silver carts go down to Seann Bhral
events.body: Refusing the request of A' Chompanaidh that its silver pass through the quays of Ros dhomhain, Comann an Airgid sends its first carts of bar silver eighteen miles down the valley to Seann Bhral, and pays the port's custodians by the Muileann chiar weight on every bar. Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir tells the agent of A' Chompanaidh the compact gives no ground to object.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Seann Bhral the silver port

links.label: Legacy
links.title: The Muileann chiar weight made law

told_in.book: Of the Ledgers at the Adit
told_in.section: VI. Of the Guild Chest

events.title: The guild's book of weighings filled
events.body: In the summer after the compact the smelting-floors of Muileann chiar work from dawn to dark, and the guild's paper book of the weighings, begun in An Aois Scaraidh and kept in a dozen hands, is filled by the autumn and a new one begun.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Seann Bhral the silver port

told_in.book: Of the Ledgers at the Adit
told_in.section: VI. Of the Guild Chest

events.title: The carters of Baile gheal
events.body: The carters of Baile gheal in the south-west take up the carrying of Seann Warr brine-salt round the lake to the capital, a trade the Company does not trouble to claim. It keeps the town's folk out of the pits for the whole age.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The guild enters the Baile gheal salt in its ledger

events.title: Ùna locks the compact in the guild chest
events.body: On the day Comann an Airgid reckons its year, the three keyholders open the guild chest and Cùmhnant an Airgid is read aloud in both tongues. Ùna nic Choinnich, aged fifty-nine, lays it back on the new book of weighings beside the notched boards of the old ledger, and the three locks are turned.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Silver Compact

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The guild enters the Baile gheal salt in its ledger

told_in.book: Of the Ledgers at the Adit
told_in.section: VI. Of the Guild Chest

events.title: The guild enters the Baile gheal salt in its ledger
events.body: A carter from the west brings word to Muileann chiar that the carters of Baile gheal have taken up the Seann Warr salt trade round the lake. Ùna nic Choinnich has it written into the guild's new ledger as a thing the humans did not take.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The carters of Baile gheal

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Ùna locks the compact in the guild chest

told_in.book: Of the Ledgers at the Adit
told_in.section: VI. Of the Guild Chest

events.title: The hearths of Àth dhearg take the tower on half-pay
events.body: The custodian of Àth dhearg calls the town's hearths to the room over the net-store. A' Chompanaidh will pay half the cost of a tower on the north-eastern cape in marks and send the lens and oil; the town is to find the stone and the hands, the other half of the pay being the promise that the light will bring its boats home. The town agrees.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Taigh-solais Àth dhearg lit

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Àth dhearg builds the tower

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Torcall's cairn set in the footing of the tower

told_in.book: Of the Keeper's Daybook
told_in.section: I. Of the Fire-Shelf and the Tower

events.title: Torcall's cairn set in the footing of the tower
events.body: The masons of Àth dhearg raise the tower over the old fire-shelf on the cape. They take down the cairn Torcall Clachair built there with James Fenn and set its stones in the footing, facing the sea, and turn a stair inside the wall. The old cut stair up the cliff is left as it was.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The beacon headlands walked

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Àth dhearg builds the tower

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The hearths of Àth dhearg take the tower on half-pay

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first line of the Àth dhearg daybook

told_in.book: Of the Keeper's Daybook
told_in.section: I. Of the Fire-Shelf and the Tower

events.title: Taigh-solais Àth dhearg lit
events.body: The third beacon is lit on the north-east coast at Àth dhearg. Its keeper, Tormod mac Pheadair, keeps a daybook of every ship he sees, and from his book the number of human sailings in these years is known.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The hearths of Àth dhearg take the tower on half-pay

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first line of the Àth dhearg daybook

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Two dates at the head of the daybook

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The Àth dhearg boats brought home in the Bealltach gale

events.title: The first line of the Àth dhearg daybook
events.body: On the night of the lighting Tormod mac Pheadair, keeper of Taigh-solais Àth dhearg, writes the first line in the grey-bound book of the humans' paper that A' Chompanaidh left him: lit at dusk, the wind west and light, and no ship. It is the first keeper's daybook kept on the island.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Taigh-solais Àth dhearg lit

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Torcall's cairn set in the footing of the tower

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Two dates at the head of the daybook

told_in.book: Of the Keeper's Daybook
told_in.section: VIII. Of the Dry Year and the Seed

events.title: Two dates at the head of the daybook
events.body: A man of A' Chompanaidh, unable to tell the days of passing ships from the nights of the moon, writes out the humans' months for the keeper of Àth dhearg. Thereafter Tormod mac Pheadair heads every entry with the humans' day above and the night of the moon beneath, and writes the humans' days in over his first entries.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Taigh-solais Àth dhearg lit

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first line of the Àth dhearg daybook

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The Àth dhearg boats brought home in the Bealltach gale

told_in.book: Of the Keeper's Daybook
told_in.section: II. Of the First Line

events.title: The Àth dhearg boats brought home in the Bealltach gale
events.body: A north-easterly gale catches four boats of Àth dhearg on the long lines beyond the reef. The keeper lights the lamp an hour before dusk. Three boats come home by the light through the night, one from the wrong side of the reef; the fourth returns at dawn a man short. Tormod mac Pheadair enters the boats and the lost man by name.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Taigh-solais Àth dhearg lit

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Two dates at the head of the daybook

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The masons' pay entered in the roll of Àth dhearg

told_in.book: Of the Keeper's Daybook
told_in.section: III. Of the Boats Brought Home

events.title: Àth dhearg builds the tower
events.body: The masons of the beacon at Àth dhearg are its own townsmen, paid half in marks and half in the promise that the tower will guide their own boats home. Tormod mac Pheadair, the keeper, is one of them.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The hearths of Àth dhearg take the tower on half-pay

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Torcall's cairn set in the footing of the tower

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The masons' pay entered in the roll of Àth dhearg

events.title: The masons' pay entered in the roll of Àth dhearg
events.body: When A' Chompanaidh pays the eleven masons of the tower in marks at its foot, the custodian's clerk enters the payment in the town's roll, and beside it that the other half of their pay was made in the Bealltach gale, in four boats and three of them home.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Àth dhearg builds the tower

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Àth dhearg boats brought home in the Bealltach gale

told_in.book: Of the Keeper's Daybook
told_in.section: III. Of the Boats Brought Home

events.title: Pirates off the eastern coast
events.body: Raiders in low black boats take a Company coal ship off the eastern coast and burn her to the waterline, cargo and all. The Company says the silver guild paid them. The silver guild says nothing.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The keeper of Àth dhearg sees the burning collier

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The keeper will not write the black boats

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The collier's crew fed near Ceann leathan

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A' Chompanaidh charges Comann an Airgid with the burning

events.title: The keeper of Àth dhearg sees the burning collier
events.body: Two nights after entering a laden collier of A' Chompanaidh going south, Tormod mac Pheadair sees a red light low in the south under the cloud from the middle watch until near dawn, and writes that he does not know what it was. The carters bring word four days later that raiders have burned her.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Pirates off the eastern coast

told_in.book: Of the Keeper's Daybook
told_in.section: IV. Of the Glow in the South

events.title: The keeper will not write the black boats
events.body: In Dubhlas a clerk of A' Chompanaidh rides to Àth dhearg to read the daybook and asks the keeper to write in black raiding boats seen going south before the burning. Tormod mac Pheadair answers that he saw none and will write no boat he has not seen. The clerk reports the book of no assistance.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Pirates off the eastern coast

told_in.book: Of the Keeper's Daybook
told_in.section: IV. Of the Glow in the South

events.title: The gunboat entered at Àth dhearg
events.body: In Teasach of the forty-seventh year a black two-masted ship of war of A' Chompanaidh, a gun in her bows under canvas and more men on deck than any trader carries, comes round the north coast and south past the cape. The keeper of Àth dhearg enters her with more care than any ship before.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A cove burned near Ceann leathan

told_in.book: Of the Keeper's Daybook
told_in.section: V. Of the Gunboat and the Cove

events.title: The collier's crew fed near Ceann leathan
events.body: The raiders who burn the collier of A' Chompanaidh put her crew into their own boat and set them rowing for the land. The crew come ashore alive at a fishing village near Ceann leathan, where the households feed and shelter them until a rider can carry word south to Seann Bhral.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Pirates off the eastern coast

told_in.book: Of the Keeper's Daybook
told_in.section: IV. Of the Glow in the South

events.title: A' Chompanaidh charges Comann an Airgid with the burning
events.body: Within a month of the burning the agents of A' Chompanaidh say at Seann Bhral and Ros dhomhain, and write to Arthur Lisle, that Comann an Airgid paid the raiders in spite for the surveyors turned back from the adit at Muileann chiar. The guild makes no answer.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Pirates off the eastern coast

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Ùna nic Choinnich and the silver guild

told_in.book: Of the Keeper's Daybook
told_in.section: IV. Of the Glow in the South

events.title: A cove burned near Ceann leathan
events.body: A Company gunboat hunts the raiders to a cove near Ceann leathan and burns every boat drawn up on the shingle, most of them belonging to the town's fishermen. The raiders are not found.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The gunboat entered at Àth dhearg

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Àth dhearg lends two boats to Ceann leathan

events.title: Àth dhearg lends two boats to Ceann leathan
events.body: A fisherman of Ceann leathan walks north nearly forty miles with two sons to ask Àth dhearg for a boat after the gunboat burns the cove. The households talk into the night and lend two, to be returned when Ceann leathan has built its own, and the three sail them south in Lùghnas.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A cove burned near Ceann leathan

told_in.book: Of the Keeper's Daybook
told_in.section: V. Of the Gunboat and the Cove

events.title: The wall's footing on the shingle of Baile dhìreach
events.body: Promised timber by A' Chompanaidh, the yard-master Daniel Lusk asks the council of four at Baile dhìreach for a dry-stone wall up the town's shingle and lays its footing while they argue. The town's members hold that the shingle is kept and not built on. On the third night the stones are carried below the wrack-line.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The end of the joint council

told_in.book: Of the Keeper's Daybook
told_in.section: VI. Of the Wall on the Shingle

events.title: The shingle clause read from both books
events.body: Nathan Cobb reads the compact of Baile dhìreach from the humans' book, where the shingle is the town's property; Iain Hale reads it from the Dia-thìris book, where the shingle is kept for the town. Asked by both sides which book is right, Iain Hale closes the book and says nothing.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The end of the joint council

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Baile dhìreach under one council

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The Hales keep their house at Baile dhìreach

told_in.book: Of the Keeper's Daybook
told_in.section: VI. Of the Wall on the Shingle

events.title: The end of the joint council
events.body: The mixed council of Baile dhìreach breaks up in a quarrel over a boundary wall and never meets again. The human families go to Ros bheag and Ros dhomhain; the Dia-thìrich families stay. Households that were both split or fell silent, and which did which is not told.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The wall's footing on the shingle of Baile dhìreach

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The shingle clause read from both books

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The Hales keep their house at Baile dhìreach

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The humans' book set back on the shelf

events.title: The Hales keep their house at Baile dhìreach
events.body: When the council breaks and the human families leave for Ros bheag and Ros dhomhain, Samuel Hale, Eilidh nic Ruairidh and their son Iain stay in their house by the well at the head of the street. They take neither side on the wall and speak of other things when it is mentioned.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The end of the joint council

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A marriage in two tongues

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The shingle clause read from both books

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Iain Hale refuses the yard at Inis chrom

told_in.book: Of the Keeper's Daybook
told_in.section: VII. Of the Yard That Went East

events.title: Iain Hale refuses the yard at Inis chrom
events.body: Daniel Lusk offers Iain Hale the foreman's place in the yard going to Inis chrom, for more marks than the yard has ever paid. After a night on the shingle and a talk with his father, Iain Hale refuses, and that winter builds the town's boats on the old slip by the town's leave.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The boatyard moves to Inis chrom

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Hales keep their house at Baile dhìreach

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The humans' book set back on the shelf

told_in.book: Of the Keeper's Daybook
told_in.section: VII. Of the Yard That Went East

events.title: The boatyard moves to Inis chrom
events.body: The human boatbuilders of Baile dhìreach move their yard to Inis chrom, a day's sail east, where the Company has promised them timber. The town takes them in without a joint council or any other compact, and within a generation they fade from its rolls.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Iain Hale refuses the yard at Inis chrom

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The humans' book set back on the shelf

events.title: The humans' book set back on the shelf
events.body: When the yard has sailed for Inis chrom, Iain Hale finds the council's book in the humans' tongue left open on the mending-table in the net-loft at Baile dhìreach, at a page with a date and nothing under it. He closes it and sets it back on the shelf beside the Dia-thìris book.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The boatyard moves to Inis chrom

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The end of the joint council

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Iain Hale refuses the yard at Inis chrom

told_in.book: Of the Keeper's Daybook
told_in.section: VII. Of the Yard That Went East

events.title: The rain fails in the Àth dhearg daybook
events.body: Through the spring and summer of the forty-eighth year the daybook of Àth dhearg records dry winds night after night, the fields inland yellow before midsummer, a heath fire of three days, and the burn below the town stopped, which it has never done in memory. Rain is written once in four months.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The dry year in the east

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Tormod mac Pheadair reads the seed loan at Baile ruadh

told_in.book: Of the Keeper's Daybook
told_in.section: VIII. Of the Dry Year and the Seed

events.title: The dry year in the east
events.body: For a single season the rain fails over the eastern farmlands about Achadh shean. It is a warning, and no one heeds it.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The rain fails in the Àth dhearg daybook

events.title: Tormod mac Pheadair reads the seed loan at Baile ruadh
events.body: Called by his wife's kin, the keeper of Àth dhearg walks to Baile ruadh and reads to its council, figure by figure, the terms in the humans' figures by which A' Chompanaidh's store at Seann Dunn lends seed corn for grain over five harvests. He finds the figures as the interpreter gave them.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Baile ruadh loses its seed

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The rain fails in the Àth dhearg daybook

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Baile ruadh's seed debt entered

told_in.book: Of the Keeper's Daybook
told_in.section: VIII. Of the Dry Year and the Seed

events.title: Baile ruadh loses its seed
events.body: At Baile ruadh in the east the drought kills the seed corn in the ground, and the town borrows seed from the Company's store at Seann Dunn, at a price paid back over five harvests. It is the first Dia-thìreach town to owe the Company a debt in grain.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Tormod mac Pheadair reads the seed loan at Baile ruadh

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Baile ruadh's seed debt entered

events.title: Baile ruadh's seed debt entered
events.body: The custodians' roll of Baile ruadh enters the town's debt of seed corn to A' Chompanaidh under the night of the moon, with the measure and the five harvests, the first debt in grain to the strangers in any roll of the island. The clerk writes beside it the name of the keeper who read the figures.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Baile ruadh loses its seed

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Tormod mac Pheadair reads the seed loan at Baile ruadh

told_in.book: Of the Keeper's Daybook
told_in.section: VIII. Of the Dry Year and the Seed

events.title: Aonghas mac Coinnich's question
events.body: At Dùn thais the druid master Aonghas mac Coinnich puts to his students a question the school's register calls new: why the humans cannot see the colour in broken coal that every Dia-thìreach child sees. He does not answer it, and the register notes that he called it the wrong question.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Three students carry the question west

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Eachann Mòr asks the question at Dùn thais

events.title: Three students carry the question west
events.body: In the autumn three students of Taigh na Deasbaid at Dùn thais walk over the high moor to Baile Mòr uaine, carrying Aonghas mac Coinnich's question with a sealed copy in the register-keeper's hand. The masters of Baile Mòr uaine take it up at the dark of the year.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Aonghas mac Coinnich's question

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The druid students of Baile Mòr uaine

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The four hundred leaves come back to Dùn thais

told_in.book: Of the Question at Dùn thais
told_in.section: II. Of the Summer of Arguing

events.title: The druid students of Baile Mòr uaine
events.body: Students of Aonghas mac Coinnich carry his question to Baile Mòr uaine and teach it in the town's hall of disputation. The hall's record of the argument runs to four hundred leaves, and ends, like his, without an answer.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Three students carry the question west

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The four hundred leaves come back to Dùn thais

events.title: The four hundred leaves come back to Dùn thais
events.body: The record of the argument at Baile Mòr uaine comes back to Dùn thais leaf by leaf with the carriers, four hundred leaves in all. Its last leaf lists those who spoke and notes that the hall adjourned because the peat was done. Aonghas mac Coinnich reads every leaf and names no argument the best.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The druid students of Baile Mòr uaine

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Three students carry the question west

told_in.book: Of the Question at Dùn thais
told_in.section: II. Of the Summer of Arguing

events.title: Cathair gheal in the northern concession
events.body: The human families of the northern concession found a market town at Cathair gheal, with a stone hall for their magistrate and a chapel. The Administration issues its charter without asking the custodians.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Eachann Mòr loses his seat

events.title: Eachann Mòr loses his seat
events.body: The council at Cathair dhearg protests Cairt Chathair gheal, which names no custodian, and receives an answer in the humans' tongue that none of its members can read with confidence. At the autumn choosing at Ceann àrsaidh the households put out Eachann Mòr, who has no letters of that tongue, and choose Dùghall Òg of the carting families, who worked five years at A' Chompanaidh's weigh-house.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Cathair gheal in the northern concession

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The family of Eachann Mòr

told_in.book: Of the Question at Dùn thais
told_in.section: IV. Of Eachann Mòr's Seat

events.title: Human farms at Cnoc ghorm
events.body: Human farmers of the concession clear land beside the Dia-thìrich village of Cnoc ghorm in the upland north-west, and build a mill. The villagers sell them grain until the mill is working, and then stop.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Cnoc ghorm stops selling grain

events.title: Cnoc ghorm stops selling grain
events.body: Through the first winter the villagers of Cnoc ghorm sell grain at a fair price to the human farmers who have cleared land beside them, and carry it on their own ponies. When the farmers' mill turns in the spring, they sell no more, and give no reason. Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise's letters speak of a coolness at the old village.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Human farms at Cnoc ghorm

told_in.book: Of the Question at Dùn thais
told_in.section: III. Of the Town with No Custodian

events.title: A fishing station at Ceann mhòr
events.body: A few human fishing families of the concession settle at Ceann mhòr, the harbour under the north-western headland. They are the first humans to fish the island's waters for a living and not for the Company's table.

events.title: The first Dia-thìreach child sent over the sea
events.body: One family, hoping for better treatment, sends a son to be schooled in the humans' homeland. He is never known to return.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Calum's ship sails north-about

events.title: The family of Eachann Mòr
events.body: The family that sent its son away was that of Eachann Mòr, a custodian of Ceann àrsaidh who had lost his seat on the council. The boy, Calum, sailed over the sea on a Company ship with a letter from the Mission and a purse of marks.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Eachann Mòr loses his seat

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Calum's ship sails north-about

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Eachann Mòr's first letter over the sea

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The passenger line read at A' Chompanaidh's counter

events.title: Calum's ship sails north-about
events.body: Calum, son of Eachann Mòr, thirteen years old, goes aboard a ship of A' Chompanaidh at the quay below Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir at Ros dhomhain with Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise's letter and a purse of marks sewn into his coat. A pilot of Caol leathan takes her down the Abhainn gheal on the evening tide, and she turns north up the west coast to go round by the north to the humans' land.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first Dia-thìreach child sent over the sea

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The family of Eachann Mòr

told_in.book: Of the Question at Dùn thais
told_in.section: V. Of the Ship That Went North-about

events.title: The Mission school
events.body: The Mission opens a school at Ros dhomhain for Dia-thìrich children, taught in the humans' tongue. It takes thirty pupils in its first year, most of them overseers' children, and among them the Mission counts its first Dia-thìrich converts.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Eachann Mòr's first letter over the sea

events.title: Eachann Mòr's first letter over the sea
events.body: No letter comes from Calum by the autumn ships. In the winter Eachann Mòr writes to his son in Dia-thìris, pays a pupil of Scoil na Teachdaireachd to put it into the humans' tongue beneath his lines, and gives it with a mark to the master of the first ship going north. No answer comes to it, nor to the three he sends after it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The family of Eachann Mòr

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Mission school

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ciorstaidh nic Eachainn at the school of Inis bhàn

told_in.book: Of the Question at Dùn thais
told_in.section: VI. Of the Letters That Did Not Come

events.title: Schooling at Inis bhàn
events.body: The custodians of Inis bhàn in the north open a school of their own in answer to the Mission's, and teach the old reckoning, the rolls and the names of the hills. The Mission complains that the pupils come to its school the next year already knowing how to argue.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ciorstaidh nic Eachainn at the school of Inis bhàn

events.title: Ciorstaidh nic Eachainn at the school of Inis bhàn
events.body: Eachann Mòr sends his daughter Ciorstaidh, ten years old, to the custodians' new school at Inis bhàn. She comes home at midsummer able to name forty hills and to argue the boundaries of her father's parish. The custodians of Inis bhàn keep Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise's complaint about their pupils as a testimonial.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Schooling at Inis bhàn

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Eachann Mòr's first letter over the sea

told_in.book: Of the Question at Dùn thais
told_in.section: VI. Of the Letters That Did Not Come

events.title: Tobacco on the concession farms
events.body: Human farmers of the northern concession plant tobacco on the sheltered slopes behind Ceann mhòr and sell the dried leaf to the Company's ships. Of the crops the humans brought, it alone is still grown on Dia-thìr.

events.title: Drochaid Ros fhionn
events.body: The Company rebuilds the old bridge over the river at Ros fhionn to carry the eastern coal road. While the carts run it is the busiest crossing on that side of the island.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The students at Drochaid Ros fhionn

events.title: The students at Drochaid Ros fhionn
events.body: Aonghas mac Coinnich takes the students of Dùn thais to watch the first coal-carts cross the rebuilt bridge at Ros fhionn, forty in an afternoon. The island's drivers throw down lumps for them to name; the two human drivers look at their loads as at stones. Ailean Clachair's sign stays in the keystone.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Drochaid Ros fhionn

told_in.book: Of the Question at Dùn thais
told_in.section: VII. Of the Coal Road in the East

events.title: Coal through Inis bheag
events.body: Coal from the eastern workings is carted over the new bridge and down to the river quays of Inis bheag, and goes by barge to Caol chrom at the river mouth for shipping. The Company deepens the river at the quays, and the town's old fish market is moved to make room for the coal stage.

events.title: Baile mhin ships the eastern coal
events.body: The river quays of Baile mhin, below Inis bheag on the Abhainn bheag, take the eastern coal that Inis bheag cannot load. The townsfolk are paid by the barge, and with the gain the town builds its first stone houses.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The passenger line read at A' Chompanaidh's counter

events.title: The passenger line read at A' Chompanaidh's counter
events.body: In the third year after his son sailed Eachann Mòr asks at A' Chompanaidh's counter at Ros dhomhain after the ship by name. She has come and gone twice since, under another master now. Against the day Calum sailed the clerk reads one line, a native boy, his fare paid in full, and says his book knows nothing more.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The family of Eachann Mòr

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Baile mhin ships the eastern coal

told_in.book: Of the Question at Dùn thais
told_in.section: VI. Of the Letters That Did Not Come

events.title: Caol gharbh passed by
events.body: The coal road to Inis bheag passes Caol gharbh by a mile, and the town, which had hoped for the traffic, gets only its dust. Its custodians write that they had not known a town could be harmed by a road it was not on.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Caol gharbh's letter on the door at Dùn thais

events.title: Caol gharbh's letter on the door at Dùn thais
events.body: Aonghas mac Coinnich pins a copy of the letter of Caol gharbh's custodians, who wrote that they had not known a town could be harmed by a road it was not on, to the door of Taigh na Deasbaid at Dùn thais beside the carved lintel. It stays there until the rain takes it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Caol gharbh passed by

told_in.book: Of the Question at Dùn thais
told_in.section: VII. Of the Coal Road in the East

events.title: The thing in the north-western sea
events.body: The crew of a Company brig see a beast greater than their ship off the north-western headlands. The Administration's clerk files their report with the complaints about pirates, and the Dia-thìrich sailors of the coast say they had wondered when the humans would see it.

events.title: A brig lost in the mist
events.body: A Company brig bound for the northern landing with tools is caught by a gale in sea mist off Eilean fhada and driven onto the skerries. Her crew wade ashore at low water and walk to the harbour at Caol bheag. Thereafter the Company's charts mark the northern passage closed to its ships from midwinter to the end of spring, the season of the gales.

events.title: Whale-boats out of Àth fhionn
events.body: Human fishermen of the concession teach the boats of Àth fhionn to hunt whales with the hand-lance, and not wait for them to strand. The oil is sold to the Company for its lamps, and from this time whale-boats go out from the north coast every summer.

events.title: Surveyors lost at Doire uaine
events.body: Two Company surveyors go up into the hills at Doire uaine against the villagers' counsel and are not seen again. The Company sends a search party, which comes back after a day and will go no further.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The search party returns from Doire uaine

events.title: The search party returns from Doire uaine
events.body: A' Chompanaidh's search party of eight men goes up into the hills of Doire uaine and comes down the same evening. They report the lost surveyors' chains laid out along a ridge and a ring of fire-stones with no ash in it, and refuse to go further for pay or threats. The agent writes to Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir that the men are idle.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Surveyors lost at Doire uaine

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The offerings at Doire uaine

told_in.book: Of the Question at Dùn thais
told_in.section: VIII. Of the Things the Clerks Could Not File

events.title: The offerings at Doire uaine
events.body: After the surveyors are lost the villagers of Doire uaine leave salt and coal for the sìth at the foot of the hills, as their grandparents did after any death on the high ground. The Company forbids coal to be left lying and has the offerings gathered up, and the villagers leave salt alone.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The search party returns from Doire uaine

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Eachann Mòr asks the question at Dùn thais

events.title: Eachann Mòr asks the question at Dùn thais
events.body: At the end of harvest Eachann Mòr rides two days from Ceann àrsaidh to Dùn thais and asks Aonghas mac Coinnich whether his son, five years among the humans, will see the colour in the coal when he comes home. The master puts a broken lump in his hand and will not answer. The register records that a man came to ask the question and the master did not answer it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Aonghas mac Coinnich's question

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The offerings at Doire uaine

told_in.book: Of the Question at Dùn thais
told_in.section: IX. Of the Question Put Back

events.title: The tithe raised
events.body: The share of mined coal taken by the humans' Administration rises steeply. What the Dia-thìrich receive does not rise with it.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Anne Colby lands at Ros dhomhain

events.title: Anne Colby lands at Ros dhomhain
events.body: Anne Colby comes ashore at the Ros dhomhain quays at two and twenty, sent out by Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise with a chest of linen and instruments she has scarcely been shown how to use, hoping to hear word of a brother lost years before on Harrow's ships. She finds no word of him; within the year she finds the flux.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The tithe raised

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The flux at Ros dhomhain

told_in.book: Of the Tithe and the Flux
told_in.section: III. Of the Sick-House in the Chapel

events.title: Lisle's tithe schedule
events.body: The new schedule goes out from the Residency under Arthur Lisle's hand and raises the Administration's share from one part in five to one part in three. The custodians receive a copy in the humans' tongue, with a rendering made by a Mission pupil.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Barabal nic Dhùghaill reads the schedule at Cathair dhearg

events.title: Barabal nic Dhùghaill reads the schedule at Cathair dhearg
events.body: A pupil of Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise of fifteen, Barabal nic Dhùghaill, renders Lisle's three sealed sheets into Dia-thìris before the council, reading the new fraction twice over at the old custodian of Cnoc bheag's asking. The council has her rendering copied word for word into every coal town's roll, with her own name set at the foot of each copy.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Lisle's tithe schedule

told_in.book: Of the Tithe and the Flux
told_in.section: I. Of the Schedule Read Twice

events.title: Weighing the grain at Dùn fhiadhaich
events.body: At Dùn fhiadhaich the tithe-gatherers begin to weigh grain as well as coal, saying the town's farms feed the pits and share in their gain. The custodians' roll calls it the tithe on the tithe.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The tithe on the tithe named at Dùn fhiadhaich

events.title: The tithe on the tithe named at Dùn fhiadhaich
events.body: Griogair Fada, the largest farmer under Cnoc naomh, asks the young tithe-gatherer who set the new weight on grain and gets no answer he can carry home. The custodians of Dùn fhiadhaich enter the weighing in their roll under a name of their own coining, deachamh an deachaimh, the tithe on the tithe.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Weighing the grain at Dùn fhiadhaich

told_in.book: Of the Tithe and the Flux
told_in.section: II. Of the Weighing at Dùn fhiadhaich

events.title: The flux at Ros dhomhain
events.body: A bloody flux breaks out in the crowded quarters at the Ros dhomhain quays. The Mission's nurse, Anne Colby, makes a sick-house of the chapel, and it is said that she kept the dead below two hundred.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Anne Colby lands at Ros dhomhain

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A' Chompanaidh's surgeon visits once

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Mòr nic Amhlaidh's counsel on names

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Colby turns the chapel into a sick-house

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Colby's roll of the dead by name

events.title: A' Chompanaidh's surgeon visits once
events.body: A' Chompanaidh's own surgeon comes to the chapel door at Ros dhomhain, will not step past the threshold, and tells Colby she would do better to let the sick lie where they were found. He sends, before he leaves the harbour, a case of salts and does not come again.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The flux at Ros dhomhain

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Mòr nic Amhlaidh's counsel on names

told_in.book: Of the Tithe and the Flux
told_in.section: III. Of the Sick-House in the Chapel

events.title: Mòr nic Amhlaidh's counsel on names
events.body: Washing the chapel floor by lamplight on Colby's first night of nursing the flux, the widow Mòr nic Amhlaidh tells her that the dying want their own names said to them more than they want the fever broken. Colby is said to have kept the counsel from that night on.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The flux at Ros dhomhain

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A' Chompanaidh's surgeon visits once

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Colby turns the chapel into a sick-house

told_in.book: Of the Tithe and the Flux
told_in.section: III. Of the Sick-House in the Chapel

events.title: Colby turns the chapel into a sick-house
events.body: Anne Colby has Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise's chapel at Ros dhomhain opened and its benches carried into the yard without asking anyone's leave, and with Mòr nic Amhlaidh and her daughter carries the flux-sick up from the harbour lodgings on a hand-barrow until the stone room and its yard hold as many as can lie down.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The flux at Ros dhomhain

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Mòr nic Amhlaidh's counsel on names

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Colby's roll of the dead by name

told_in.book: Of the Tithe and the Flux
told_in.section: III. Of the Sick-House in the Chapel

events.title: Colby's roll of the dead by name
events.body: Each evening Anne Colby sits at the chapel door with the custodians' own roll open on her knee and a clerk's boy to read her the entries, and sets down against every name who lived and who died, in English, in a column she turns round on the table for the custodians to see is kept.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The flux at Ros dhomhain

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Colby turns the chapel into a sick-house

told_in.book: Of the Tithe and the Flux
told_in.section: III. Of the Sick-House in the Chapel

events.title: The flux reaches Seann Vell
events.body: The coal barges carry the flux to Seann Vell, the river port east of the capital on the Abhainn fhionn. The custodians of the town shut the barge landing for a season, and the Company fines them for it.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A bargeman put ashore at Seann Vell

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Seann Vell shuts its landing

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A' Chompanaidh fines Seann Vell for the shut landing

events.title: A bargeman put ashore at Seann Vell
events.body: A bargeman on the coal run east from Ros dhomhain falls sick at his pole and is put ashore at the Seann Vell landing rather than carried on, the barge-master judging, wrongly, that dry land would serve him better than the water. Within the month the flux is in a dozen houses of the town.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The flux reaches Seann Vell

told_in.book: Of the Tithe and the Flux
told_in.section: IV. Of the Barges to Seann Vell

events.title: Seann Vell shuts its landing
events.body: The custodians of Seann Vell, led by Mairead nic Amhlaidh, close the only quay their river town has for the coal traffic that feeds it, and let no barge tie up there through a whole season, though the closing costs the town every fee that quay has ever earned it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The flux reaches Seann Vell

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A' Chompanaidh fines Seann Vell for the shut landing

told_in.book: Of the Tithe and the Flux
told_in.section: IV. Of the Barges to Seann Vell

events.title: A' Chompanaidh fines Seann Vell for the shut landing
events.body: A letter from the pay office fines Seann Vell for the season's lost landing fees and says nothing of the flux the closing was meant to check. Mairead nic Amhlaidh reads it to the town council on the landing steps within sight of that season's graves, and the town pays it from the same purse that buried its dead.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The flux reaches Seann Vell

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Seann Vell shuts its landing

told_in.book: Of the Tithe and the Flux
told_in.section: IV. Of the Barges to Seann Vell

events.title: Walter Crane Commissioner
events.body: Arthur Lisle dies at the Residency of a fever of the heart. Walter Crane, who had been the Company's chief agent at the pits, is made Commissioner after him, the first to hold both offices one after the other.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Arthur Lisle dies at Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir

events.title: Arthur Lisle dies at Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir
events.body: Arthur Lisle dies at Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir above Ros dhomhain of a fever that settles in his chest and then his heart, a fortnight dying by inches and signing papers to the last. He is one and sixty, Àrd-mhaor twenty years, remembered by the custodians for a raised voice never once heard at their council table, though not forgiven the schedule.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Walter Crane Commissioner

told_in.book: Of the Tithe and the Flux
told_in.section: V. Of the Seal Passed On

events.title: The pay office at Ceann mhin
events.body: Crane moves the Company's pay office for the southern workings to Ceann mhin, and makes the crews walk there to be paid, a day each way, in place of sending the paymaster to them. The crews are not paid for the walk.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Uisdean Ruadh's first walk to Ceann mhin

events.title: Uisdean Ruadh's first walk to Ceann mhin
events.body: Uisdean Ruadh, a hewer of Muileann chrom, walks with forty of his gang before light on a morning of frost to stand in the pay line at Ceann mhin till near dusk, and walks home again in the dark. He keeps the cost of it afterward on a notched stick, kept still by his family three generations on.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The pay office at Ceann mhin

told_in.book: Of the Tithe and the Flux
told_in.section: VI. Of the Day's Walk to Ceann mhin

events.title: Dòmhnall mac Raghnaill Maor
events.body: Raghnall Maor dies, and the Company gives his staff to his son Dòmhnall. The overseer's office, which the custodians had hoped would die with the man, becomes a family's inheritance.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Raghnall Maor buried beside the eleven

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Raghnall Maor dies at Muileann chrom

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A' Chompanaidh gives Dòmhnall his father's staff

events.title: Raghnall Maor buried beside the eleven
events.body: Raghnall Maor is buried on the hill above Muileann chrom beside the eleven of his first gallery, in thin rain, with both shifts of the pit standing at the grave together, a thing not done for any death there before. Anne Colby stands at the grave's edge with her roll and adds, that evening, a line naming his office, the only such line the roll holds.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Dòmhnall mac Raghnaill Maor

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Raghnall Maor dies at Muileann chrom

told_in.book: Of the Tithe and the Flux
told_in.section: VII. Of Raghnall's Burying

events.title: Raghnall Maor dies at Muileann chrom
events.body: Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill, called Raghnall Maor, dies at two and seventy in the slate-roofed house A' Chompanaidh built him above the pit he first walked as a guide. Anne Colby, sent for by his son, sits with him two nights before the end; he asks her once whether she writes her dead down by name and tells her it is a good thing to keep doing.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Dòmhnall mac Raghnaill Maor

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Raghnall Maor buried beside the eleven

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A' Chompanaidh gives Dòmhnall his father's staff

told_in.book: Of the Tithe and the Flux
told_in.section: VII. Of Raghnall's Burying

events.title: A' Chompanaidh gives Dòmhnall his father's staff
events.body: Within the week of the burying a clerk from Ceann mhin brings Dòmhnall mac Raghnaill the office, the slate roof and the crews together as one paper needing only his mark. The custodians of Muileann chrom, who had hoped the office might die with Raghnall, see it pass from father to son as if it had always been meant to.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Dòmhnall mac Raghnaill Maor

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Raghnall Maor dies at Muileann chrom

told_in.book: Of the Tithe and the Flux
told_in.section: VII. Of Raghnall's Burying

events.title: Edwin Lowe sent to Muileann bheag
events.body: Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise sends the cleric Edwin Lowe up from Ros dhomhain to look into a complaint laid by the keepers of the new Taigh-solais Muileann bheag. He rides three days by mule-track and a fourth along the open coast, and finds the beacon burning coal, the first of the island's lights to do so.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Taigh-solais Muileann bheag lit

told_in.book: Of Lowe's Spade
told_in.section: I. Of the Coloured Flame at Muileann bheag

events.title: Taigh-solais Muileann bheag lit
events.body: The fourth beacon is lit on the northern shore at Muileann bheag, the first to burn coal and not oil. Its keepers say the flame throws a colour on the water that no oil lamp ever did.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Edwin Lowe sent to Muileann bheag

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ailig mac Griogair shows Lowe the coloured water

events.title: Ailig mac Griogair shows Lowe the coloured water
events.body: The keeper Ailig mac Griogair takes Lowe up the beacon stair and points out a green colour he says lies on the water beneath the flame, further than the beam itself should carry. Lowe looks a long while and sees only firelight on the swell, and writes that he cannot see what the keeper sees.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Taigh-solais Muileann bheag lit

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The fishermen of Muileann bheag

told_in.book: Of Lowe's Spade
told_in.section: I. Of the Coloured Flame at Muileann bheag

events.title: The fishermen of Muileann bheag
events.body: The fishermen of Muileann bheag complain that the colour the coal flame casts on the water drives the herring off. The keepers do not change the lamp. Within a season the herring come back, and the complaint is withdrawn in a letter the Company keeps.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Ailig mac Griogair shows Lowe the coloured water

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The keeper's son answers Lowe on the point

events.title: The keeper's son answers Lowe on the point
events.body: Ailig's young son stands the watch beside Lowe on two further nights and tells him the colour is not a thing looked for but a thing seen, as rain is felt before it falls. Lowe records the boy's answer as the most honest, and the least useful, given him in eleven years on the island.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The fishermen of Muileann bheag

told_in.book: Of Lowe's Spade
told_in.section: I. Of the Coloured Flame at Muileann bheag

events.title: The dig at Làrach an Teampaill
events.body: The Mission cleric Edwin Lowe digs for a season at Làrach an Teampaill with Company labourers, seeking proof of an older faith on the island. He finds cut stone, burnt bone and marks he cannot read, and writes that the ruin's builders "were not the present race." The custodians agree, and add nothing.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Griogal Odhar on Mòd and the older ground

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The shepherds of Àth mhòr turn their flocks off the mound

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Tormod Ruadh sets down his spade

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Four custodians view the pit at Làrach an Teampaill

events.title: Griogal Odhar on Mòd and the older ground
events.body: Asked whether any order of the island's faiths claims the ruin, Griogal Odhar tells Lowe that Mòd himself is said not to claim ground older than the vein, for a god who eats the hill can only eat what grew in the hill's own time. No order has ever asked for the ground, and none has been refused it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The dig at Làrach an Teampaill

told_in.book: Of Lowe's Spade
told_in.section: II. Of the Dig at Làrach an Teampaill

events.title: The shepherds of Àth mhòr turn their flocks off the mound
events.body: Before the digging begins the shepherds of Àth mhòr move their flocks off the mound of Làrach an Teampaill, which they have grazed every other season, saying only that it is the custom to keep beasts from a grave while the grave stands open.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The dig at Làrach an Teampaill

told_in.book: Of Lowe's Spade
told_in.section: II. Of the Dig at Làrach an Teampaill

events.title: Tormod Ruadh sets down his spade
events.body: The eldest of Lowe's labourers, Tormod Ruadh, refuses to dig further once burnt bone is found beside the altar stone, saying he will cut coal for his wage but not dig a man from his own grave for a stranger's paper. The rest of the crew stop with him.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The dig at Làrach an Teampaill

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Four custodians view the pit at Làrach an Teampaill

told_in.book: Of Lowe's Spade
told_in.section: II. Of the Dig at Làrach an Teampaill

events.title: Four custodians view the pit at Làrach an Teampaill
events.body: Custodians of Doire ghlas, Doire fhiadhaich and Àth mhòr walk out together to the opened pit, judge that the stone, the bone and the flints beside it are of no people or craft they know, and have Lowe cover the pit again with the word said over any grave whose kin cannot be found.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The dig at Làrach an Teampaill

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Tormod Ruadh sets down his spade

told_in.book: Of Lowe's Spade
told_in.section: II. Of the Dig at Làrach an Teampaill

events.title: Martha Gale reads the partnership at Muileann chiar
events.body: Martha Gale brings A' Chompanaidh's offer of partnership to Comann an Airgid hall at Muileann chiar. A clerk reads it in the humans' tongue and a guild boy puts it into Dia-thìris sentence by sentence, at Ùna nic Choinnich's insistence, so that no hand voting on it can say it did not understand.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The silver guild refuses again

told_in.book: Of Lowe's Spade
told_in.section: V. Of the Answer of Comann an Airgid

events.title: The pillar at Cnoc chiar
events.body: Edwin Lowe copies the writing on the pillar near Cnoc chiar and sets it beside Wren's copy of the obelisk at Cnoc bheag. He judges that the two scripts are not the same, and that neither is of the Dia-thìrich. His notes stop there.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Lowe sets Colbh Cnoc chiar beside Wren's copy of Carragh Cnoc bheag

events.title: Lowe sets Colbh Cnoc chiar beside Wren's copy of Carragh Cnoc bheag
events.body: Lowe lays his rubbing of Colbh Cnoc chiar beside Samuel Wren's old copy of Carragh Cnoc bheag and judges the two hands are not the same, though something in the shapes of both puts him in mind of a single idea, as two strangers' faces can share an expression without sharing a feature.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The pillar at Cnoc chiar

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The obelisk at Cnoc bheag copied

told_in.book: Of Lowe's Spade
told_in.section: III. Of the Pillar and the Column

events.title: Voss stays behind at Baile Mòr dhìreach
events.body: When his glazing of A' Chompanaidh contract ends, Peter Voss does not take passage home, telling the muster clerk only that he has found white sand below Baile Mòr dhìreach the like of which he never found in three counties of an Tìr Thall, and means to see what it will make in a furnace.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The glass-house at Baile Mòr dhìreach

told_in.book: Of Lowe's Spade
told_in.section: IV. Of Voss's Glass-House

events.title: The column at Cnoc ghorm
events.body: Lowe's last copy is of the column near Cnoc ghorm, and beside it he writes that its marks are like the pillar's, but not near enough to help. He leaves Dia-thìr the next year and takes his notebooks with him.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Lowe sails for home

events.title: The glass-house at Baile Mòr dhìreach
events.body: Peter Voss, a glazier left behind when his Company contract ended, builds a glass-house at Baile Mòr dhìreach and melts the white sand of Cuan ruadh with charcoal from the hills. It is the first glass made on Dia-thìr. Within a generation his Dia-thìrich apprentices carry the craft to the towns of the capital shore.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Voss stays behind at Baile Mòr dhìreach

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Cairistìona nic Griogair sees the first pane

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first three firings give only slag

events.title: Cairistìona nic Griogair sees the first pane
events.body: Voss's fourth firing gives a pale green pane clear enough to see a gull through. His apprentice Cairistìona nic Griogair, who carried sand for him all that summer, laughs at the sight of it, the first laugh heard in the glass-house yard since the furnace was raised.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The glass-house at Baile Mòr dhìreach

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first three firings give only slag

told_in.book: Of Lowe's Spade
told_in.section: IV. Of Voss's Glass-House

events.title: The first three firings give only slag
events.body: Voss's first three firings of white sand and charcoal give only a black glassy slag, which the town's children carry off for luck and the custodians' clerk records as Voss's first stones, being none. Voss breaks each batch himself and changes the fire and the sand before trying again.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The glass-house at Baile Mòr dhìreach

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Cairistìona nic Griogair sees the first pane

told_in.book: Of Lowe's Spade
told_in.section: IV. Of Voss's Glass-House

events.title: The silver guild refuses again
events.body: Martha Gale, an agent of the Company, offers the silver guild of Muileann chiar a partnership, on terms the guild's ledger calls generous. Ùna nic Choinnich, now very old, has the offer read aloud twice in the guild hall, and it is refused by show of hands.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Martha Gale reads the partnership at Muileann chiar

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ùna nic Choinnich questions A' Chompanaidh's beam

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The guild's hands refuse the partnership

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ùna nic Choinnich dies at Muileann chiar

events.title: Lowe sails for home
events.body: Edwin Lowe takes ship at Ros dhomhain the year after copying Calbh Cnoc ghorm, his notebooks sealed under his berth. No answer is ever recorded as coming back over the sea to the stone he copied or the bone he uncovered and covered again.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The column at Cnoc ghorm

told_in.book: Of Lowe's Spade
told_in.section: III. Of the Pillar and the Column

events.title: Ùna nic Choinnich questions A' Chompanaidh's beam
events.body: Ùna nic Choinnich, some eighty winters old, has the paragraph on A' Chompanaidh's weighing-beam read a third time and asks twice what the weight would be measured against, unsatisfied with the clerk's answers both times, before putting the offer to the guild's hands.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The silver guild refuses again

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The guild's hands refuse the partnership

told_in.book: Of Lowe's Spade
told_in.section: V. Of the Answer of Comann an Airgid

events.title: The guild's hands refuse the partnership
events.body: The guild hall at Muileann chiar refuses A' Chompanaidh's partnership by every hand but one, an old silversmith too deaf that year to have followed the second reading. Martha Gale takes the count without argument and thanks the hall in a careful, correct Dia-thìris never heard from her again.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The silver guild refuses again

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Ùna nic Choinnich questions A' Chompanaidh's beam

told_in.book: Of Lowe's Spade
told_in.section: V. Of the Answer of Comann an Airgid

events.title: The camp at Achadh dhomhain
events.body: A new camp is opened at Achadh dhomhain for the deep galleries under the hill, and within a few seasons it is the most crowded place in the district. Its houses are built of spoil.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Beitris Bhàn takes up the laying-out at Achadh dhomhain

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The nine of the first winter

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Cormag mac Ailein raises the first house of spoil

events.title: Beitris Bhàn takes up the laying-out at Achadh dhomhain
events.body: Beitris Bhàn walks up from Àth ìseal in the camp's first winter with her mother's knife and takes the end room of a house of spoil, next the well, to lay out the camp's dead. Within the week the first bodies are brought to her table.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The camp at Achadh dhomhain

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The nine of the first winter

told_in.book: Of the Smoke in the Gallery
told_in.section: I. Of the First Winter of Achadh dhomhain

events.title: The nine of the first winter
events.body: Achadh dhomhain buries nine in its first winter: two hewers dead of the damp, a child crushed under a runaway cart of spoil, and six of the camp cough. Beitris Bhàn cuts the turf for each grave herself, the camp having no man yet spared from the pit for the work.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The camp at Achadh dhomhain

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Beitris Bhàn takes up the laying-out at Achadh dhomhain

told_in.book: Of the Smoke in the Gallery
told_in.section: I. Of the First Winter of Achadh dhomhain

events.title: Cloth for the camps at Dùn chiar
events.body: The weavers of Dùn chiar take a Company contract for canvas for the camp tents and sacks for the coal, and the town thrives on it. Its custodians note that never before had the town made anything for a use it did not approve.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Dùn chiar votes to weave for the camps

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Cormag mac Ailein raises the first house of spoil

events.title: Dùn chiar votes to weave for the camps
events.body: The town council of Dùn chiar votes twenty-six to nine to take a contract of A' Chompanaidh for camp canvas, against the eldest weaver Ealasaid Bhuidhe, who signs the roll of dissent and then weaves canvas with the rest once the custodian has ruled.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Cloth for the camps at Dùn chiar

told_in.book: Of Lowe's Spade
told_in.section: VI. Of the Camp at Achadh dhomhain and the Cloth of Dùn chiar

events.title: Cormag mac Ailein raises the first house of spoil
events.body: The hewer Cormag mac Ailein builds the first house of Achadh dhomhain's camp from stacked spoil chinked with clay and roofs it with Dùn chiar's first bolts of canvas before the frost, tarring the seams himself, his household under it before the year's shortest day.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The camp at Achadh dhomhain

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Cloth for the camps at Dùn chiar

told_in.book: Of Lowe's Spade
told_in.section: VI. Of the Camp at Achadh dhomhain and the Cloth of Dùn chiar

events.title: The first of the undying generation
events.body: A girl is born in the mining camps who takes more raw coal into her body over her life than any Dia-thìreach in living memory, and she does not age as the folk about her age. Her name is Aisling.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The wife's telling, over a body at Beitris Bhàn's table

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The washing-women name nighean an rìgh

events.title: The coach to the camps
events.body: The Company puts a coach on the road between the quay at Ros dhomhain and the camps at Muileann chrom, twice a week each way, changing horses at the old waypoint houses. Clerks and overseers ride in it. The crews walk.

events.title: The coal weighed at the quay
events.body: The Company sets up a great steelyard at the Ros dhomhain quay, and thenceforth the island's yield is known by the ton and the hundredweight. The custodians' old count, kept in seasons of labour, is no longer entered in the roll.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The steelyard changes the count

events.title: The steelyard changes the count
events.body: After A' Chompanaidh's great steelyard is hung at Ros dhomhain, the custodians' old count of the yield, kept in baskets and seasons of a crew's labour, is entered less and less in the rolls, until it is not entered at all. Ùna nic Choinnich says the island has let the wrong hill be written down.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The coal weighed at the quay

told_in.book: Of the Smoke in the Gallery
told_in.section: II. Of the Coach and the Steelyard

events.title: Ros dhìreach the second coal port
events.body: The Company opens a second coal stage at Ros dhìreach on the southern coast for the workings south of the hills. Its first cargo is lost in a squall off the harbour mouth, and the fishermen moved to make room for the stage will not go out after it.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The wreck off Ros dhìreach

events.title: The wreck off Ros dhìreach
events.body: Ros dhìreach's first cargo goes down in a squall within a mile of the new coal stage, taking the boat and two of the crew who had gone out to trim her load. The fishermen whose grounds were given over for the stage will not put out past the wreck for a season after.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Ros dhìreach the second coal port

told_in.book: Of the Smoke in the Gallery
told_in.section: II. Of the Coach and the Steelyard

events.title: Ùna nic Choinnich dies at Muileann chiar
events.body: Ùna nic Choinnich dies in her own bed at Muileann chiar, eighty-five years old, having led Comann an Airgid since before Fiabhras nan Coigreach and twice put A' Chompanaidh's offers to a show of hands and twice seen them refused. Achadh dhomhain, which never saw her, mourns her by the sayings that came down the road ahead of the coach.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The silver guild refuses again

told_in.book: Of the Smoke in the Gallery
told_in.section: V. Of Ùna nic Choinnich and the Shrines

events.title: The nameless change
