events.body: What is befalling the child born two years before has as yet no name in any tongue spoken on the island. Decades pass before anyone tries to make one.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The women's rule of silence

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The wash-house women first mark the child's stillness

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The wife's telling, over a body at Beitris Bhàn's table

events.title: The women's rule of silence
events.body: Beitris Bhàn tells the women who sat the night of the telling that a charge laid on a man by a spirit is not theirs to spend on the camp's talk, whatever they make of the child in their own kitchens. No meeting is called and no vote taken, but the rule holds among them for years.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The nameless change

told_in.book: Of the Smoke in the Gallery
told_in.section: IV. Of the Child the Rolls Gave Three Things

events.title: The wash-house women first mark the child's stillness
events.body: Season on season the women who handle the camp's dying notice, before anyone else in Achadh dhomhain, that Aisling is not changing as a growing child should, and keep what they notice among themselves.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The nameless change

told_in.book: Of the Smoke in the Gallery
told_in.section: IV. Of the Child the Rolls Gave Three Things

events.title: The first steamer
events.body: The first ship driven by an engine comes into Ros dhomhain, a Company paddle-steamer out of an Tìr Thall. The fishermen row out to look at a ship going against the wind with no sail set. Within a generation the Company's coal goes out in nothing else.

events.title: The wife's telling, over a body at Beitris Bhàn's table
events.body: At a laying-out in the camp's fourth winter, Donnchadh mac Thormoid's wife tells the sitting women, for the first time outside her own house, what her husband met in the deep gallery and what it charged him to keep, and what passed the night their daughter was born. She says the words are his and she will change none of them.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first of the undying generation

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The nameless change

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Beitris Bhàn's first climb to Cill ghlas

told_in.book: Of the Smoke in the Gallery
told_in.section: III. Of What the Wife Told the Women

events.title: The shrine at Cill dhìreach
events.body: At Cill dhìreach, a village at the edge of the workings, the custodians keep a small shrine where the pit crews leave the first piece of coal from each new gallery. The Company suffers the custom, for it costs a stone a gallery.

events.title: The keepers of Cill ghlas
events.body: The custodians of the shrine at Cill ghlas, in the hills among the workings, keep the old rites at the mouth of the oldest cutting while the Company's pits deepen about them. It is the last shrine in the district that the pit crews still visit on the old feast days.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Beitris Bhàn's first climb to Cill ghlas

events.title: Beitris Bhàn's first climb to Cill ghlas
events.body: Beitris Bhàn climbs the hill path to Cill ghlas for the first time at Lùnastal and sets a single piece of coal by the flame at the mouth of the oldest cutting, more from the habit of a hard winter's laying-out than from any settled custom of her own people. She says nothing to the custodian, and the custodian says nothing to her.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The keepers of Cill ghlas

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The wife's telling, over a body at Beitris Bhàn's table

told_in.book: Of the Smoke in the Gallery
told_in.section: V. Of Ùna nic Choinnich and the Shrines

events.title: A' Phlàigh Uaine
events.body: The Green Death goes through the mining camps. The coal dust is blamed, though no study of it is ever finished. Twenty-six settlements have cases.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first grave dug in An Acair Uaine

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Anne Colby comes to Beitris Bhàn's door

events.title: The first cases at Achadh dhomhain
events.body: The Green Death is first marked at Achadh dhomhain: a greenish pallor, then a cough that brings up dark dust, then weakness. The camp buries forty in the first month, in a field beyond the spoil-heaps still called the green acre.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first grave dug in An Acair Uaine

events.title: The first grave dug in An Acair Uaine
events.body: Beitris Bhàn helps dig the first grave in the stony field beyond Achadh dhomhain's spoil-heaps, on a day the camp's own grave-diggers are themselves too sick to work. Within weeks the whole camp is calling the field an Acair Uaine without anyone having named it so on purpose.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A' Phlàigh Uaine

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first cases at Achadh dhomhain

told_in.book: Of A' Phlàigh Uaine
told_in.section: I. Of the Green Acre

events.title: Sìne Ruadh orders the huts of Àth ghlas burned
events.body: The custodian of Àth ghlas, Sìne Ruadh, orders every hut where a death has occurred burned to the ground with its bedding before the next nightfall, over A' Chompanaidh's agent's written protest at the loss of its property. She burns nine huts before the summer ends.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Àth ghlas burns its huts

told_in.book: Of A' Phlàigh Uaine
told_in.section: II. Of the Blank Line

events.title: The clerk leaves a line blank after the twenty-sixth settlement
events.body: The custodian's clerk who keeps the roll of settlements with cases of A' Phlàigh Uaine leaves a blank line after the twenty-sixth name. It is still blank when a different hand takes up the roll the following spring, and no twenty-seventh name is ever entered in it.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Twenty-six settlements

told_in.book: Of A' Phlàigh Uaine
told_in.section: II. Of the Blank Line

events.title: Twenty-six settlements
events.body: The sickness spreads along the coal roads from the camps at Muileann chrom, Àth ìseal and Cnoc fhiadhaich, and falls hardest on Ros dhìreach, Ceann òg, Inis ìseal, Baile dhomhain, Achadh fhada, Cnoc bheag, Muileann uaine, Cuan àrsaidh and Inis bhàn. The custodians' roll lists the twenty-six settlements that had cases, and leaves a blank line after the last, as though waiting for another.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The clerk leaves a line blank after the twenty-sixth settlement

events.title: The Green Death at Baile chrom
events.body: The Green Death comes to Baile chrom in the hills, not the town of that name in the north-west. The scribes keep the two apart with care, for in later tellings of the island's hungers they are confused.

events.title: Àth ghlas burns its huts
events.body: At Àth ghlas the custodians order every hut where a death has been burned with its bedding. The Company protests the loss of its property. The custodians note that the sickness stops sooner at Àth ghlas than anywhere else.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Sìne Ruadh orders the huts of Àth ghlas burned

events.title: The dead of Cnoc naomh
events.body: At Cnoc naomh the dead of the Green Death are laid in the burial ground of the town's old shrine until it is full, and then in a field outside. The field is never ploughed again.

events.title: Walter Crane walks the sick-rows at Achadh dhomhain
events.body: Àrd-mhaor Crane walks the worst of the sickness's second summer at Achadh dhomhain and does not walk faster past the bad huts than the ordinary ones, a thing the custodians and Beitris Bhàn both note and remember afterward in his favour.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Walter Crane dies of the Green Death

told_in.book: Of A' Phlàigh Uaine
told_in.section: IV. Of the Seal and the Letter-Book

events.title: Beitris Bhàn nails a feather over her own door
events.body: After laying out the fortieth body of the season, Beitris Bhàn nails a hawk's feather above her own door at Achadh dhomhain. The overseer's boy finds it and reports his father, and she pays the week's pay it costs her and nails up another within the month.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The camps turn to the hawk

told_in.book: Of A' Phlàigh Uaine
told_in.section: V. Of the Feathers Over the Door

events.title: Nathaniel Bright opens his table of weighings
events.body: At Muileann chrom, Nathaniel Bright begins keeping a ruled black-bound book of the lungs he weighs from A' Phlàigh Uaine's dead, with the custodians' leave and a custodian standing by at each opening. Anne Colby brings her own sick-house tally to set beside it that winter.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Doctor Bright's study

told_in.book: Of A' Phlàigh Uaine
told_in.section: III. Of Doctor Bright's Table

events.title: Doctor Bright's study
events.body: Nathaniel Bright, physician to the Administration, begins to study the sickness at Muileann chrom, weighing the dust in the lungs of the dead. In the second season of the work he falls ill, and his notebooks break off in the middle of a table.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Nathaniel Bright opens his table of weighings

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Bright's table breaks off mid-row

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Nathaniel Bright dies at Muileann chrom

events.title: Walter Crane dies of the Green Death
events.body: Commissioner Crane, who had walked the camps in the worst of the sickness, dies of it at the Residency. Martha Gale, the Company's agent at Ros dhomhain, holds his seal for the months until another comes.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Walter Crane walks the sick-rows at Achadh dhomhain

events.title: Anne Colby comes to Beitris Bhàn's door
events.body: Anne Colby, unsent by Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise and unasked by any custodian, comes to Achadh dhomhain to learn from the layer-out Beitris Bhàn what her own hands have taught her of A' Phlàigh Uaine. The two begin washing the camp's dead together, a custom the camp comes to call An Dithis a Nigh Còmhla.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A' Phlàigh Uaine

told_in.book: Of A' Phlàigh Uaine
told_in.section: VI. Of the Washing

events.title: Bright's table breaks off mid-row
events.body: Nathaniel Bright falls ill in the third season of his study. His last entry stops after the weight of a dead man's lung, with the column for the dust in it left empty and the pen, by the mark it leaves, set down and never taken up again.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Doctor Bright's study

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Nathaniel Bright dies at Muileann chrom

told_in.book: Of A' Phlàigh Uaine
told_in.section: III. Of Doctor Bright's Table

events.title: George Tolley Commissioner
events.body: George Tolley comes from an Tìr Thall with orders that the yield must not fall for the sickness. He does not visit the camps. His letter-book blames the dust, the Dia-thìrich custom of sleeping near the fire, and the custodians' shrines, in that order.

events.title: Quarantine at Caol mhin
events.body: Tolley sets a quarantine station at Caol mhin on the northern coast for ships from an Tìr Thall, and holds them offshore until their crews are looked over. It is the first order of his rule the Dia-thìrich approve, and they say so.

events.title: The camps turn to the hawk
events.body: The hawk-priests still barred from the camps, the crews carry their sermons in themselves. The overseers' reports of these years list hawk-feathers nailed above hut doors as a matter for punishment.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Beitris Bhàn nails a feather over her own door

events.title: Nathaniel Bright dies at Muileann chrom
events.body: Nathaniel Bright dies at Muileann chrom of the same sickness he had spent three seasons weighing in other men's lungs, and is buried by Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise apart from An Acair Uaine and the field at Cnoc naomh. His book is filed at Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir and never taken up by any physician after him.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Doctor Bright's study

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Bright's table breaks off mid-row

told_in.book: Of A' Phlàigh Uaine
told_in.section: III. Of Doctor Bright's Table

events.title: Anne Colby's sick-houses
events.body: Anne Colby opens sick-houses at Àth ìseal and Achadh dhomhain and nurses there until the sickness ebbs. She is the only human the camp folk name in their own accounts of the plague, and they name her kindly.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The shrine women keep An Acair Uaine through the stoppage

events.title: Catrìona's request to Silas Crewe
events.body: Catrìona nic Eachainn, crew-leader of the seventh shift at Baile thais, asks the agent Silas Crewe to close the third and fourth galleries, where A' Phlàigh Uaine struck worst, until the surgeon rules on the dust. Crewe answers that the yield must not fall on a physician's guess, and says only that he will write it up.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first strike

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The strike at Baile thais

told_in.book: Of Stad-oibre Baile thais
told_in.section: II. Of the Agent's Answer

events.title: Sìneag searches the old rolls for a law of rest
events.body: Asked by Catrìona nic Eachainn whether any old law binds a hill's rest, the custodian Sìneag of Baile thais searches her rolls and finds none: Lagh an Loscaidh Bhig governs the coal burned, not the coal cut, and no custodian before this age had needed to write a law about men sickening below ground.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first strike

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Raghnall Breac stands his first day among the strikers

told_in.book: Of Stad-oibre Baile thais
told_in.section: III. Of the Coal-Tub

events.title: The huts of Cnoc gharbh
events.body: After the sickness the people of Cnoc gharbh, who had worked the southern galleries, leave their camp huts and go back to the old village on the hill. The next year the Company builds the huts again and brings in crews from the west.

events.title: The first strike
events.body: A whole mining settlement stops work for eleven days over conditions worsened by the plague two years before. The strike ends when the food, which the humans' Administration holds, runs out.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Catrìona's request to Silas Crewe

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Sìneag searches the old rolls for a law of rest

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Raghnall Breac stands his first day among the strikers

events.title: Raghnall Breac stands his first day among the strikers
events.body: A hewer's boy of seven, too young that year to be paid a man's wage, sets down his water-pail at the pit-mouth of Baile thais on the morning Catrìona nic Eachainn calls the halt, and stays through the yard's long quiet with the shift twice his age.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first strike

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The strike at Baile thais

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Sìneag searches the old rolls for a law of rest

told_in.book: Of Stad-oibre Baile thais
told_in.section: III. Of the Coal-Tub

events.title: The shrine women keep An Acair Uaine through the stoppage
events.body: Through the eleven days no coal left Baile thais, the shrine women go on leaving dishes of meal on the mounds of An Acair Uaine where A' Phlàigh Uaine's dead were laid, finding a little to spare each day though A' Chompanaidh's store stood barer by the day beside them.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Anne Colby's sick-houses

told_in.book: Of Stad-oibre Baile thais
told_in.section: V. Of the Twelfth Morning

events.title: Beathag Ruadh asks Catrìona to end the stand
events.body: On the tenth night of the stoppage, her bread gone and five children to feed, Beathag Ruadh asks Catrìona nic Eachainn, plainly and without reproach, whether the crews should go back below rather than starve for galleries that would go on being worked regardless. Catrìona has no answer, and sits with her by the fire till morning.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The strike at Baile thais

told_in.book: Of Stad-oibre Baile thais
told_in.section: IV. Of the Eleven Days

events.title: The strike at Baile thais
events.body: The settlement was Baile thais, below Cill ghlas, and the crew-leader Catrìona nic Eachainn called the halt after the Company would not close the galleries where the Green Death had been worst. For eleven days no coal left the town. On the twelfth the Company's store, the only store, was empty.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Catrìona's request to Silas Crewe

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Raghnall Breac stands his first day among the strikers

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Beathag Ruadh asks Catrìona to end the stand

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Catrìona is given the surface work

events.title: The Company's granary
events.body: After the strike the Company builds a granary of its own at Muileann chrom and forbids the camps to keep grain beyond a week's ration. The overseers enforce the order, and Dòmhnall mac Raghnaill Maor signs it.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Sìneag's rolls note a granary built against a stoppage

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Dòmhnall Maor signs the granary order

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The overseers search the huts of Baile thais for hidden meal

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Dòmhnall Maor dies at Muileann chrom

events.title: Sìneag's rolls note a granary built against a stoppage
events.body: The custodian Sìneag writes in her rolls that she has never before read of a granary raised to answer a stoppage rather than a harvest, and sets the words down as they stand, without further comment, for whoever should read the roll after her.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Company's granary

told_in.book: Of Stad-oibre Baile thais
told_in.section: III. Of the Coal-Tub

events.title: Dòmhnall Maor signs the granary order
events.body: Within the month of the strike's end, Dòmhnall mac Raghnaill Maor, Steward at Muileann chrom, sets his mark to the order that forbids any camp household to keep more grain than a week's ration, the rest to be held under lock in A' Chompanaidh's new granary and drawn against a crew-leader's tally.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Company's granary

told_in.book: Of Stad-oibre Baile thais
told_in.section: VI. Of the Granary

events.title: The overseers search the huts of Baile thais for hidden meal
events.body: Enforcing the granary order with more zeal than it asks, the overseers at Baile thais search huts for grain kept back from the week's ration, and twice that autumn fine a household a day's wage for flour found under a bed, though in both cases the flour had come up from Ros gharbh by night and never passed A' Chompanaidh's scales.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Company's granary

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Fish smuggled from Ros gharbh

told_in.book: Of Stad-oibre Baile thais
told_in.section: VI. Of the Granary

events.title: Catrìona is given the surface work
events.body: Before the winter after the stoppage is out, the seventh shift is given to a crew-leader loyal to Silas Crewe, and Catrìona nic Eachainn is set to sorting slate at the surface at half a hewer's pay, work she keeps eleven months before the sheds are said to have more hands than they need.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The strike at Baile thais

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Catrìona is refused work at Cnoc fhiadhaich and Àth ìseal

told_in.book: Of Stad-oibre Baile thais
told_in.section: VII. Of the Road East

events.title: Fish smuggled from Ros gharbh
events.body: The fishermen of Ros gharbh carry salt fish up to the camps by night, past the Company's granary rule. The custodians' roll calls it the only trade of that decade that ran the right way.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The overseers search the huts of Baile thais for hidden meal

events.title: Catrìona is refused work at Cnoc fhiadhaich and Àth ìseal
events.body: Turned off the sorting-sheds at Baile thais, Catrìona nic Eachainn walks first to Cnoc fhiadhaich and then to the timber camp beyond Àth ìseal asking for work, and is turned away at each gate before she has said her name twice, the agents already knowing her by sight.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Catrìona goes to the silver town

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Catrìona is given the surface work

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Catrìona walks east over the hills to Muileann chiar

told_in.book: Of Stad-oibre Baile thais
told_in.section: VII. Of the Road East

events.title: Catrìona walks east over the hills to Muileann chiar
events.body: With her savings spent and refused work at every pit of A' Chompanaidh, Catrìona nic Eachainn takes what she owns and walks east from Baile thais over the hills to Muileann chiar, three days on foot, the black spoil of the coal country giving way at last to the grey of the silver town.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Catrìona goes to the silver town

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Catrìona is refused work at Cnoc fhiadhaich and Àth ìseal

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Comann an Airgid's hands vote to take Catrìona on

told_in.book: Of Stad-oibre Baile thais
told_in.section: VII. Of the Road East

events.title: Catrìona goes to the silver town
events.body: Turned out of Baile thais and refused work at every Company pit, Catrìona nic Eachainn goes east to Muileann chiar, and the silver guild takes her on as a refiner. The Company asks that she be sent back. The guild's answer was filed and has not survived.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Catrìona is refused work at Cnoc fhiadhaich and Àth ìseal

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Catrìona walks east over the hills to Muileann chiar

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Comann an Airgid's hands vote to take Catrìona on

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A' Chompanaidh writes to Muileann chiar for Catrìona's return

events.title: Comann an Airgid's hands vote to take Catrìona on
events.body: Heard without interruption by the master of Comann an Airgid, Catrìona nic Eachainn's account of the stoppage at Baile thais is put to the guild's own hands rather than decided from above, and the hands vote by a wide margin to take her on as a refiner.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Catrìona goes to the silver town

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Catrìona walks east over the hills to Muileann chiar

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A' Chompanaidh writes to Muileann chiar for Catrìona's return

told_in.book: Of Stad-oibre Baile thais
told_in.section: VII. Of the Road East

events.title: A' Chompanaidh writes to Muileann chiar for Catrìona's return
events.body: A' Chompanaidh's counting-house at Ros dhomhain writes to Comann an Airgid asking that Catrìona nic Eachainn, lately of Baile thais, be sent back to answer for the stoppage of two years before. The guild's clerk drafts an answer, read once in the guild hall and sent south; neither letter has survived.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Catrìona goes to the silver town

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Comann an Airgid's hands vote to take Catrìona on

told_in.book: Of Stad-oibre Baile thais
told_in.section: VII. Of the Road East

events.title: The springs at Muileann ruadh
events.body: The Administration builds a new bath-house at the hot springs near Muileann ruadh for its officers mending from fevers. Dia-thìrich who had bathed there for centuries are let in on certain days, and charged a penny.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A penny at the door of Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh

events.title: Three priests will not stand for the blessing
events.body: Three of the younger priests of Òrd Mhacha stand apart at the back of the temple hall rather than take their places for the blessing of the coin. Beathag Ruadh lets it pass unremarked before Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir's clerk, and tells Fearghas mac Mhuirich only that the order answers for the rite done rightly, not for the road a rightly blessed thing afterward walks.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Macha's priests bless the coin

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The order blesses Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir's first coin

told_in.book: Of the Priced Silver and the Blessed Coin
told_in.section: III. Of the Two Horses

events.title: The order blesses Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir's first coin
events.body: At Tolley's asking, Beathag Ruadh and the priests of Òrd Mhacha bless the new-struck coin in the temple at Cathair dhearg, naming both horses of the rite, Dubh Sainglenn and Liath Macha. Fearghas mac Mhuirich stands his place and says the words, though he watches Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir's clerk carry the satchel out and finds he cannot say why the morning troubles him.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Macha's priests bless the coin

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Three priests will not stand for the blessing

told_in.book: Of the Priced Silver and the Blessed Coin
told_in.section: III. Of the Two Horses

events.title: A penny at the door of Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh
events.body: The bath-house Riaghaltas nan Coigreach built at Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh near Muileann ruadh opens to Dia-thìrich two days of the week, at a penny the door, for water the district had bathed in unasked since before any custodian's roll began. Catrìona nic Eachainn pays her penny and finds the water unchanged and only the door made new.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The springs at Muileann ruadh

told_in.book: Of the Priced Silver and the Blessed Coin
told_in.section: I. Of the Silver Priced by Dia-thìreach Hands

events.title: Muileann chiar grows
events.body: The silver town grows beside the coal workings, for the humans want both, and the digging goes faster than the old reverence would ever have allowed.

events.title: Artair mac Iain seated after ten empty years
events.body: Comhairle a' Chùraim, unable to agree a head since Alasdair Liath's death, seats Artair mac Iain of the eastern shires as Ceann a' Chùraim, six-and-fifty years old, in the hall where Tormod mac Ailein once signed Cùmhnant Cathair dhearg. Fearghas mac Mhuirich says the order's blessing over him, both horses named.

told_in.book: Of the Priced Silver and the Blessed Coin
told_in.section: II. Of the Seat Ten Years Empty

events.title: The guild raises a daughter town
events.body: As Muileann chiar's lanes fill past holding, Comann an Airgid raises a second town a mile to the west for its carters and coal-breakers, under the old town's own name. The custodians' rolls thereafter call them the old town and the new, and do not always trouble to say which they mean.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A second Muileann chiar

told_in.book: Of the Priced Silver and the Blessed Coin
told_in.section: I. Of the Silver Priced by Dia-thìreach Hands

events.title: A second Muileann chiar
events.body: The silver trade crowds the old town, and the guild settles its refiners and carters in the coal-breakers' mill town to the west, which is called by the silver town's name from then on. The rolls call them the old town and the new, and do not always say which they mean.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The guild raises a daughter town

events.title: The guild refuses A' Chompanaidh's price a third time
events.body: A' Chompanaidh asks a third time that Comann an Airgid sell at A' Chompanaidh's own price, naming a magistrate at Ros dhomhain who might rule the question. The seven refiners of the guild hall vote it down without one dissenting hand. Catrìona nic Eachainn, in the hall for the vote, counts it the one table on the island where the Dia-thìrich still set a price.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Silver for marks

told_in.book: Of the Priced Silver and the Blessed Coin
told_in.section: I. Of the Silver Priced by Dia-thìreach Hands

events.title: The second cheapening cried at the market crosses
events.body: A crier of Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir reads the second cheapening of the barter table at every market cross without a custodian's council having seen it beforehand. Word of it reaches Muileann chiar three days after Cathair dhearg, carried by a carter who had heard it cried at Baile Mòr fhionn.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The second change of coin

told_in.book: Of the Priced Silver and the Blessed Coin
told_in.section: IV. Of the Fleece and the Boats

events.title: The wool of Baile Mòr fhionn left to the moths
events.body: Finding a fleece worth under the new table what half a fleece was worth before, the weavers of Baile Mòr fhionn stop bringing wool to the humans' market and load it for their own crossing instead. A' Chompanaidh, holding the only deep-water berths on that coast, refuses them the freight, and the wool sits two winters in the warehouses.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Wool marked down at Baile Mòr fhionn

told_in.book: Of the Priced Silver and the Blessed Coin
told_in.section: IV. Of the Fleece and the Boats

events.title: Silver for marks
events.body: The silver guild begins to sell bar silver to the Company for marks, at a price the guild sets. It is the only ware on Dia-thìr in this age priced by Dia-thìrich hands, and the guild's hall fills with human coin.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The guild refuses A' Chompanaidh's price a third time

events.title: Caol fhiadhaich sells eleven of its boats
events.body: Called for the first time in marks rather than in kind, the harbour dues at Caol fhiadhaich cannot be raised any way but by selling boats. Eleven of two-and-twenty go to A' Chompanaidh at its own asking price, and the men who sailed them go into the pits the following season under A' Chompanaidh's contracts.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The boats of Caol fhiadhaich sold

told_in.book: Of the Priced Silver and the Blessed Coin
told_in.section: IV. Of the Fleece and the Boats

events.title: Silversmiths at Muileann bhàn
events.body: Silversmiths settle at Muileann bhàn on the road to the silver town and live by working the guild's bar into ornaments for the humans' market. Theirs is the one Dia-thìreach craft sold in an Tìr Thall under a Dia-thìreach name.

events.title: The washing-women name nighean an rìgh
events.body: At the stream below the camp of Àth ìseal, the eldest of the washing-women first says aloud what the wash-stones had for some seasons only thought: that a girl of the camp who does not age as other children age may be of the old line of kings, and names her nighean an rìgh. Most of the camp says they do not believe it and use the name anyway.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The first of the undying generation

told_in.book: Of the Priced Silver and the Blessed Coin
told_in.section: VI. Of the Name at the Wash-Stones

events.title: Macha's priests bless the coin
events.body: At Tolley's asking the priests of Òrd Mhacha at Cathair dhearg, the order of the capital and the crown, bless the Residency's new coin. The priesthood of Macha teaches that the two horses of her rite, Dubh Sainglenn the black and Liath Macha the grey, each have their due; the dissenting priests say the coin is only one of them.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Three priests will not stand for the blessing

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The order blesses Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir's first coin

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Fearghas refuses to bless the second coin

events.title: Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir notes the order divided
events.body: Word of Fearghas mac Mhuirich's refusal reaches Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir within the month. Tolley, near his own retiring, does not send for him; Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir's letter-book records only that the order of Òrd Mhacha at the capital is divided on a religious nicety, and does not say what the nicety was.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The second change of coin

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Fearghas refuses to bless the second coin

told_in.book: Of the Priced Silver and the Blessed Coin
told_in.section: V. Of the Second Asking

events.title: Fearghas refuses to bless the second coin
events.body: Asked to bless Riaghaltas nan Coigreach's larger second coin as the first was blessed, Fearghas mac Mhuirich, now eldest of the order at Cathair dhearg since Beathag Ruadh's death, tells the order he will not say the words, holding that a rite for a wheel cannot answer a road that turns only one way. None of the order says the words in his place.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The second change of coin

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Macha's priests bless the coin

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir notes the order divided

told_in.book: Of the Priced Silver and the Blessed Coin
told_in.section: V. Of the Second Asking

events.title: The second change of coin
events.body: The barter goods of the Dia-thìrich are marked down against the humans' coin a second time, on terms the humans' Administration alone sets.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The second cheapening cried at the market crosses

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir notes the order divided

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Fearghas refuses to bless the second coin

events.title: Wool marked down at Baile Mòr fhionn
events.body: At Baile Mòr fhionn, where wool had been the measure of every bargain, a fleece is now worth by the Residency's table what a half-fleece was worth before. The town's weavers stop bringing wool to market and send it over the sea on their own account, until the Company refuses them freight.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The wool of Baile Mòr fhionn left to the moths

events.title: The boats of Caol fhiadhaich sold
events.body: The fishing fleet of Caol fhiadhaich, unable to pay the new harbour dues in marks, sells half its boats to the Company. The men who sailed them go into the pits under the next year's contracts.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Caol fhiadhaich sells eleven of its boats

events.title: The dissenters go to Cnoc bheag
events.body: Priests of Macha who refused the blessing leave the capital's temple and settle in the sacred forest at Cnoc bheag. There they keep the older reading of Macha's two horses, and take in custodians who have lost their seats.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Fearghas leaves the capital's temple for Cnoc bheag

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The dissenters' first fire under the oaks

events.title: Iain Maor
events.body: Dòmhnall mac Raghnaill Maor dies, and his son Iain takes the overseer's staff. Iain Maor is the first overseer schooled at the Mission; he keeps his reports in the humans' tongue and his household in Dia-thìris.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Dòmhnall Maor dies at Muileann chrom

events.title: Dòmhnall Maor dies at Muileann chrom
events.body: Dòmhnall mac Raghnaill Maor, overseer of the coal country five-and-twenty years and signer of the granary order that stood against Catrìona nic Eachainn's strike, dies at Muileann chrom in his sixty-seventh year. Word reaches Muileann chiar by carter, and the guild hall names him a hard man gone before a harder trade going on.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Iain Maor

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Company's granary

told_in.book: Of the Priced Silver and the Blessed Coin
told_in.section: VIII. Of the Staff Passed On

events.title: Fearghas leaves the capital's temple for Cnoc bheag
events.body: Fearghas mac Mhuirich walks north with eleven of the order who think as he does, to Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag. Griogair, eldest of those who stay at Cathair dhearg, walks with them as far as the north road and calls it two roads to the one rite rather than a falling-out.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The dissenters go to Cnoc bheag

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The dissenters' first fire under the oaks

told_in.book: Of the Priced Silver and the Blessed Coin
told_in.section: VII. Of the Fire under the Trees

events.title: The dissenters' first fire under the oaks
events.body: Custodians without seats and priests without a temple begin to gather at the forest of Cnoc bheag through the summer, until the grove holds near as many of one kind as the other. On the last evening of the spring Fearghas mac Mhuirich lights Teine a' Chlachair there and says the rite of the two horses whole.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The dissenters go to Cnoc bheag

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Fearghas leaves the capital's temple for Cnoc bheag

told_in.book: Of the Priced Silver and the Blessed Coin
told_in.section: VII. Of the Fire under the Trees

events.title: The Levy
events.body: Tolley issues an ordinance, the Levy, by which every farming village in the west and north must send one in five of its able grown folk to the pits for two years. The villages are paid in marks, at the new rate.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The draft read at Baile chrom

events.title: Levy officers at Caol mhòr
events.body: The Levy's officers take their first tally at Caol mhòr in the north-west, reading the names of the chosen from a list in the humans' tongue. The custodians of the town write the names again in Dia-thìris, that they may know whom to look for.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The wrong son taken at Caol mhòr

events.title: The Levy in the north-west
events.body: The Levy falls hardest on the villages about Baile chrom and the northern concession, which had never sent crews to the pits. The Dia-thìrich of the concession are taken; its human farmers are spared.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The concession's human farmers spared An Togail

events.title: An Togail read at Cnoc thais
events.body: An Togail's officers read their list at Cnoc thais, and the mason Dùghall Clachair hears his own name and his whole crew's called for the pits. Two days into the eastward march they are turned out instead to the headland at Baile chrom, where the fifth and last coast beacon is begun.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Building the last beacon at Baile chrom

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The masons of Cnoc thais

told_in.book: Of An Togail and Fàinne nan Teintean-rabhaidh
told_in.section: IV. Of the Masons of Cnoc thais

events.title: The wrong son taken at Caol mhòr
events.body: A guessed name is matched to the wrong face at Caol mhòr's reading, and a son is marched a day's walk east before the error is found. The right man is fetched in his place; the officers' own tally and the town's roll never afterward agree by one head.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Levy officers at Caol mhòr

told_in.book: Of An Togail and Fàinne nan Teintean-rabhaidh
told_in.section: I. Of the Reading at Caol mhòr

events.title: The concession's human farmers spared An Togail
events.body: In the northern concession An Togail falls on every Dia-thìreach household while Riaghaltas nan Coigreach's own leaseholders pay nothing, the officers' list giving the reason that the concession's tenants answer to Riaghaltas nan Coigreach's leave alone.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Levy in the north-west

told_in.book: Of An Togail and Fàinne nan Teintean-rabhaidh
told_in.section: II. Of the Two Tallies

events.title: Baile ìseal sends its people
events.body: Baile ìseal sends forty-one of its people to the pits under the Levy, and nineteen come back when their term ends. The custodians' roll names the other twenty-two and the camps they were sent to.

events.title: Muileann naomh buys its way out
events.body: The custodians of Muileann naomh pay the Levy's officers in silver to halve the town's tally. The officers take the silver and the whole tally. The complaint is lodged at the Residency and filed.

events.title: The druid school's hall shut
events.body: George Tolley shuts the hall of the druid school at Dùn thais over a lecture on whether the humans' blindness to the coal's colour is a kind of sickness. The masters go on teaching in their own houses, to smaller rooms each year.

events.title: A gale strips the beacon's scaffold
events.body: A two-day gale out of the north-west tears the scaffolding from the third course of the rising tower at Baile chrom. Dùghall Clachair climbs the bare walls alone in the wind to judge whether the stone has shifted; it has not.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Building the last beacon at Baile chrom

told_in.book: Of An Togail and Fàinne nan Teintean-rabhaidh
told_in.section: IV. Of the Masons of Cnoc thais

events.title: The last disputation at Doire chiar
events.body: At Doire chiar, a village of the druid schools north of the eastern workings, the masters hold the last open disputation of the school on the eve of Bealltainn, in the open air on the village threshing-floor. Its matter is whether a question may be forbidden. The Administration's clerk who attends writes that it may.

events.title: Teaching in the sacred forest
events.body: Druid masters who may no longer teach in a hall begin to teach under the trees in the sacred forest of Flidais near Muileann chiar, where the Administration has no building to shut.

events.title: Building the last beacon at Baile chrom
events.body: Work begins on the fifth and last beacon, on the north-western headland at Baile chrom, with masons taken by the Levy from the very villages whose fields they leave untilled.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: An Togail read at Cnoc thais

links.label: Caused by
links.title: A gale strips the beacon's scaffold

events.title: Uisdean mac Lachlainn named keeper of Taigh-solais Baile chrom
events.body: Uisdean mac Lachlainn of the headland villages is named the beacon's first keeper, on the recommendation of the very masons who built it: Dùghall Clachair among them, who signed the letter along with two of his crew.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Taigh-solais Baile chrom lit

told_in.book: Of An Togail and Fàinne nan Teintean-rabhaidh
told_in.section: V. Of the Ring Made Whole

events.title: The masons of Cnoc thais
events.body: The Levy takes the masons of Cnoc thais to build the beacon at Baile chrom. Their foreman, Dùghall Clachair, cuts the names of his crew into the lintel of the lamp-room, the only writing on any of the five towers.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: An Togail read at Cnoc thais

events.title: The five beacons complete
events.body: The ring of coast beacons is finished: Taigh-solais Baile chrom, Baile ìseal, Muileann bheag, Àth dhearg and Tobar dhearg. They serve a trade that is by now plunder in all but name.

events.title: Cuan ruadh loses its trade
events.body: The ring of beacons finished, the Company's steamers round the island without putting in, and within a few years the old coasting trade of Cuan ruadh up and down the eastern shore dies.

events.title: Taigh-solais Baile chrom lit
events.body: The beacon at Baile chrom is lit with a coal flame, and the ring is whole. The Company's ships can now round the island by night, and the keepers' daybooks show the sailings doubled within a few years.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Uisdean mac Lachlainn named keeper of Taigh-solais Baile chrom

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Uisdean begins to write beyond the weather

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Uisdean's hand on the valve

events.title: The draft read at Baile chrom
events.body: An Togail is read at the market cross of Baile chrom, first in the humans' tongue and then in Dia-thìris by a clerk who stumbles over the numbers. It falls hardest on the coast and hill villages; the concession farms to the north, worked by the strangers' own people, send no one.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Levy

told_in.book: Of Gorta Baile chrom
told_in.section: I. Of the Empty Road

events.title: Gorta Baile chrom
events.body: The Great Hunger follows a failed harvest across thirty-four settlements, made worse because the Levy has taken so many to the pits that too few are left to till the land.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first harvest short

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Uisdean begins to write beyond the weather

events.title: The first harvest short
events.body: The harvest round Baile chrom comes in at less than half the carts of the year before, the fields sown thin for want of hands and beaten further by two summer storms. Uisdean counts the carts against his own earlier tally and finds the shortfall for himself.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Gorta Baile chrom

told_in.book: Of Gorta Baile chrom
told_in.section: I. Of the Empty Road

events.title: Baile chrom goes hungry
events.body: The hunger is worst at Baile chrom itself, whose people could see the new beacon from their empty fields. The custodians write that more died there than anywhere else, and the Administration, which kept its own count, does not gainsay them.

events.title: The famine country
events.body: The custodians' roll draws the bounds of the famine country along the north-west shore and the hills behind it. Within them lie Baile chrom in its own shire; Ceann mhòr, Àth fhionn and Àth dhearg in the shire of Ceann mhòr; Muileann àrsaidh in the shire of Cnoc thais; and Achadh àrsaidh in the shire of Muileann àrsaidh. Thirty-four settlements are counted within the line, and the roll gives the dead of each.

events.title: Uisdean begins to write beyond the weather
events.body: In his second spring keeping the daybook of Taigh-solais Baile chrom, Uisdean mac Lachlainn writes down more than the wind and the oil for the first time: that a farmer of his acquaintance ploughs alone, with none of the hands who worked beside him the year before.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Taigh-solais Baile chrom lit

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Gorta Baile chrom

told_in.book: Of Gorta Baile chrom
told_in.section: I. Of the Empty Road

events.title: The hunger at Doire ghlas
events.body: At Doire ghlas in the north the hunger takes the old and the very young first. The village sends its young folk to the camps for the Company's rations, and by the year's end it is half empty.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Mòr nic Aonghais sends her son south

events.title: Inis mhin eats its seed
events.body: In the second winter of the hunger the townsfolk of Inis mhin on the north coast eat their seed corn. The Mission kitchen at the harbour feeds three hundred a day for a season.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The kitchen at Inis mhin's harbour

events.title: Mòr nic Aonghais sends her son south
events.body: At Doire ghlas, a woman named Mòr nic Aonghais walks her fourteen-year-old son as far as the boundary stone and no further, by the coast's custom, and sends him to the camps for A' Chompanaidh's ration rather than keep him at a table with too little on it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The hunger at Doire ghlas

told_in.book: Of Gorta Baile chrom
told_in.section: II. Of the Bounds of the Hunger

events.title: The kitchen at Inis mhin's harbour
events.body: With its seed corn eaten and no crop sown, Inis mhin is fed through the second winter of the hunger by Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise's kitchen at the harbour, which serves three hundred a day on fish broth and biscuit brought by sea from Cathair gheal.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Inis mhin eats its seed

told_in.book: Of Gorta Baile chrom
told_in.section: II. Of the Bounds of the Hunger

events.title: Anne Colby's letter to Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir
events.body: With the relief ship idle at anchor, Anne Colby writes to Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir at Ros dhomhain asking only who should be told to unload it. Eleven days pass before an answer that names no one and settles nothing, noting only that Àrd-mhaor Tolley has heard her concern.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The relief ship

told_in.book: Of Gorta Baile chrom
told_in.section: III. Of the Ship at Ros dhomhain

events.title: The relief ship unloaded without an order
events.body: After a month idle in the roads at Ros dhomhain, the relief ship's holds are opened at last when a clerk of Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir and a clerk of A' Chompanaidh set men to the work themselves, without waiting for either office to settle the dispute between them.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The relief ship

told_in.book: Of Gorta Baile chrom
told_in.section: III. Of the Ship at Ros dhomhain

events.title: Anne Colby takes the kitchen at Baile chrom
events.body: Anne Colby goes north to Baile chrom to run Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise's kitchen in a net-shed by the harbour, and keeps it through the worst of the hunger on the relief ship's grain and whatever the boats can add to it.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The relief ship

told_in.book: Of Gorta Baile chrom
told_in.section: IV. Of the Kitchen Below the Tower

events.title: The hunger reaches Seann Bhrenn
events.body: The hunger reaches as far east as Seann Bhrenn, where the custodians open the old grain-pits of the Holy Age, unfilled in living memory. They hold only dust.

events.title: The relief ship
events.body: A relief ship with grain from an Tìr Thall lies a month at Ros dhomhain while the Residency and the Company dispute who shall pay for its unloading. Meanwhile the Mission opens kitchens at Cathair gheal and Baile chrom, and Anne Colby, come back to the island, keeps the one at Baile chrom.

links.title: Anne Colby's letter to Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir

links.title: The relief ship unloaded without an order

events.title: Uisdean's hand on the valve
events.body: In the second winter of the hunger, Uisdean mac Lachlainn climbs to the lamp of Taigh-solais Baile chrom and stands a long while with his hand on the oil valve, weighing whether to let the light fail. He writes the thought into the daybook and lets the lamp burn on.

links.title: Taigh-solais Baile chrom lit

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The Levy set aside

events.title: Anne Colby's private roll of names
events.body: At the Baile chrom kitchen Anne Colby keeps a book of her own, apart from Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise's, writing every name she feeds and crossing it through, gently, in the corner of the page, whenever that person does not come again.

links.title: The relief ship

links.title: Uisdean's hand on the valve

links.title: An Togail read ended at Baile chrom

told_in.book: Of Gorta Baile chrom
told_in.section: IV. Of the Kitchen Below the Tower

events.title: The Levy set aside
events.body: The Levy is set aside in the famine districts, too late for the harvest. It is not repealed. The custodians note that it was never used again, nor needed to be, for the villages had learned what it meant.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Uisdean's hand on the valve

links.label: Leads to
links.title: An Togail read ended at Baile chrom

events.title: Cnoc mhòr walks south
events.body: Rather than starve, the families of Cnoc mhòr in the north walk south to the camps and take work under the Company. Their village stands empty for a generation.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The grass in Cnoc mhòr's street

events.title: An Togail read ended at Baile chrom
events.body: The clerk who first read An Togail at the market cross of Baile chrom returns to read that it is set aside in the famine districts, two harvests after the failure it caused. The custodians note it is not repealed, only set by, and expect no more of it.

links.title: The Levy set aside

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Anne Colby's private roll of names

told_in.book: Of Gorta Baile chrom
told_in.section: VI. Of the Order That Came Too Late

events.title: The grass in Cnoc mhòr's street
events.body: A carter passing through empty Cnoc mhòr some weeks after its people leave finds every door shut but unbarred, and grass already coming up between the stones of the street, a sign that reaches the kitchen at Baile chrom before the village itself is spoken of again.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Cnoc mhòr walks south

told_in.book: Of Gorta Baile chrom
told_in.section: VI. Of the Order That Came Too Late

events.title: Robert Haskins Commissioner
events.body: George Tolley retires with honours. Robert Haskins, who follows him, orders that the custodians' council be consulted on the tithe, and then sets the tithe before the council has met.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Word of Tolley's retiral reaches Cill ghlas

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Aonghas Ruadh calls the custodians of the east

events.title: Word of Tolley's retiral reaches Cill ghlas
events.body: A carter brings Peigi Ghlas, custodian of Cill ghlas, the worn word that George Tolley is going home with honours and that Robert Haskins, who follows him, means to ask the custodians' council its mind before he sets anything down. Peigi trims the shrine lamp and tells the flame, not the carter, what three such promises have been worth before.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Robert Haskins Commissioner

told_in.book: Of the Petition on the Bench
told_in.section: I. Of the Word from Ros dhomhain

events.title: Customs at Seann Dunn
events.body: Haskins opens a customs house at Seann Dunn on the eastern coast, and a Company store with it. The store sells the east its seed and its tools, and within a few years its ledgers hold the debts of half the district.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Coinneach Òg tells of the store's ledgers at Seann Dunn

events.title: The custodians ride to Ceann àrsaidh
events.body: Custodians of nineteen settlements come in to Ceann àrsaidh through am Faoilleach, on foot and by cart, and camp along the inside of the town wall while they wait for the last of their number. Peigi Ghlas of Cill ghlas walks it in two days, carrying her cloak and her village's slate of An Togail's and the famine's dead rolled with it.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first petition

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The gathering at Ceann àrsaidh

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Aonghas Ruadh calls the custodians of the east

told_in.book: Of the Petition on the Bench
told_in.section: II. Of the Store at Seann Dunn

events.title: Aonghas Ruadh calls the custodians of the east
events.body: Once the tithe goes up on A' Chompanaidh's boards before any custodian's answer has reached Ros dhomhain, Aonghas Ruadh of Ceann àrsaidh sends riders to the settlements of the east and the hills, naming a day in am Faoilleach to draw up one grievance in one hand rather than let it be filed apart, settlement by settlement, as every single letter before it had been.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Robert Haskins Commissioner

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first petition

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The custodians ride to Ceann àrsaidh

told_in.book: Of the Petition on the Bench
told_in.section: III. Of the Nineteen at Ceann àrsaidh

events.title: Coinneach Òg tells of the store's ledgers at Seann Dunn
events.body: At a fire inside the wall of Ceann àrsaidh, Coinneach Òg of the eastern coast tells the gathered custodians how A' Chompanaidh's store at Seann Dunn, opened as help against a bad year, now holds the debts of near half his district, entered against named households, and grows no smaller in any year, only more slowly.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Customs at Seann Dunn

links.title: The drafting argued over three days

told_in.book: Of the Petition on the Bench
told_in.section: II. Of the Store at Seann Dunn

events.title: The first petition
events.body: For the first time the custodians of the Dia-thìrich act together, and not settlement by settlement, and lay a written grievance before the humans' Administration. It is not answered.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The custodians ride to Ceann àrsaidh

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Aonghas Ruadh calls the custodians of the east

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The drafting argued over three days

events.title: The drafting argued over three days
events.body: In the hall behind the market square at Ceann àrsaidh the nineteen custodians argue three days over how to set their grievance down. An old custodian of the hills wants every death named; Aonghas Ruadh argues for one plain page that might be read where a long roll would only be filed. The shorter paper carries, and the old man signs it all the same.

links.title: The first petition

links.title: The gathering at Ceann àrsaidh

links.title: Coinneach Òg tells of the store's ledgers at Seann Dunn

told_in.section: III. Of the Nineteen at Ceann àrsaidh

events.title: The gathering at Ceann àrsaidh
events.body: The petition was drawn up at Ceann àrsaidh by custodians of nineteen settlements, meeting for the first time as one body. Peigi Ghlas, custodian of Cill ghlas, carried it to the Residency and handed it to a clerk.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The custodians ride to Ceann àrsaidh

links.title: The drafting argued over three days

events.title: Peigi Ghlas at Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir
events.body: Peigi Ghlas carries the fair copy of the nineteen settlements' petition to Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir at Ros dhomhain, is turned back twice at the gate, and on the third day is shown into a stone passage smelling of lamp-soot to wait on a worn bench before a young clerk takes the paper, thanks her, and lays it on an unremarkable pile.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The gathering at Ceann àrsaidh

told_in.book: Of the Petition on the Bench
told_in.section: IV. Of the Bench in the Passage

events.title: Aonghas Ruadh's letters go unanswered
events.body: Through the year after the petition is filed, Aonghas Ruadh writes twice more to Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir asking only whether the paper of am Faoilleach was received and read. The first letter gets no reply at all; the second, in the autumn, is answered in a strange clerk's hand that the matter remains under consideration.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The gathering at Ceann àrsaidh

told_in.book: Of the Petition on the Bench
told_in.section: V. Of Brìde's Lamp

events.title: Two days on the bench in the lamp-soot passage
events.body: Before the clerk receives her, Peigi Ghlas is turned back at Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir's gate once and kept waiting a second day in a yard and a windowless passage, on a stone bench worn pale in the middle by everyone who has sat there before her, with the boy of Ceann àrsaidh who carries the second copy standing at her shoulder.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The gathering at Ceann àrsaidh

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Three more names cut into the slate at Cill ghlas

told_in.book: Of the Petition on the Bench
told_in.section: IV. Of the Bench in the Passage

events.title: Three more names cut into the slate at Cill ghlas
events.body: In the year the petition waits unanswered, Peigi Ghlas adds three more names to the slate she keeps by the shrine door: two of a fall of stone at Baile thais, and an old hewer of Cill ghlas who does not come up from the gallery one evening in an t-Sultain, of nothing but the going down itself, done too many years too many times.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The gathering at Ceann àrsaidh

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Two days on the bench in the lamp-soot passage

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Peigi Ghlas trims Brìde's lamp at the year's end

told_in.book: Of the Petition on the Bench
told_in.section: V. Of Brìde's Lamp

events.title: Peigi Ghlas trims Brìde's lamp at the year's end
events.body: On a frost-still evening near the close of an Dùbhlachd, with no answer yet come from Ros dhomhain, Peigi Ghlas climbs to the shrine at Cill ghlas and trims the flame called Brìde's square and clean, as she does every evening of her life, the one thing no clerk's pile can take out of her hands.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The gathering at Ceann àrsaidh

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Three more names cut into the slate at Cill ghlas

told_in.book: Of the Petition on the Bench
told_in.section: V. Of Brìde's Lamp

events.title: Àth fhionn signs
events.body: Ruairidh mac Thormoid, custodian of Àth fhionn in the south-east, is the eldest of those who signed the petition. He was born before the humans' coin was struck, and says so beside his name.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ruairidh mac Thormoid writes 'born before the coin'

events.title: Ruairidh mac Thormoid writes 'born before the coin'
events.body: Ruairidh mac Thormoid of Àth fhionn, who walked to Ceann àrsaidh on his own feet and remembers, by his own count, a world before the mark was struck, signs the petition last and slowest, and adds beside his name the only line any of the nineteen thought to add: born before the coin.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Àth fhionn signs

told_in.book: Of the Petition on the Bench
told_in.section: III. Of the Nineteen at Ceann àrsaidh

events.title: Grievance first written
events.body: From these years come the oldest writings of grievance among the Dia-thìrich that survive. No hand is yet raised in them; yet in them it is first written that something has gone wrong.

events.title: Leabhar Baile thais
events.body: The oldest of them is a book of complaints kept at Baile thais, set down by many hands over some years: wages, deaths, the granary, the stream at Doire mhòr. The custodians' copyists call it Leabhar Baile thais.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Griogair mac Aonghais tells Fearchar to sing it

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Fearchar sits two nights over Leabhar Baile thais

events.title: Griogair mac Aonghais tells Fearchar to sing it
events.body: Old Griogair mac Aonghais, who broke coal beside Fearchar's father before him, tells Fearchar that a column is for men who have given up hoping to be heard, and that he should sing the grievance instead of writing it. Fearchar carries the book back to Baile thais and begins working verses to the granary's short week.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Leabhar Baile thais

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Fearchar sits two nights over Leabhar Baile thais

told_in.book: Of Fearchar Bàrd's Songs
told_in.section: I. Of the Book That Would Not Stay Shut

events.title: Fearchar sits two nights over Leabhar Baile thais
events.body: A copy of the grievance book reaches Muileann dhearg folded in a meal-sack, and Fearchar Bàrd, a breaker of coal at the belt since boyhood, reads it by tallow light two nights running. He finds he can put nothing of his own into its columns, though he knows the granary's short week and the stream at Doire mhòr as well as any hand that wrote there.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Leabhar Baile thais

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Griogair mac Aonghais tells Fearchar to sing it

told_in.book: Of Fearchar Bàrd's Songs
told_in.section: I. Of the Book That Would Not Stay Shut

events.title: The songs of Fearchar Bàrd
events.body: The poet Fearchar Bàrd, a breaker of coal at Muileann dhearg since boyhood, makes songs of the Levy and the famine, and they are sung in the camps. The overseers forbid them, and because they were forbidden several were written down.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Fearchar repays the docked wage

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Fearchar's first song sung at the pit-mouth

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The overseer's clerk copies the forbidden song

events.title: Songs at An Taigh-òsta Grianach
events.body: The songs of Fearchar Bàrd are sung in the roadside houses of the east, and An Taigh-òsta Grianach becomes known for them. The Company's carters sing them too, the keeper writes, not always knowing what they sing.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Fearchar hears his own song sung unknowing

events.title: Fearchar repays the docked wage
events.body: Fearchar Bàrd walks to Baile thais to repay out of his own wage the boy docked half a week's pay for singing his song, and the boy refuses the coin, saying he would rather have sung it than not. The song is sung again within the week, further than before.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The songs of Fearchar Bàrd

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Fearchar's first song sung at the pit-mouth

told_in.book: Of Fearchar Bàrd's Songs
told_in.section: II. Of the Song That Was Forbidden and So Written Down

events.title: Fearchar's first song sung at the pit-mouth
events.body: Fearchar Bàrd sings his first finished song, four verses on An Togail and the famine, at the pit-mouth of Muileann dhearg while the crews wait out a stopped winding-gear. It is carried to Baile thais within the month by crews he never asked to carry it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The songs of Fearchar Bàrd

links.title: Fearchar repays the docked wage

links.title: The overseer's clerk copies the forbidden song

told_in.book: Of Fearchar Bàrd's Songs
told_in.section: II. Of the Song That Was Forbidden and So Written Down

events.title: The overseer's clerk copies the forbidden song
events.body: An overseer at Baile thais has Fearchar's song taken down word for word from a boy of the crews so that it can be shown forbidden, and a docker's pay is cut by half a week for the singing of it. The clerk's copy, made to condemn the song, becomes the only complete written record of it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The songs of Fearchar Bàrd

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Fearchar's first song sung at the pit-mouth

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Fearchar hears his own song sung unknowing

told_in.book: Of Fearchar Bàrd's Songs
told_in.section: II. Of the Song That Was Forbidden and So Written Down

events.title: The Company's deep-water quay
events.body: The Company builds at Ros dhomhain a deep-water quay for the new iron steamships, which burn the island's own coal to carry it away. Fearchar Bàrd makes a song of that, the most quoted of all his songs.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The fire-ship loads at Ros dhomhain

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Fearchar makes the ship song

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The carters sing the ship song for their own quay

events.title: The deep quay at Ceann chaol
events.body: A second deep-water quay is built at Ceann chaol in the south-east for the eastern coal. Its builders are brought from the coast, and the village of forty houses becomes a town of four hundred.

events.title: Fearchar hears his own song sung unknowing
events.body: Riding east on Comann an Airgid's business, Fearchar Bàrd sits unknown at An Taigh-òsta Grianach and hears six carters of A' Chompanaidh sing his granary song through, missing a line they cannot remember. He says nothing of whose it is, and finds the mis-singing harder to bear than the forbidding had been.

links.title: Songs at An Taigh-òsta Grianach

links.title: The overseer's clerk copies the forbidden song

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The fire-ship loads at Ros dhomhain

told_in.book: Of Fearchar Bàrd's Songs
told_in.section: III. Of the Roadside House in the East

events.title: Baile thais walls its pithead
events.body: The Company rings the pithead at Baile thais with a stone wall and a gate, and pays a watchman to count who goes in. It is the first working on Dia-thìr walled against its own crews.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The wall rises at Baile thais

events.title: Catrìona nic Eachainn dies at the silver town
events.body: Catrìona nic Eachainn dies at Muileann chiar, a refiner of the silver guild to the end. The camp folk of Baile thais send men to her burying, and the Company docks each of them a day's pay.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Fearchar makes Catrìona's lament

events.title: The fire-ship loads at Ros dhomhain
events.body: Fearchar Bàrd, at Ros dhomhain on Comann an Airgid's errand, watches A' Chompanaidh's first iron steamship take on coal through the night at the new deep-water quay, burning the island's own fuel to carry the rest away. He stands at the rail until past midnight, watching the loading by lamplight.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Company's deep-water quay

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Fearchar hears his own song sung unknowing

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Fearchar makes the ship song

told_in.book: Of Fearchar Bàrd's Songs
told_in.section: IV. Of the Quay That Ate the Hill

events.title: Fearchar makes the ship song
events.body: That same night, sitting on the new quay's coiled rope, Fearchar Bàrd makes the song of the ship that eats the hill to carry the hill away, the most quoted of all his songs. He sings it first to the loading gang he stood beside, too tired themselves to do more than nod.

links.title: The Company's deep-water quay

links.title: The fire-ship loads at Ros dhomhain

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The wall rises at Baile thais

told_in.book: Of Fearchar Bàrd's Songs
told_in.section: IV. Of the Quay That Ate the Hill

events.title: The wall rises at Baile thais
events.body: A' Chompanaidh rings the pithead at Baile thais with a stone wall and a single gate through the summer, and sets a lamed former hewer to keep the tally-book at the gate. Fearchar Bàrd, home from Ros dhomhain, walks the wall's length and makes no song of it that year.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Baile thais walls its pithead

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Fearchar makes the ship song

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Fearchar makes Catrìona's lament

told_in.book: Of Fearchar Bàrd's Songs
told_in.section: V. Of the Wall at Baile thais

events.title: Fearchar makes Catrìona's lament
events.body: On the walk home from Muileann chiar, Fearchar Bàrd makes the lament for Catrìona nic Eachainn, naming the coal-tub and the empty shelves she counted and the guild's bench where she stood to the end, and ending it, as her life had ended, without complaint. The dozen who had known her weep at it on the road.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Catrìona nic Eachainn dies at the silver town

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The wall rises at Baile thais

told_in.book: Of Fearchar Bàrd's Songs
told_in.section: VI. Of Catrìona's Burying

events.title: The quay fire
events.body: A fire starts in the Company's coal sheds at Ros dhomhain and burns three days, taking two streets of the harbour quarter with it. The Company's inquiry finds no cause; the harbour quarter's own account has several.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The carters sing the ship song for their own quay

events.title: The council without a high custodian
events.body: After the death of the last high custodian the Council of Custodians cannot agree on another, and sits for years with the seat empty. Robert Haskins writes to an Tìr Thall that this makes the council easier to deal with.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Artair mac Iain dies at Cathair dhearg

events.title: Artair mac Iain dies at Cathair dhearg
events.body: Artair mac Iain, Ceann a' Chùraim for twenty and four years, dies at Cathair dhearg at eighty years old. Word of his death reaches Fearchar Bàrd on the road home from An Taigh-òsta Grianach, carried faster than either fire or song by a rider changing horses at every post-house.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The council without a high custodian

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The carters sing the ship song for their own quay

told_in.book: Of Fearchar Bàrd's Songs
told_in.section: VII. Of the Fire on the Quay, and the Empty Seat

events.title: The carters sing the ship song for their own quay
events.body: At An Taigh-òsta Grianach, Fearchar Bàrd hears the fire-ship's carters sing his ship song louder and rougher than before, now that their own quay has burned, though none of them know the song or its maker. He sits again unknown, and does not tell them.

links.title: The Company's deep-water quay

links.title: The quay fire

events.title: Tiormachd Achadh shean
events.body: The Long Drought lies on the island's dry season three years together, and bears hard on a people already worn thin by the tallies of the pits.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Iseabail begins her forty pages

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Baile chaol slaughters its herd

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Iseabail drives Àth mhòr's beasts west and counts the dead

links.title: Riaghaltas nan Coigreach's watchman recalled from Allt an Àigh
