links.label: Leads to
links.title: Coll's report names the drought-fever's true cause

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Every custodian of the drought country petitions Haskins

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise bores wells that hold at Achadh shean and Àth chrom

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise's rig strikes water at Achadh shean

events.title: Iseabail begins her forty pages
events.body: Understanding that her petition will be answered with nothing but the words under consideration, Iseabail nic Leòid begins writing, over a winter, a full account of the drought's three years: the wells, the cattle, the fever's dead, the watchman recalled from Allt an Àigh, for whoever may someday want to know its cost.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Tiormachd Achadh shean

told_in.book: Of Tiormachd Achadh shean
told_in.section: VII. Of the Petition, Begun Alone

events.title: The wells of Achadh shean
events.body: At Achadh shean, whose name the drought bears, the wells fail in the second summer, and the cattle are driven west in a column the roll calls a day long. Fewer than half reach water.

events.title: The dry country
events.body: The custodians' roll counts ten districts of the east as drought country, worst at Achadh shean, Àth uaine, Achadh àrsaidh and Muileann chiar, and reaching down to Cuan ruadh and west toward Baile chaol. The Administration keeps no count of its own.

events.title: The cattle of Baile chaol
events.body: At Baile chaol the herds are slaughtered in the second summer of the drought, rather than watched as they die. The salt meat is sold to the Company for the camps, at a price the Company names.

events.title: Doire fhionn walks for water
events.body: At Doire fhionn in the east the women walk each day to the spring at Àth ruadh and back for water, half a day's journey. The custodians record it for the three dry years, and then cease.

events.title: Baile chaol slaughters its herd
events.body: With no grazing left within four days' driving, Baile chaol's custodian Ealasaid Ruadh orders the town's whole herd killed and the meat salted rather than risk the loss of it on the road. The town loses fewer of its people to hunger that winter than any other of the ten drought districts.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Tiormachd Achadh shean

told_in.book: Of Tiormachd Achadh shean
told_in.section: III. Of Baile chaol's Choice

events.title: Iseabail drives Àth mhòr's beasts west and counts the dead
events.body: Iseabail nic Leòid leads the herds of Àth mhòr and Achadh shean on a day-long drive west to the tarn above Doire fhionn. Fewer than half the beasts reach water on their own legs; she keeps a private count of the fallen, ninety-eight marks by the drive's end, and of the eleven calves among them.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Tiormachd Achadh shean

told_in.book: Of Tiormachd Achadh shean
told_in.section: II. Of the Cattle Column

events.title: Pilgrims at Allt an Àigh
events.body: The spring of Allt an Àigh, said never to have failed, runs on through all three dry years. Pilgrims who keep Na Seann Spioradan come to it from all the east, the first of them at Bealltainn, and the Administration sets a watchman to charge them for the water. He is called back after one season.

events.title: The pilgrims' road at Inis uaine
events.body: Pilgrims bound for Allt an Àigh gather at Inis uaine, and the townsfolk feed them freely, as the Old Spirits require. The town's own wells are low, and it gives away more water than it keeps.

events.title: Riaghaltas nan Coigreach's watchman recalled from Allt an Àigh
events.body: Riaghaltas nan Coigreach posts a watchman at Allt an Àigh to charge a set rate for the water. He is refused by an old woman of Achadh àrsaidh who will not pay a stranger for water that has run free since before his people came, and is called back before the season is out; the spring's keepers enter the word restored under his going.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Tiormachd Achadh shean

told_in.book: Of Tiormachd Achadh shean
told_in.section: IV. Of the Spring That Did Not Fail

events.title: Achadh chaol's households go down to the pits
events.body: With its grazing gone two years running, Achadh chaol sends its young to sign hewers' contracts at Cnoc fhiadhaich and elsewhere in numbers its custodian has never before had to record, families who had kept beasts and small fields for generations going down into the galleries for a wage that a dry year cannot touch.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Tiormachd Achadh shean

told_in.book: Of Tiormachd Achadh shean
told_in.section: VI. Of Achadh chaol Going Down

events.title: Drought-fever at Baile Mòr ruadh
events.body: A fever of foul water follows the drought into the towns, worst at Baile Mòr ruadh, where the wells had been deepened into the old middens. Seventeen die. The Mission's report is the first to name the cause rightly.

events.title: The fever at Cnoc shean
events.body: The drought-fever spreads to Cnoc shean, whose one well is found tainted. The custodians close it, and for a year the town drinks from carts.

events.title: The Mission's wells
events.body: The Mission sinks deep wells at Achadh shean and Àth chrom with a boring-rig brought from an Tìr Thall, and they hold. The custodians of the east set down the Mission's wells and the Company's tallies on facing pages, without comment.

events.title: Coll's report names the drought-fever's true cause
events.body: Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise's physician at Baile Mòr ruadh, a young man named Coll, tests the town's water and finds it fouled by the old midden ground its deep wells were sunk through. His report to Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise's house at Cathair dhearg is the first that autumn to name the fever's cause rightly.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Tiormachd Achadh shean

told_in.book: Of Tiormachd Achadh shean
told_in.section: V. Of the Drought-Fever

events.title: Every custodian of the drought country petitions Haskins
events.body: Each of the ten drought districts' custodians petitions Àrd-mhaor Haskins in her own hand, unknown to the others, asking that A' Chompanaidh's quota be set aside until two seasons of ordinary rain are counted. Iseabail nic Leòid rides her own petition to Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir and is told, as every other has been told, that the matter is under consideration.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Tiormachd Achadh shean

told_in.book: Of Tiormachd Achadh shean
told_in.section: VII. Of the Petition, Begun Alone

events.title: Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise bores wells that hold at Achadh shean and Àth chrom
events.body: Following Coll's report, Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise bores new wells at Achadh shean and Àth chrom, dug deep and clean of old ground. The wells hold, and the drought-fever does not follow them; the custodians of the drought country begin entering Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise's wells and A' Chompanaidh's unmoved quota on facing pages of their rolls.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Tiormachd Achadh shean

told_in.book: Of Tiormachd Achadh shean
told_in.section: V. Of the Drought-Fever

events.title: Achadh chaol goes to the pits
events.body: Their fields burned out by the drought, the people of Achadh chaol in the north-east go to the pits for wages, the first villagers of the eastern farm country to do so. Their custodian writes it down as the end of the village, not a flitting.

events.title: The tally not lowered
events.body: The coal tally is not lowered in the drought. The custodians of the east, their joint petition unanswered, each write to Haskins alone; to each he answers that the matter is under consideration.

events.title: Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise's rig strikes water at Achadh shean
events.body: A third well bored by Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise's rig on the moor above Achadh shean strikes clean, running water deeper than any well the drought country has dug, marking the drought's end there. Iseabail nic Leòid rides out to see it and adds the day to her forty pages.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Tiormachd Achadh shean

told_in.book: Of Tiormachd Achadh shean
told_in.section: VII. Of the Petition, Begun Alone

events.title: The petition of Àth mhòr
events.body: Iseabail nic Leòid, custodian of Àth mhòr, writes the longest of the single petitions, forty pages listing her town's dead beasts. Haskins answers in two lines. Both survive, bound together by a later clerk.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A' Chompanaidh's survey marks the Hale cutting

events.title: A' Chompanaidh's survey marks the Hale cutting
events.body: A' Chompanaidh's surveyors, working out a new gallery above Baile dhìreach, mark the narrow customary cutting held by Eilidh nic Ruairidh's line for four generations. The agent Pryce offers Thomas Hale a small sum to sign it over rather than test A' Chompanaidh's claim.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The petition of Àth mhòr

links.label: Leads to

told_in.section: I. Of the Forty Pages and the Four Words

events.title: Thomas Hale's suit filed at Ros dhomhain
events.body: Thomas Hale walks the three days from Baile dhìreach to Ros dhomhain and files a claim at A' Chompanaidh's court, a copy of his grandmother's marriage roll in his coat and no other paper. The clerk gives a hearing date a full season off, at the back of the court's list.

links.title: The case of Thomas Hale

told_in.section: III. Of the Walk to Ros dhomhain

events.title: Mairead nic Aoidh copies the marriage roll
events.body: The custodian of Baile dhìreach copies, under her own seal, the roll's page of the second year recording the marriage of Eilidh nic Ruairidh and Samuel Hale in two tongues, so that Thomas Hale may carry proof of the line to A' Chompanaidh's court.

links.title: The case of Thomas Hale

links.title: Thomas Hale's suit filed at Ros dhomhain

told_in.section: II. Of the Paper on the Table

events.title: The first inheritance of mixed blood
events.body: A suit over whether the grandchild of a marriage between a Dia-thìreach and a human may inherit the customary rights of mining is decided, and the Administration makes the ruling wholly to its own gain.

events.title: The case of Thomas Hale
events.body: The child was Thomas Hale, grandson of the marriage at Baile dhìreach of Eilidh nic Ruairidh and Samuel Hale, who claimed a share in a customary cutting through his Dia-thìrich grandmother. Oliver Dunstan, magistrate at Ros dhomhain, ruled that customary rights descend only through the line the Administration owns, and that it owns only its own.

links.title: A' Chompanaidh's survey marks the Hale cutting

events.title: Dunstan's ruling read at A' Chompanaidh's counter
events.body: Oliver Dunstan's ruling against Thomas Hale is posted at the Ros dhomhain counter among a dozen others of the same list. It holds that no marriage entered in a custodian's roll, however old, creates a line Riaghaltas nan Coigreach recognises, and confirms the cutting to A' Chompanaidh.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The case of Thomas Hale

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Mairead nic Aoidh copies the marriage roll

told_in.section: IV. Of Dunstan's Ruling

events.title: Dunstan's rule applied
events.body: Within a few years Dunstan's ruling is used to pass eleven customary cuttings to the Company, each because some holder in the line had married a human or been born of one. The custodians stop entering such marriages in the roll.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Mairead nic Aoidh stops entering marriages in the roll

events.title: Mairead nic Aoidh stops entering marriages in the roll
events.body: The custodian of Baile dhìreach ceases to enter marriages between Dia-thìrich and humans in her roll, judging that under Riaghailt Dunstan such an entry has become a paper a family's enemies may use against it rather than one that protects anything.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Dunstan's rule applied

links.title: The cutting at Seann Bhral taken

told_in.section: V. Of the Eleven Cuttings

events.title: The cutting at Seann Bhral taken
events.body: A second magistrate at Ros dhomhain, citing Thomas Hale's case by name, decides a claim on a customary working at Seann Bhral against a cooper's daughter's line, married three generations back to a human pilot. The ruling runs to a single page.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The case of Thomas Hale

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Dunstan's rule applied

links.title: Mairead nic Aoidh stops entering marriages in the roll

told_in.section: V. Of the Eleven Cuttings

events.title: The coast's custodians follow Baile dhìreach's example
events.body: Within the year other custodians of the western coast quietly stop entering two-tongue marriages in their own rolls, without any word agreed between the districts. The marriages go on; only the writing of them fails.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Dunstan's rule applied

told_in.book: Of Lagh na h-Aon Loidhne
told_in.section: V. Of the Eleven Cuttings

events.title: A cutting at Cnoc dhubh taken
events.body: Among the cuttings taken under Dunstan's rule is the old customary working at Cnoc dhubh, held by one family since the Holy Age. A great-grandmother of the line had married a human sailor; that is enough.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Griogair mac Ailein taken up at Cnoc chaol

events.title: Griogair mac Ailein taken up at Cnoc chaol
events.body: Griogair mac Ailein, a breaker of the Cnoc chaol sorting-floor, is taken up by A' Chompanaidh's constables over a dispute at the pay office and refuses to sign for a short-weighted cartload he did not cut. He is held in A' Chompanaidh's lock-up pending a hearing never set.

links.title: A cutting at Cnoc dhubh taken

events.title: The Lamp-Watch
events.body: A fellowship of pit crews calling itself the Lamp-Watch begins to meet at Baile thais and Cnoc chaol under cover of a burial club. Its first known deed is to pay for the burying of an old breaker who had died in the Company's lock-up.

links.title: Griogair mac Ailein taken up at Cnoc chaol

events.title: Griogair mac Ailein dies in the lock-up
events.body: Griogair mac Ailein dies in A' Chompanaidh's lock-up at Cnoc chaol of a fever A' Chompanaidh's own surgeon records as already advanced when he was taken. He has no family living to claim him.

links.title: The Lamp-Watch

told_in.section: VI. Of Faire nan Lòchran and Griogair mac Ailein

events.title: Thomas Hale sent for to read the surgeon's note
events.body: Dòmhnall Ruadh, a crew-leader of Baile thais, carries a letter to Baile dhìreach asking Thomas Hale, known along the coast for his hard-won knowledge of Riaghaltas nan Coigreach's law, to stand at Griogair mac Ailein's graveside and read A' Chompanaidh's surgeon's note releasing the body.

links.title: The Lamp-Watch

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The fellowship at Baile thais buys the ground and the box

told_in.section: VI. Of Faire nan Lòchran and Griogair mac Ailein

events.title: The fellowship at Baile thais buys the ground and the box
events.body: Comann an Adhlacaidh newly begun among the pit crews of Baile thais and Cnoc chaol, calling itself Faire nan Lòchran among its own members, gathers its members' wages to buy Griogair mac Ailein's grave-ground and coffin, meaning his burying to be seen done properly in A' Chompanaidh's own eye.

links.title: Thomas Hale sent for to read the surgeon's note

events.title: Thomas Hale reads the surgeon's note at the grave
events.body: At a grave dug on the bare hill above the Cnoc chaol pit-head, Thomas Hale reads Griogair mac Ailein's release aloud in A' Chompanaidh's own tongue before some thirty of the fellowship, so that no clerk may afterward say the burying was done without A' Chompanaidh's leave.

events.title: Edward Vane Commissioner
events.body: Robert Haskins is called home after a quarrel with the Company over the price of steamship berths, and Edward Vane follows him. Vane is the first Commissioner born on Dia-thìr, at the Residency, and he speaks Dia-thìris, badly, but he speaks it.

links.title: Robert Haskins leaves Ros dhomhain

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Edward Vane answers the port custodian

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Vane speaks Dia-thìris before the council at Cathair dhearg

events.title: Robert Haskins leaves Ros dhomhain
events.body: Robert Haskins, sixty-nine years old and Àrd-mhaor nine years, sails from Ros dhomhain after a quarrel with A' Chompanaidh over the price of a steamship berth. He never once, in nine years, spoke a full sentence of Dia-thìris without a clerk at his elbow to mend it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Edward Vane Commissioner

told_in.book: Of the Night Shift
told_in.section: I. Of the Man Who Spoke It Badly

events.title: Edward Vane answers the port custodian
events.body: Edward Vane, come up the same quay eleven days after Haskins sails, answers the custodian's customary greeting in Dia-thìris, badly and unprompted, the first Àrd-mhaor in living memory to do so without a clerk beside him.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Edward Vane Commissioner

told_in.book: Of the Night Shift
told_in.section: I. Of the Man Who Spoke It Badly

events.title: The tram-road to Ros dhìreach
events.body: Vane lays an iron tram-road, drawn by mules, from the southern workings down to the coal port at Ros dhìreach. It halves the cost of shipping coal, and ends the carting trade of the villages on the old road.

events.title: Vane speaks Dia-thìris before the council at Cathair dhearg
events.body: Edward Vane goes up to Cathair dhearg unsummoned and speaks three sentences of Dia-thìris to Comhairle a' Chùraim before finishing through Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise's interpreter, telling the council he has come home. The clerk enters the word exactly, wrong tense and all.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Edward Vane Commissioner

told_in.book: Of the Night Shift
told_in.section: I. Of the Man Who Spoke It Badly

events.title: The night-shift order
events.body: For the first time the digging is made to run without ceasing, day and night, and the mountain is given no season of rest at all.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The custodian of Cnoc chaol writes the bare page

events.title: The night crews at Cnoc chaol
events.body: The order falls first on Cnoc chaol, where the Company's newest galleries are opened to crews working by coal-lamp in two shifts. The custodians' roll writes that the hill was given no silence at all, and leaves the rest of the page blank.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The custodian of Cnoc chaol writes the bare page

events.title: The custodian of Cnoc chaol writes the bare page
events.body: Vane's Àithne na h-Oidhche is read at every pit-mouth from Cnoc chaol to Muileann chiar. The young custodian of Cnoc chaol enters it in her roll and writes beneath it a single line, that the hill is given no silence at all, and leaves the rest of the page blank.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The night-shift order

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The night crews at Cnoc chaol

told_in.book: Of the Night Shift
told_in.section: II. Of the Iron Road and the Order That Followed It

events.title: The day shift stands in the yard at Cnoc chaol
events.body: Three hundred hewers of the day shift refuse to go down for the night change and stand in the yard through the last light, saying nothing to the overseer who twice asks their meaning. No chant is raised and no threat made; they simply do not move.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The night-shift strike

told_in.book: Of the Night Shift
told_in.section: III. Of the Two Shifts and the Week It Lasted

events.title: New crews replace the standing shift within the week
events.body: A' Chompanaidh brings crews up the tram-road from the coast towns within a week, humans and Dia-thìrich both, and sets them to the night shift before the stand at Cnoc chaol is a fortnight old. The camp's own crews go back to the day shift they still have.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The night-shift strike

told_in.book: Of the Night Shift
told_in.section: III. Of the Two Shifts and the Week It Lasted

events.title: Muileann dhomhain shuts every door
events.body: The milling town of Muileann dhomhain refuses to house or feed the strikebreaking crews sent up from the coast. Every inn and counter turns them away, and the well at the crossroads is found blocked with stones on the second morning, by no hand the custodian troubled to guess at.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The strikebreakers of Muileann dhomhain

told_in.book: Of the Night Shift
told_in.section: III. Of the Two Shifts and the Week It Lasted

events.title: Baile ghorm's potteries take the lamp-body contract
events.body: The potteries of Baile ghorm take A' Chompanaidh's contract for clay coal-lamp bodies, thousands fired in a season on the same wheels that once turned bowls for the coast trade. Their own book notes them the first lamps made on the island for work commanded in the dark.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Coal-lamps from Baile ghorm

told_in.book: Of the Night Shift
told_in.section: VII. Of the Iron Chariot

events.title: The night-shift strike
events.body: The crews at Cnoc chaol refuse the night shift, and within a week are replaced by crews brought from the coast under the Company's new contracts. The Lamp-Watch keeps the strikers' families for a season, and then its money is gone.

links.title: New crews replace the standing shift within the week

links.title: Faire nan Lòchran's purse runs dry

events.title: The strikebreakers of Muileann dhomhain
events.body: The crews that replace the strikers at Cnoc chaol are brought through Muileann dhomhain, where the townsfolk turn them from every door. They sleep in the Company's barns, and several go home the next season.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Muileann dhomhain shuts every door

events.title: Faire nan Lòchran's purse runs dry
events.body: Faire nan Lòchran, keeping the households of the crews who stood at Cnoc chaol, empties its purse by the second winter. Its own reckoning, kept in an unnamed hand, closes the year's account at nothing, and beneath it notes only that the hill was not given back its silence.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Lamp-Watch

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The night-shift strike

told_in.book: Of the Night Shift
told_in.section: III. Of the Two Shifts and the Week It Lasted

events.title: Matthew Dunne's sermon
events.body: Matthew Dunne, the Mission's minister at Ros dhomhain, preaches against the night-shift order from the chapel pulpit, saying the Dia-thìrich are right that even the ground must rest. The Company complains to the Mission, and Dunne is called back to an Tìr Thall. The Lamp-Watch copies the sermon and reads it in the camps.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Matthew Dunne preaches the fallow year

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Matthew Dunne sails for an Tìr Thall

events.title: Matthew Dunne preaches the fallow year
events.body: Matthew Dunne preaches at Ros dhomhain that the Dia-thìrich are right, and that ground owed no season of rest was owed the same fallow year the humans' own scripture asks of a field. He does not name A' Chompanaidh; the chapel knows his meaning without it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Matthew Dunne's sermon

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Matthew Dunne sails for an Tìr Thall

told_in.book: Of the Night Shift
told_in.section: IV. Of the Sermon at Ros dhomhain

events.title: Matthew Dunne sails for an Tìr Thall
events.body: Recalled within the season on A' Chompanaidh's complaint, Matthew Dunne, three-and-thirty, preaches a last, ordinary sermon to a full chapel and goes down to the Ros dhomhain quay in the rain. Faire nan Lòchran has a copy of his fallow-year sermon within the week.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Matthew Dunne's sermon

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Matthew Dunne preaches the fallow year

told_in.book: Of the Night Shift
told_in.section: IV. Of the Sermon at Ros dhomhain

events.title: The camps begin saying Casad Dhonnchaidh
events.body: Among the Dia-thìrich hewers of Cnoc chaol Grodadh nan Scamhan spares more than it takes, unlike among the humans of the night crews. The old women of the camps, who know the telling of the hewer of Achadh dhomhain whose cough stopped on the night his daughter was born, call any such cough among their own Casad Dhonnchaidh, and say no more.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The lung-rot at Cnoc chaol

told_in.book: Of the Night Shift
told_in.section: V. Of Donnchadh's Cough

events.title: The lung-rot at Cnoc chaol
events.body: A wasting sickness of the lungs spreads among the night crews at Cnoc chaol and Baile thais. Unlike the Green Death it kills slowly. The Company pays the widows a pension for a year, then stops.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The camps begin saying Casad Dhonnchaidh

events.title: Iain Maor and the night shift
events.body: Iain Maor, overseer at Muileann chrom, writes to the Company that the night shift is killing his crews faster than it is paying for them. The letter survives because the Company filed it with his dismissal, which was undone a month later for want of anyone else.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Iain Maor dismissed and restored

events.title: Iain Maor dismissed and restored
events.body: Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir answers Iain Maor's letter with a notice relieving him of the overseer's staff for conduct unbecoming his office. His daughter Mòrag reads it to him by lamplight. Within a month, the crews having slowed the galleries to nothing, an unsigned notice restores him with no mention of the first.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Iain Maor and the night shift

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first coal train runs to Ros dhomhain

told_in.book: Of the Night Shift
told_in.section: VI. Of Iain Maor's Letter

events.title: The coal line
events.body: The Company opens its railway from the pits at Muileann chrom down by Cathair dhearg to the deep-water quay at Ros dhomhain. Its engines burn the island's own coal, as the steamships do, and the tram-road to Ros dhìreach is left to the mules. Within a year the carters' guild of Doire chaol, which had hauled the coal on Rathad na Mèinne for eighty years, loses the long haul. From the first day the Dia-thìrich call the engine carbad-iarainn, the iron chariot, and the railway the coal line.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first coal train runs to Ros dhomhain

events.title: Coal-lamps from Baile ghorm
events.body: The potteries of Baile ghorm take a contract for clay lamp-bodies for the night crews, thousands in a year. The potters' own book notes that they are the first lamps made on the island for work in the dark by command.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Baile ghorm's potteries take the lamp-body contract

events.title: The first coal train runs to Ros dhomhain
events.body: A' Chompanaidh's iron road opens from the pits at Muileann chrom, past the hill below Cathair dhearg, to the deep-water quay at Ros dhomhain. Iain Maor and his daughter Mòrag watch the first loaded train take the grade at a pace no mule ever kept; the crews name it carbad-iarainn before the day is out.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The coal line

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Iain Maor dismissed and restored

told_in.book: Of the Night Shift
told_in.section: VII. Of the Iron Chariot

events.title: Fionnan born
events.body: A second child is born bound to the coal as Aisling was, half a century after her. So it is known that the thing is no chance of one birth: it comes of the digging, and it will go on.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Fionnan's birth reaches the cellar

events.title: Fionnan's birth reaches the cellar
events.body: The birth of Fionnan, entered by an eastern custodian among the ordinary births of the year, reaches Seilear Muileann chaol folded into a roll like any other. No hand marks the line for what it is; the copyists learn to find it again only once the word for the thing exists to look for.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Fionnan born

told_in.book: Of the Cellar at Muileann chaol
told_in.section: I. Of the Second Birth

events.title: The Administration's count of the people
events.body: The Administration counts the people of Dia-thìr by district for the first time. Its figures for the humans are true to the household; for the Dia-thìrich they are rounded to the hundred, and in the hill districts to the thousand.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The count of the people copied in the cellar

events.title: Cailean mac Eachainn taken on at the cellar
events.body: Cailean mac Eachainn, a turf-cutter's son of Muileann chaol with a plain hand at his letters, is taken on by Na Trì Teaghlaichean of the cellar when Seònag Bhàn's eyes fail her past close work. He is asked first not whether he can write fair, but whether he can hold his tongue.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The custodians' rolls at Muileann chaol

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The count of the people copied in the cellar

told_in.book: Of the Cellar at Muileann chaol
told_in.section: III. Of the Three Households

events.title: The count of the people copied in the cellar
events.body: Cunntas an Riaghaltais passes through the cellar among Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir's business the custodians think worth keeping. Fearchar mac Ailpein remarks that it counts the Dia-thìrich the way a man counts trees, near enough for the timber and not near enough for the names.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Administration's count of the people

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Cailean mac Eachainn taken on at the cellar

told_in.book: Of the Cellar at Muileann chaol
told_in.section: IV. Of the Count of the People

events.title: The district of the outer coasts
events.body: The Administration makes the outer coasts one district and rules it from the harbour office at Seann Vell on Eilean ruadh, where its revenue cutters lie: the islands of the west and south, Eilean bhàn with Cuan dhearg and Cnoc chaol, and the southern edge of the windy coast in the far north-west. Its surveyors walk to the edge of the great moss there, which no chain can cross, and go no farther. Beyond it the district map is left blank.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The blank map of the outer coasts

events.title: The blank map of the outer coasts
events.body: A letter reaching the cellar notes that Riaghaltas nan Coigreach's surveyors, walking the edge of the great moss beyond Seann Vell, found no way across it and left the rest of the outer district's map blank, and that the custodians of those coasts were no readier to be counted than the moss itself.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The district of the outer coasts

told_in.book: Of the Cellar at Muileann chaol
told_in.section: IV. Of the Count of the People

events.title: Seònaid nic Dhùghaill, last of the druid masters
events.body: Seònaid nic Dhùghaill, the last master of Scoiltean nan Draoidhean to teach openly in this age, dies at Dùn thais. No one is named after her, and the school's register ends with her death. It is taken up again only long after the humans are gone.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Seònaid nic Dhùghaill's death entered at the cellar

events.title: Seònaid nic Dhùghaill's death entered at the cellar
events.body: Word reaches the cellar that Seònaid nic Dhùghaill has died at Dùn thais in her seventy-eighth year, and that the register of her school ends with her, there being none of her house or pupils willing to keep it in the open. Cailean copies the line as it stands.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Seònaid nic Dhùghaill, last of the druid masters

told_in.book: Of the Cellar at Muileann chaol
told_in.section: V. Of the Death of the Last Teacher

events.title: The custodians' rolls at Muileann chaol
events.body: The custodians of the east begin to send copies of their rolls for safe keeping to the town of Muileann chaol, which still kept Beathag nic Thòmais's loft of papers, beyond the Residency's reach. The copying is done in the houses of three families, and the copies kept in a cellar.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Cailean mac Eachainn taken on at the cellar

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The cellar comes to know the eastern hills by heart

events.title: The cellar comes to know the eastern hills by heart
events.body: Winter on winter Na Trì Teaghlaichean of the cellar copy the whole record of the eastern hills, every birth and burial and fine and fever, until between them they come to know the district better than any single custodian who keeps only his own corner of it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The custodians' rolls at Muileann chaol

told_in.book: Of the Cellar at Muileann chaol
told_in.section: III. Of the Three Households

events.title: The second Muileann chaol
events.body: Some of the copies bound for Muileann chaol go by mistake to the smaller town of that name further north, and are kept there for years before the mistake is found. The custodians note that they were kept just as well.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Nothing of weight was lost

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The receipt for a delivery never made

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Cailean fetches the mis-sent copies

events.title: Nothing of weight was lost
events.body: By lamplight Fearchar mac Ailpein and Cailean mac Eachainn match the recovered northern rolls against the cellar's own patched record of the missing years, and find that little of any weight had truly gone missing, only kept for a time in the wrong cellar.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The second Muileann chaol

told_in.book: Of the Cellar at Muileann chaol
told_in.section: VI. Of the Copies Gone Astray

events.title: The receipt for a delivery never made
events.body: Fearchar mac Ailpein finds among the cellar's bundles a northern custodian's receipt for a delivery the cellar never received. Na Trì Teaghlaichean learn only then that a second town of the same name, some hours to the north, has for years been taking in copies meant for their own cellar.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The second Muileann chaol

told_in.book: Of the Cellar at Muileann chaol
told_in.section: VI. Of the Copies Gone Astray

events.title: Cailean fetches the mis-sent copies
events.body: Cailean walks north on foot to the smaller Muileann chaol and finds three years of missing rolls kept whole and dry by an old custodian who says only that a roll is a roll, and that he kept it well until someone came to say it was theirs. Cailean carries the chest home unopened.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The second Muileann chaol

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The vote at the shrine of Cill ghlas

told_in.book: Of the Cellar at Muileann chaol
told_in.section: VI. Of the Copies Gone Astray

events.title: The word found at last
events.body: With two children now known, the custodians agree on a word for what is befalling them: fuil-ghuail, "coal-blood", rendered in the humans' tongue as coal-touched. It is meant as a physician's word. It outlives that meaning.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The vote at the shrine of Cill ghlas

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Peigi Ghlas calls the custodians to Cill ghlas

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Cailean writes the word into the physician's column

events.title: The vote at the shrine of Cill ghlas
events.body: By the light of Brìde's lamp at the mouth of the oldest cutting, the custodians gathered at Cill ghlas argue two hours over a name for the coal-blood before a show of hands settles it. Cailean mac Eachainn, come up from the cellar to write it fair, counts more hands raised than not.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The word found at last

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The custodians who named it

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Cailean fetches the mis-sent copies

told_in.book: Of the Cellar at Muileann chaol
told_in.section: IX. Of the Naming

events.title: The custodians who named it
events.body: The word was agreed at a meeting of custodians at the shrine of Cill ghlas, where the oldest cutting still stood open. They chose a plain word, fit for the physician's book. The roll gives the vote; who first put the word forward it does not say.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The vote at the shrine of Cill ghlas

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Cailean writes the word into the physician's column

events.title: Peigi Ghlas calls the custodians to Cill ghlas
events.body: Peigi Ghlas writes to every custodian within two days' walk, calling them to the shrine of Cill ghlas on the night of the coming full moon to settle a name for the change that has now come twice upon a child of the pits, and asks the cellar to send a hand who can write it fair on the spot.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The word found at last

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Cailean writes the word into the physician's column

told_in.book: Of the Cellar at Muileann chaol
told_in.section: IX. Of the Naming

events.title: Cailean writes the word into the physician's column
events.body: At Peigi Ghlas's dictation, Cailean mac Eachainn writes the agreed word into a physician's register at the mouth of the cutting, then carries the leaf home to Muileann chaol for a second fair copy. His own hand is the first to set fuil-ghuail down among the ordinary births and burials of the roll.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The word found at last

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The custodians who named it

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Peigi Ghlas calls the custodians to Cill ghlas

told_in.book: Of the Cellar at Muileann chaol
told_in.section: IX. Of the Naming

events.title: The Line of Aisling found
events.body: Cailean mac Eachainn, a copyist in the cellar at Muileann chaol, finds in the roll of the camp at Àth ìseal the marriage of Aisling's father, Donnchadh mac Thormoid, with his line written seven names back, as the custodians write a marriage. He carries the seven names up to Tobar dhìreach, to Ealasaid of Clann na Ceiste, the last who says the lines, and she knows them for the line of Somhairle son of Ailean Mòr. She says Aisling's line to him backward, from her father to the mason who found the fire. So what the camps whispered at Aisling's birth is found to be true. Cailean writes the line in the margin beside her birth.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The third mark beside a birth

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Cailean walks to Tobar dhìreach

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Cailean reads the Àth ìseal marriage line

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ealasaid of Clann na Ceiste says Sloinneadh Aisling

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Cailean writes the line in the margin

events.title: The third mark beside a birth
events.body: On the same page Cailean finds the birth of Aisling entered with a mark he has seen only three or four times in a year of copying, never explained in any book given him, and recognises it for the mark the camps' whisper had already fixed to one child in the settlement.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Line of Aisling found

told_in.book: Of Sloinneadh Aisling
told_in.section: I. Of the Roll at Àth ìseal

events.title: Cailean walks to Tobar dhìreach
events.body: Rather than report to the cellar, Cailean walks the hill road to Tobar dhìreach with the seven names copied onto a scrap of paper inside his coat, to ask whether a line so old could truly be Donnchadh's own.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Line of Aisling found

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Cailean reads the Àth ìseal marriage line

told_in.book: Of Sloinneadh Aisling
told_in.section: I. Of the Roll at Àth ìseal

events.title: Cailean reads the Àth ìseal marriage line
events.body: Copying the roll of the camp at Àth ìseal in Seilear Muileann chaol, Cailean mac Eachainn reads past the first name of a marriage line for the first time in a year of copying, and finds Donnchadh mac Thormoid's line carried seven fathers back to a name far older than a hewer's line should hold.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Line of Aisling found

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Cailean walks to Tobar dhìreach

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Ealasaid of Clann na Ceiste says Sloinneadh Aisling

told_in.book: Of Sloinneadh Aisling
told_in.section: I. Of the Roll at Àth ìseal

events.title: Ealasaid of Clann na Ceiste says Sloinneadh Aisling
events.body: Ealasaid, last of Clann na Ceiste who still says the old lines at Tobar dhìreach, hears the seven names Cailean brings and gives him Aisling's whole line back to Somhairle son of Ailean Mòr, the first king, telling him plainly that she has told him whose son the child's forebear was and no more than that.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Line of Aisling found

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Cailean reads the Àth ìseal marriage line

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Cailean writes the line in the margin

told_in.book: Of Sloinneadh Aisling
told_in.section: II. Of Tobar dhìreach

events.title: Cailean writes the line in the margin
events.body: Cailean carries Ealasaid's recital back to Muileann chaol and writes it small in the margin of the Àth ìseal roll beside Aisling's birth, telling no one at the cellar what he has done.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Line of Aisling found

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Ealasaid of Clann na Ceiste says Sloinneadh Aisling

told_in.book: Of Sloinneadh Aisling
told_in.section: III. Of the Return, and the Report that Named No One

events.title: The Administration's register
events.body: The Residency, hearing of the word, orders that any Dia-thìreach child showing the change be reported to the Commissioner's office. The custodians obey by reporting none.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The custodians' first return to Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir: none

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A custodian of Cill ghlas answers A' Chompanaidh's agent

events.title: The custodians' first return to Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir: none
events.body: When Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir orders every child with fuil-ghuail reported to An t-Àrd-mhaor's office, the custodians from Cathair dhearg to the coast make their first return and report none, though every roll among them keeps its own quiet note of such births in a physician's plain word.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Administration's register

told_in.book: Of Sloinneadh Aisling
told_in.section: III. Of the Return, and the Report that Named No One

events.title: A custodian of Cill ghlas answers A' Chompanaidh's agent
events.body: Asked by an agent of A' Chompanaidh whether she knows of any child with fuil-ghuail in her district, a custodian of Cill ghlas answers that she keeps no roll of miracles, only of births and deaths, and that the office is welcome to search her books for either.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Administration's register

told_in.book: Of Sloinneadh Aisling
told_in.section: III. Of the Return, and the Report that Named No One

events.title: Peigi Ghlas dies at Cill ghlas
events.body: Peigi Ghlas dies at Cill ghlas, her petition still unanswered, having trimmed Brìde's lamp herself the week before her death and said that she had asked Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir once and meant to leave the asking there.

told_in.book: Of Sloinneadh Aisling
told_in.section: V. Of the Staff at Muileann chrom

events.title: The third change of coin
events.body: The old barter of the Dia-thìrich is struck down as lawful payment altogether. Every bargain on the island now goes by the humans' coin.

events.title: The barter houses closed
events.body: The barter houses at Ros dhomhain and Cathair dhearg, where cloth and fish had changed hands without coin since before the Crossing, are shut by order. A clerk of the Residency writes that the ledgers are now "complete for the first time."

events.title: The fishwives of Inis mhòr
events.body: The fishwives of Inis mhòr, who had sold by barter at the river steps since before the Crossing, will take no coin for a week, in protest at the shutting of the barter houses, and give their fish away. The Company's clerks record it as a glut.

events.title: Marks borrowed at interest
events.body: Barter being struck down, the hill villages borrow marks at interest from the Company's stores to buy seed. Within a few years most of the villages of Muileann chrom owe the Company more than a year's crops.

events.title: The old market at Muileann òg
events.body: The old barter market at Muileann òg, where hill and coast had met to trade since the Holy Age, closes after its last season, and the ground stands empty.

events.title: Mòrag nic Iain Maor
events.body: Iain Maor dies, and his daughter Mòrag takes the overseer's staff at Muileann chrom, the first woman to hold it. The Company approves her in a letter that calls her "a safe pair of hands."

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Iain Maor buried at Muileann chrom

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Mòrag hangs the staff over her hearth

events.title: Iain Maor buried at Muileann chrom
events.body: Iain Maor, third of that name to hold the overseer's staff at Muileann chrom, dies in the same house he held it from and is buried within the week, the camp's custom allowing no longer delay for an office that cannot sit empty.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Mòrag nic Iain Maor

told_in.book: Of Sloinneadh Aisling
told_in.section: V. Of the Staff at Muileann chrom

events.title: Mòrag hangs the staff over her hearth
events.body: Mòrag nic Iain Maor, first woman to hold the overseer's staff at Muileann chrom, hangs it over her own hearth on iron hooks her father never had fitted, rather than keep it across her knees as he had.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Mòrag nic Iain Maor

told_in.book: Of Sloinneadh Aisling
told_in.section: V. Of the Staff at Muileann chrom

events.title: Charles Merriman Commissioner
events.body: Edward Vane dies at the Residency. Charles Merriman comes after him with a small company of armed constables, the first standing force the Administration has kept on Dia-thìr.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Edward Vane dies at Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir

events.title: The constable post at Muileann shean
events.body: Merriman's first constable post is built at Muileann shean on the northern coal road, a stone house with a yard for horses. The townsfolk call it the humans' second Residency, and do not mean it kindly.

events.title: Ruth Pallant teaches Hannah Webb the night watch
events.body: At Ceann mhòr, an old net-mender named Ruth Pallant tells the field-worker Hannah Webb of a night watch her own people's fisher-forebears learned from the island folk, kept in silence under a grey goose said to hold the sea shut. Hannah carries the telling of it home to the concession.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A grey-night vigil at Baile chrom

told_in.book: Of the Grey Goose and the Dockers
told_in.section: II. Of Hannah Webb

events.title: Hannah Webb's first vigil
events.body: In a field behind her landlord's byre near Baile chrom, Hannah Webb keeps the silent watch for the first time, and sees, or believes she sees, a pale shape cross the night sky before she sleeps through a whole night for the first time in ten years on the island.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A grey-night vigil at Baile chrom

told_in.book: Of the Grey Goose and the Dockers
told_in.section: II. Of Hannah Webb

events.title: The watch spreads along the concession's edge
events.body: Word of Hannah Webb's night vigil passes among the human labourers of the concession after a field hand sees her keeping it. Within a season a handful of others try it, and by autumn six or seven keep the field together on clear nights, spaced apart and silent.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A grey-night vigil at Baile chrom

told_in.book: Of the Grey Goose and the Dockers
told_in.section: II. Of Hannah Webb

events.title: Edward Vane dies at Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir
events.body: Àrd-mhaor Edward Vane, born at Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir above Ros dhomhain, dies there in the bed he was born in. The custodians who come to acknowledge the change of stewards find, as they had all his rule, that they had liked him rather more than they meant to.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Charles Merriman Commissioner

told_in.book: Of the Grey Goose and the Dockers
told_in.section: I. Of the New Àrd-mhaor

events.title: The post at Tobar ghorm and the custodian's rent
events.body: A second constable post rises at Tobar ghorm. The village's custodian, Uilleam Glas, takes the rent paid for the ground and clears the village of every debt it owes A' Chompanaidh's own store, to the written complaint of A' Chompanaidh's agent.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A barracks at Tobar ghorm

told_in.book: Of the Grey Goose and the Dockers
told_in.section: I. Of the New Àrd-mhaor

events.title: A barracks at Tobar ghorm
events.body: A second post is raised at Tobar ghorm, near the northern workings. The village's custodian is paid rent for the ground, and with it buys the village out of its debts to the Company store.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The post at Tobar ghorm and the custodian's rent

events.title: A grey-night vigil at Baile chrom
events.body: The Mission at Cathair gheal reports that human labourers near Baile chrom keep vigil by night in the fields, praying in silence under the sign of a grey goose, which they call the wild goose of the Spirit. The Mission cannot find whence the practice came, and calls it irregular, a superstition learned of the Dia-thìrich. The Dia-thìrich of Baile chrom disown it.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Ruth Pallant teaches Hannah Webb the night watch

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Hannah Webb's first vigil

links.label: Caused by
links.title: The watch spreads along the concession's edge

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Minister Renn writes the vigil irregular

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Baile chrom disowns the humans' watch

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Manannan's priest names the goose gone astray

events.title: Manannan's priests on the grey night
events.body: The priests of Òrd Mhanannain at Ceann mhòr answer the Mission's report of the grey-night vigils. The practice owes something to the Dia-thìrich, they say, but to their own harbours and not to Baile chrom: the human fishing families of Ceann mhòr learned from them the night prayer to keep the sea shut, and the labourers inland keep it as a vigil of their Church, a night of silence under the wild goose of the Spirit in place of a prayer to Manannan. The priests call it Manannan's prayer gone astray, and do not admit its keepers to their house.

events.title: Minister Renn writes the vigil irregular
events.body: Obadiah Renn, Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise's minister at Cathair gheal's chapel, questions Hannah Webb about the watch and, finding no scripture that knows a goose, writes to Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise's house that the practice is irregular and its origin uncertain, though he does not call it wrongdoing.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A grey-night vigil at Baile chrom

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Baile chrom disowns the humans' watch

told_in.book: Of the Grey Goose and the Dockers
told_in.section: III. Of What Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise and the Priests Said of It

events.title: Baile chrom disowns the humans' watch
events.body: The custodian of Baile chrom's lower row refuses any part of the human labourers' vigil, saying the town's own name should be left out of the keeping of it. The field folk, who had hoped to call the watch a thing shared between the two peoples, learn to call it their own alone.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A grey-night vigil at Baile chrom

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Minister Renn writes the vigil irregular

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Manannan's priest names the goose gone astray

told_in.book: Of the Grey Goose and the Dockers
told_in.section: III. Of What Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise and the Priests Said of It

events.title: The dockers' strike at Ros dhomhain
events.body: The dockers of Ros dhomhain, Dia-thìrich and human alike, refuse to load coal for nine days over the new berth charges. It is the only strike of the age in which human workers stand with Dia-thìrich. Merriman's constables break it, and the human dockers are shipped over the sea.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The berth toll and the docker Tòmas Ruadh

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Merriman's constables break the stoppage

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The human dockers shipped over the sea

events.title: Seann Vell's dockers stay out
events.body: The dockers of Seann Vell, the harbour next to Ros dhomhain, refuse to load the coal sent to them during the strike. When it ends they are not shipped over the sea, for there are no humans among them; but they are not hired again either.

events.title: Lorccan born
events.body: A third such child is born, in a mining town and not a camp; the thing is no longer bound to any one place.

events.title: Manannan's priest names the goose gone astray
events.body: A priest of the harbour temple at Ceann mhòr walks to Baile chrom, watches Hannah Webb's vigil through a night, and tells her the goose she keeps is an Gèadh Fiadhaich, wandered from Manannan's own harbours into a shape no longer entirely his people's to reclaim or to stop.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: A grey-night vigil at Baile chrom

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Baile chrom disowns the humans' watch

told_in.book: Of the Grey Goose and the Dockers
told_in.section: III. Of What Teachdaireachd na h-Eaglaise and the Priests Said of It

events.title: The berth toll and the docker Tòmas Ruadh
events.body: A' Chompanaidh posts a new toll on every ton loaded at the Ros dhomhain coal berths. The docker Tòmas Ruadh, whom Daniel Webb once pulled clear of a falling beam, tells him of it, and the two speak for the first time of standing off the hooks together.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The dockers' strike at Ros dhomhain

told_in.book: Of the Grey Goose and the Dockers
told_in.section: IV. Of the Dockers of Ros dhomhain

events.title: Merriman's constables break the stoppage
events.body: On the stoppage's tenth morning, Merriman's constables stand a rifle-line the length of the Ros dhomhain quay. The dockers, who had held nine days without a blow struck, go back to the hooks within the hour rather than test a tenth day against thirty grey coats.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The dockers' strike at Ros dhomhain

told_in.book: Of the Grey Goose and the Dockers
told_in.section: IV. Of the Dockers of Ros dhomhain

events.title: The human dockers shipped over the sea
events.body: A' Chompanaidh takes the names of every human docker who struck and offers them passage over the sea within the week, once, with the plain understanding that it will not be offered twice. Hannah Webb watches her brother Daniel go up the gangway from the Ros dhomhain quay.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The dockers' strike at Ros dhomhain

told_in.book: Of the Grey Goose and the Dockers
told_in.section: IV. Of the Dockers of Ros dhomhain

events.title: Raghnall Breac walks to Cill ghlas
events.body: With his knees gone stiff for the low work at Baile thais and two grandchildren to feed, the ageing hewer Raghnall Breac walks two days to the new galleries at Cill ghlas, where the pay is better and the headings still stand tall enough for a man to work upright. He writes to his daughter Eilidh twice a year.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Blasting-powder at Cill ghlas

told_in.book: Of Scàineadh Cill ghlas
told_in.section: II. Of Baile thais in the Winter

events.title: Cian born
events.body: A fourth is born within a year of the third. Never again do the children of the undying generation come so close together.

events.title: Blasting-powder at Cill ghlas
events.body: The Company begins to drive galleries under the hills about Cill ghlas with blasting-powder shipped from an Tìr Thall. The custodians of the shrine ask that no charge be set within sight of the old cutting. The Company's engineer marks their asking on his plan, and sets the charges below it.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Raghnall Breac walks to Cill ghlas

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Fairley marks the custodians' asking on his plan

events.title: Powder landed at Caol ìseal
events.body: The blasting-powder for the new galleries is landed at Caol ìseal on the northern coast, away from the crowded southern harbours, and carted inland under guard. The town's custodians ask what is in the barrels and are told it is lamp-oil.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Beathag Ruadh's roll at Caol ìseal

events.title: Eilidh nic Raghnaill given a seat at Faire nan Lòchran's table
events.body: The crew-leader Eilidh nic Raghnaill of Baile thais is asked, for the first time, to sit at the table where Faire nan Lòchran keeps its business, and copies its minutes into a second book kept in her own linen chest, where no clerk of A' Chompanaidh would think to look.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Lamp-Watch

told_in.book: Of Scàineadh Cill ghlas
told_in.section: II. Of Baile thais in the Winter

events.title: Fairley marks the custodians' asking on his plan
events.body: A' Chompanaidh's engineer Robert Fairley writes the custodians' request, that no charge be set within sight of the shrine at Cill ghlas, into the margin of his working plan. The plan shows the shrine as a bare shape with no depth drawn beneath it, and the numbered headings below are never measured against it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Blasting-powder at Cill ghlas

told_in.book: Of Scàineadh Cill ghlas
told_in.section: I. Of the Plan and the Mark Below It

events.title: Beathag Ruadh's roll at Caol ìseal
events.body: The custodian of Caol ìseal counts forty casks of blasting-powder off a ship of A' Chompanaidh, told to her carters as lamp-oil, and writes in her roll that the staves smelled of nothing when she put her hand to them. Her line goes unanswered into Seilear Muileann chaol with the rest of the year's roll.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Powder landed at Caol ìseal

told_in.book: Of Scàineadh Cill ghlas
told_in.section: I. Of the Plan and the Mark Below It

events.title: Scàineadh Cill ghlas
events.body: The Rending: in the hills east of the capital, about Cill ghlas, the earth tears open along a fault beneath a common working. Dozens are killed, and a whole mining district is shut for a generation.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Scàineadh Cill ghlas kills the thirty-one

events.title: The first open fight
events.body: A mining death, which the Dia-thìrich workers lay at the door of the humans' carelessness, leads to the first bloodshed between the two peoples.

events.title: The shrine at Cill ghlas lost
events.body: The Rending swallows the old cutting at Cill ghlas, where the custodians had kept the rites through all the age, and its shrine with it. The custodians' roll sets down the loss of the shrine before the loss of the dead; a later copyist has put them in the other order.

events.title: The district closed
events.body: The Company shuts the whole district of the Rending and fences it, leaving Cill ghlas, Àth chaol and their hamlets in the shires of Muileann dhearg and Muileann chiar without work. The villages empty toward Baile thais and Muileann dhearg, and the closed district is left to the thorn.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Eilidh nic Raghnaill at the fenced ground

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A' Chompanaidh fences the closed district

events.title: The meeting on the moor road
events.body: The folk turned out of the closed district send their eldest to the custodians of Muileann dhomhain, who meet them at a standing stone on the moor road below the town, lest the Company's clerks see them in the town hall. At the stone the custodians lend them the land at the edge of the fenced ground. The place is called Coinneachadh an Fhearainn, the meeting of the land.

events.title: Achadh chaol raised by the dispossessed
events.body: Folk of the closed district build a new village at Achadh chaol, at the edge of the fenced ground, on land lent by the custodians of Muileann dhomhain. It is the only settlement of the age founded by Dia-thìrich for Dia-thìrich with no Company surveyor's hand in it.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Achadh chaol's first roll opened

events.title: The fight at Muileann chrom
events.body: The death that began it was a flooded gallery at Muileann chrom, where seven died after the pumps were stopped to save fuel. When the Company's agent came to the pithead the crews stoned him and his constables, and the constables fired. Four Dia-thìrich and one constable were killed.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Fionnlagh's warning at Muileann chrom

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The flooded gallery takes seven

events.title: Eilidh nic Raghnaill at the fenced ground
events.body: Eilidh nic Raghnaill walks to Cill ghlas to find her father's grave and finds instead the fence and the fallen headgear of the eighth heading. A constable turns her away from the closed ground. She writes nothing of the hour in Faire nan Lòchran's book.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The district closed

told_in.book: Of Scàineadh Cill ghlas
told_in.section: IV. Of the Fenced Ground and the Stone on the Moor Road

events.title: Scàineadh Cill ghlas kills the thirty-one
events.body: On the ninth of an t-Ògmhios the fault beneath Cill ghlas tears open and the ground above the eighth heading and the old shrine cutting comes down together. The custodians' roll names thirty-one dead, among them the hewer Raghnall Breac, and says four bodies more were never brought up.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Scàineadh Cill ghlas

told_in.book: Of Scàineadh Cill ghlas
told_in.section: III. Of the Ground that Spoke First

events.title: A' Chompanaidh fences the closed district
events.body: A' Chompanaidh's surveyors return within the week to fence the district from Cill ghlas to Àth chaol, and Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir's order forbids any wage or working on any ground inside the fence. Households leave through the autumn and winter, first in twos and threes, then whole villages together.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The district closed

told_in.book: Of Scàineadh Cill ghlas
told_in.section: IV. Of the Fenced Ground and the Stone on the Moor Road

events.title: Fionnlagh's warning at Muileann chrom
events.body: The overseer Fionnlagh tells the new agent Edgar Holt that the flooded ground under one heading at Muileann chrom has never gone a night without its pumps, drawing as it does from an unmapped old working above it. Holt orders the pumps stopped regardless, to spare coal for the winding-gear until a delayed barge arrives.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The fight at Muileann chrom

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The flooded gallery takes seven

told_in.book: Of Scàineadh Cill ghlas
told_in.section: V. Of the Pumps Stopped to Save Fuel

events.title: The flooded gallery takes seven
events.body: With the pumps idle overnight, the gallery at Muileann chrom fills to the roof, and seven men of the change of shift, Fionnlagh among them, do not come up. Mòrag nic Iain Maor stands at the pit-mouth as they are brought up and laid in a row on the wet boards.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The fight at Muileann chrom

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Fionnlagh's warning at Muileann chrom

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Mòrag's testimony struck from the inquiry

told_in.book: Of Scàineadh Cill ghlas
told_in.section: V. Of the Pumps Stopped to Save Fuel

events.title: Mòrag's testimony struck from the inquiry
events.body: At Riaghaltas nan Coigreach's inquiry at Ros dhomhain, the fourth Steward Mòrag nic Iain Maor carries A' Chompanaidh's own staff into the room and testifies that Edgar Holt ordered the pumps stopped against his overseer's warning. The commissioners rule her account improper and have the clerk strike it from the record.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Mòrag Maor at the inquiry

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The flooded gallery takes seven

told_in.book: Of Scàineadh Cill ghlas
told_in.section: VI. Of the Inquiry and the Copy That Was Kept

events.title: Mòrag Maor at the inquiry
events.body: At the Administration's inquiry into the fight the overseer Mòrag nic Iain Maor bears witness that the pumps were stopped on the agent's order. Her words are struck out. The Lamp-Watch gets a copy of them all the same.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Mòrag's testimony struck from the inquiry

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Faire nan Lòchran keeps the struck copy

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Mòrag's private book

events.title: The grey fever
events.body: A fever of the chest comes in on the ships and runs over the whole island, from the capital to the eastern farms. It kills the young and strong more than the old, the Mission notes in alarm. The camps, already hungry, bury more than the towns.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Tormod Buidhe's sister's boy dies of Am Fiabhras Glas

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Eilidh nic Raghnaill begins Comann an Adhlacaidh's book

events.title: The grey fever at Cathair mhòr
events.body: At Cathair mhòr the grey fever shuts the market for the first time in the town's memory. The custodians' roll gives the dead by street, and the longest list is of the street where the carters lived.

events.title: The grey fever at Dùn thais
events.body: At Dùn thais the fever takes the physician the Administration sent to treat it, and two of the Mission's nurses. The old houses of the druid masters are opened as sick-rooms.

events.title: Achadh chaol's first roll opened
events.body: Aonghas Mòr, once keeper of the lost shrine, opens the first custodians' roll of Achadh chaol on the day the new village's well is finished, its first line giving the well's depth and naming no shrine and no dead. It is the only settlement of the age raised without any surveyor of A' Chompanaidh's hand in it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Achadh chaol raised by the dispossessed

told_in.book: Of Scàineadh Cill ghlas
told_in.section: IV. Of the Fenced Ground and the Stone on the Moor Road

events.title: Faire nan Lòchran keeps the struck copy
events.body: A Dia-thìreach clerk who keeps A' Chompanaidh's own file copy of the inquiry's minutes has the struck-through page carried north to Baile thais folded inside sailcloth. Eilidh nic Raghnaill copies it a second time into Faire nan Lòchran's linen-chest book, the stricken line copied as stricken, and is given a full seat at the table that winter.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Mòrag Maor at the inquiry

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The Lamp-Watch

told_in.book: Of Scàineadh Cill ghlas
told_in.section: VI. Of the Inquiry and the Copy That Was Kept

events.title: Tormod Buidhe's sister's boy dies of Am Fiabhras Glas
events.body: A boy not yet old enough for his first wage dies of Am Fiabhras Glas at Baile thais under Eilidh nic Raghnaill's sitting, having asked her, near the end, what month it was. His mother keeps his name from Comann an Adhlacaidh's book, and Eilidh does not ask for it twice.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The grey fever

told_in.book: Of the Warning and the Constables
told_in.section: I. Of the Grey Fever

events.title: Eilidh nic Raghnaill begins Comann an Adhlacaidh's book
events.body: Eilidh nic Raghnaill begins keeping a plain hand-written record for Comann an Adhlacaidh at Baile thais, answering to no custodian's roll, after watching her father Raghnall Breac carry twenty years of names in his memory and give none of them to paper. She means not to do the same.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The grey fever

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Eilidh nic Raghnaill drafts An Dàrna Athchuinge

told_in.book: Of the Warning and the Constables
told_in.section: I. Of the Grey Fever

events.title: Eilidh nic Raghnaill drafts An Dàrna Athchuinge
events.body: In Comann an Adhlacaidh's room at Baile thais, Eilidh nic Raghnaill drafts An Dàrna Athchuinge over three nights by a single coal lamp, with Griogal and two others reading each page back to her aloud. She writes its last sentence twice before settling the wording Griogal judges means it rather than asks permission to mean it.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The second petition

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Eilidh nic Raghnaill

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Eilidh nic Raghnaill begins Comann an Adhlacaidh's book

told_in.book: Of the Warning and the Constables
told_in.section: II. Of An Dàrna Athchuinge

events.title: The second petition
events.body: This one carries a threat beneath its words, not a plea. It is the first writing of the Dia-thìrich the Administration troubles to answer, and it answers with more guards, not with concessions.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Eilidh nic Raghnaill drafts An Dàrna Athchuinge

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir's clerk underlines the petition's last sentence

events.title: The signatories of Cnoc dhìreach
events.body: Coinneach Ruadh, custodian of Cnoc dhìreach, signs the second petition, and in the same week is turned out of his post as clerk to the Company store. He is one of eleven who sign and lose Company work for it.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A' Chompanaidh dismisses Coinneach Ruadh at his own store

events.title: Eilidh nic Raghnaill
events.body: The second petition was drawn up by Eilidh nic Raghnaill, a crew-leader of Baile thais and one of the Lamp-Watch, and signed by custodians and crew-leaders of thirty-one settlements. It ends with a sentence the Residency underlined: that the hill would not be worked by people who were not asked.

links.label: Caused by
links.title: Eilidh nic Raghnaill drafts An Dàrna Athchuinge

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir's clerk underlines the petition's last sentence

events.title: A' Chompanaidh dismisses Coinneach Ruadh at his own store
events.body: A' Chompanaidh's agent at Cnoc dhìreach delivers Coinneach Ruadh's letter of dismissal at the store's door in front of the week's flour queue, the day his signature to An Dàrna Athchuinge dries. He is offered twice the chance to withdraw his name and twice declines it, saying a name once given is not the giver's to take back.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The signatories of Cnoc dhìreach

told_in.book: Of the Warning and the Constables
told_in.section: II. Of An Dàrna Athchuinge

events.title: Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir's clerk underlines the petition's last sentence
events.body: A clerk of Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir underlines in red ink An Dàrna Athchuinge's last sentence, that the hill will not go on being worked by people who are not asked, before passing the fair copy Eilidh nic Raghnaill made up the office. The custodians afterward agree it is the first sign Riaghaltas nan Coigreach has read a Dia-thìrich word and understood it.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The second petition

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Eilidh nic Raghnaill

told_in.book: Of the Warning and the Constables
told_in.section: II. Of An Dàrna Athchuinge

events.title: The constables tripled
events.body: Merriman answers by tripling the constables and posting companies at Muileann chrom, Baile thais, Ceann fhada and Cnoc chaol, each with a walled store. The constables are paid from the tithe.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The first constables' company reaches Baile thais

events.title: Barracks at Dùn chrom
events.body: A barracks for the constables is built at Dùn chrom, on the capital side of the hills, with room for two hundred men. For most of its first year it stands empty, for want of constables to fill it.

events.title: Ìomhar Seabhag
events.body: At Seann Skell the hawk-priest Ìomhar Seabhag preaches that Mòd's hunger has turned on those who have eaten the hill. The hawk-shrines of the west begin to serve as meeting-houses for the Lamp-Watch, and the constables do not yet know it.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Eilidh nic Raghnaill reads Ìomhar Seabhag's sermon to Faire nan Lòchran

events.title: The hawk-faithful of Ros gheal
events.body: At Ros gheal the hawk-faithful fishing families, who had chased out the Company's customs officers a century before, raise a shrine to Mòd on the harbour wall. The constables order it down. It is built again three times in a single season.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The fourth shrine stands at Ros gheal

events.title: The hawk and the druids at Inis bhàn
events.body: At Inis bhàn the priests of the hawk and a few who still keep the questions of the druid school in private meet for a disputation, the first between them in living memory. It is written that it settled nothing, and that both sides afterwards signed the petition.

events.title: The grey fever in the north-west
events.body: The grey fever returns and settles in the north-west, about Baile chrom and the towns of the concession, where it kills humans as readily as Dia-thìrich. The Mission's hospital at Cathair gheal overflows, and for the first time Dia-thìrich and human sick lie in the same wards.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: An overman gives up his cot at Cathair gheal

events.title: The first constables' company reaches Baile thais
events.body: Forty constables under an officer named Prosser march into Baile thais on the twenty-fifth of Gearran and wall the settlement's old open store within the fortnight, taking the camp's well inside the new wall. Eilidh nic Raghnaill and Comann an Adhlacaidh watch the company make camp on ground that had been common land that same morning.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The constables tripled

told_in.book: Of the Warning and the Constables
told_in.section: III. Of the Answer

events.title: The fourth shrine stands at Ros gheal
events.body: After the constables tear down the hawk-faithful's shrine on the Ros gheal harbour wall three mornings running, unnamed hands raise it a fourth time and the constables stop trying. The shrine stands afterward as the ordinary furniture of a wall that had always carried something.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The hawk-faithful of Ros gheal

told_in.book: Of the Warning and the Constables
told_in.section: IV. Of Òrd an t-Seabhaig and the Sermon

events.title: An overman gives up his cot at Cathair gheal
events.body: In the crowded shared ward at Cathair gheal a Dia-thìreach overman of the north-west galleries gives up his own bed to a human boy of the concession no more than nine years old, and sits the night on the floor beside him. Hannah Webb writes of it to Eilidh nic Raghnaill at Baile thais.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The grey fever in the north-west

told_in.book: Of the Warning and the Constables
told_in.section: IV. Of Òrd an t-Seabhaig and the Sermon

events.title: Muileann fhionn shut in
events.body: Muileann fhionn, a Dia-thìreach mill town in the north-west, shuts its roads against the fever and keeps them shut for a season. Human carters of the concession are turned back with their loads at the town's edge.

events.title: The fever at Tobar fhiadhaich
events.body: At Tobar fhiadhaich in the north the fever takes one household in three. The custodians of the village burn no huts; they had heard of Àth ghlas in their grandparents' time, but judge it too late.

events.title: The road-houses make ready
events.body: The road-houses along the old mining roads begin to serve as waystations for bands of armed men. The roads make ready for a war not yet declared.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Aonghas takes the loft at An Taigh-seinnse Mòr

events.title: An Taigh-seinnse Òir
events.body: An Taigh-seinnse Òir, the great house on the eastern road beyond Dùn dhearg, digs a well in its yard and builds a wall round the well. The keeper tells the Company's carters it is against thieves.

events.title: An Leòmhann Buidhe
events.body: An Leòmhann Buidhe, the road-house on the northern road through the druid country, takes on six new ostlers in a single season, none of whom know anything of horses.

events.title: Eilidh nic Raghnaill reads Ìomhar Seabhag's sermon to Faire nan Lòchran
events.body: A fowler leaves a written copy of Ìomhar Seabhag's Seann Skell sermon with Comann an Adhlacaidh's door-keeper at Baile thais, and Eilidh nic Raghnaill reads it aloud to the room by the same lamp she drafted An Dàrna Athchuinge by. For once she does not write anything in the club's book afterward.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: Ìomhar Seabhag

told_in.book: Of the Warning and the Constables
told_in.section: IV. Of Òrd an t-Seabhaig and the Sermon

events.title: Aonghas takes the loft at An Taigh-seinnse Mòr
events.body: A crew-leader from Baile thais asks Aonghas, keeper of An Taigh-seinnse Mòr since Seònaid Bhàn's line came to him, whether the loft above his stable might hold men now and again with no questions asked. He agrees, and stops in time asking what they carry.

links.label: Follows from
links.title: The road-houses make ready

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Seònaid's house

told_in.book: Of the Houses on the Roads
told_in.section: I. Of the House at the Halfway Stage

events.title: An Taigh-òsta Grianach walled
events.body: An Taigh-òsta Grianach, called the singing house since the songs of Fearchar Bàrd, raises a wall round its yard and sets a watch on its gate.

events.title: Am Buabhall Fortanach barred
events.body: Am Buabhall Fortanach, the great road-house on the south-western road, bars its gates at dusk and keeps a watch on the roof. Its keeper, Tormod Buabhall, keeps a list of travellers and sends it up the road each week, to whom is not told.

events.title: The harbour of Doire shean
events.body: The little harbour of Doire shean, below Am Buabhall Fortanach, becomes the landing for the goods the house cannot take by road. The fishermen of Doire shean are paid in silver from the east.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The fishermen of Doire shean paid in eastern silver

events.title: An Taigh-seinnse Reòta
events.body: At An Taigh-seinnse Reòta on the northern road the stables are rebuilt with a loft for sleeping men. The Company's carters mark that the loft is never empty, and never holds the same men twice.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: Coinneach nan Ràmh's word on the loft at the Reòta

events.title: An Sligeanach Fad' às
events.body: An Sligeanach Fad' às, on the eastern road near the silver country, becomes the post-house through which the Lamp-Watch sends word from the camps to Muileann chiar. The silver guild pays its keeper's rent.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: The Sligeanach's psalter

events.title: The runners of Àth fhiadhaich
events.body: Runners from Àth fhiadhaich carry the Lamp-Watch's letters from An Sligeanach Fad' às to the silver town. They are boys of twelve and thirteen, too young for the constables to stop.

links.label: Leads to
links.title: A boy of Àth fhiadhaich at Aonghas's door

events.title: A boy of Àth fhiadhaich at Aonghas's door
